Analytic adic geometry required for diamonds

p-adic Hodge theory and p-adic geometry · 14 definitions · 17 constructions · 17 planets

A0Completed tensor products and adic fibre products

Analytic locus of an adic spaceconstructionplanetThe analytic locus X_a of an adic space: open adic subspace, Tate charts, and restriction of adic morphisms

Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5). A point x ∈ X is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U such that O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit, equivalently if its support in some (every) open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) is not an open ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism; Tau Ceti ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint). The set X_a of analytic points is open. The analytic locus AdicSpace.analyticLocus X is the open adic subspace of X on X_a, with its open immersion ι_X : X_a → X; X is analytic (AdicSpace.IsAnalytic X) if X_a = X. Properties: (a) for an open subspace U ⊆ X, U_a = X_a ∩ U; (b) for X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete, |X_a| is Tau Ceti's spaAnalytic A⁺; it is quasi-compact, and for a pair of definition (A₀, I) and generators G = {g₁, …, g_r} of I it is the union of the rational subsets R(G/gᵢ), whose coordinate rings A⟨G/gᵢ⟩ are Tate rings (Tate charts); X_a = X if A is Tate, and X_a = ∅ iff the Hausdorff quotient of A is discrete; (c) X_a is analytic, and every morphism from an adic space to an analytic adic space is adic; (d) restriction: a morphism f : Y → X is adic iff f(Y_a) ⊆ X_a (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), and then there is a unique f_a : Y_a → X_a with ι_X ∘ f_a = f ∘ ι_Y, functorially in f; (e) universal property: for an analytic adic space T, a morphism T → X factors through ι_X iff it is adic, and then uniquely; (f) base change: if Y ×_X Z exists (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and Z → X is adic, then (Y ×_X Z)_a = p⁻¹(Y_a) = Y_a ×_X Z for the projection p. Conventions: non-Tate Huber pairs such as Witt vector rings and A_inf are allowed at the input; the constructions of AdicSpacesPartII R0 (completed tensor products, fibre products) are applied to their analytic loci through the Tate charts of (b), on which every morphism is adic. For an adic space over Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) with adic structure morphism, X_a is the preimage of Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); in general (Spa ℤ_p⟦T⟧, Spa A_inf) it is larger and contains analytic points of characteristic p. Lean name: AdicSpace.analyticLocus.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space (anchor Layer 5); (b) additionally X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete.
  • (d)–(f) concern morphisms of adic spaces; (f) needs the fibre product to exist.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/analytic-locus-restriction

A1Finite étale and étale geometry

Finite étale morphismdefinitionplanetFinite étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces by the local algebraic description

Let f: Y → X be a morphism of analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5; every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism). f is finite étale (AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f) if X has a covering by open affinoid subspaces V = Spa(A, A⁺) such that, for each of them, f⁻¹(V) is affinoid, B := O_Y(f⁻¹(V)) is a finite étale A-algebra via f^♯, and the morphism of Huber pairs (O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O_Y⁺(f⁻¹V)) is the morphism (A, A⁺) → Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (natural topology on B, plus ring the integral closure of A⁺); equivalently f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺) over V with B ∈ FÉt(A) (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16, Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii)). The condition is local on the target by definition. Its 'every open affinoid' form (the shape of ECD Definition 6.2(i)) holds over open affinoids with strongly sheafy coordinate ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global). Conventions: the plus ring is part of the condition (a finite étale ring map with plus ring B° is not finite étale in this sense when A⁺ ≠ A°); f need not be surjective (the empty space over X, and the inclusion of a clopen subspace, are finite étale); on locally noetherian analytic spaces the notion is Huber's 'finite and étale' (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). The same local condition read in the category of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation) is Kedlaya–Liu's notion for preadic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized).

Hypotheses

  • f a morphism of analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5 objects all of whose points are analytic).
  • The defining cover is part of the existence statement; no particular cover is fixed.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism

Étale siteconstructionplanetThe small étale site of a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair). The small étale site X_ét consists of: the category Et/X = AdicSpace.smallEtale X, the full subcategory of adic spaces over X whose structure morphism is étale in A1's sense (Mathlib MorphismProperty.Over of AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription over X, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), all X-morphisms being admitted (they are automatically étale, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation); and the Grothendieck topology AdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology X generated by the pretopology of jointly surjective families: (f_i: U_i → U)_i is a covering iff |U| = ∪_i f_i(|U_i|), all points counted, including points of higher rank (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19; Huber §2.1; Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(3)). Properties: (i) Et/X has the final object X, fibre products (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and equalisers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), hence all finite limits, and its objects are locally strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition (iii)); (ii) the jointly surjective families form a Mathlib Pretopology (isomorphisms; stability under base change by the surjectivity of |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W|; composition); (iii) open subspaces of X are objects and open coverings are coverings, and the inclusion of the analytic site (Mathlib Opens.grothendieckTopology) is a continuous functor preserving finite limits, giving the morphism of sites λ_X: X_ét → X_an; (iv) for a morphism g: X' → X of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, base change U ↦ U ×_X X' is a continuous functor Et/X → Et/X' preserving finite limits, defining a morphism of sites g_ét: X'_ét → X_ét with direct image (g_*F)(U) = F(U ×_X X') (Mathlib Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous) and inverse image g^{-1} (Mathlib Functor.sheafPullback), with (h ∘ g)_ét ≅ h_ét ∘ g_ét canonically. On locally noetherian X this is Huber's X_et (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). For an analytic X that is not locally strongly sheafy, Kedlaya–Liu's site with Yoneda-adic-space objects is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized. These are geometric sites: no derived category or cohomology is defined here (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0).

Hypotheses

  • X locally strongly sheafy analytic (so all fibre products of étale X-spaces exist among adic spaces).
  • Coverings are jointly surjective on all points of the adic spaces, not only on rank-one points.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site

Geometric pointconstructionplanetGeometric points of analytic adic spaces and their fibre functors on the étale site

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space with its étale site X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site: objects the adic spaces étale over X in A1's local-description sense, coverings the jointly surjective families; on locally noetherian X this is Huber's X_et with its topology, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison). A geometric point of X (AdicSpace.GeometricPoint X) is a morphism of adic spaces ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X with C an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of arbitrary rank (rank one, C⁺ = O_C, is a special case, not the definition); its support is x = ξ(s), s the closed point. (a) For every x ∈ X there is a geometric point with support x: with k(x)^ the completed residue field and k(x)^+ its valuation ring, take C the completion of an algebraic closure of k(x)^ and C⁺ a valuation ring of C with C⁺ ∩ k(x)^ = k(x)^+ (extension of valuation rings; C⁺ is then open and bounded). (b) The fibre functor ε_ξ: X_ét → Set, U ↦ Hom_X(Spa(C, C⁺), U) (the lifts of ξ to U), is a point of the site X_ét in Mathlib's sense (GrothendieckTopology.Point): its category of elements (the étale neighbourhoods of ξ) is cofiltered and essentially small, and coverings go to jointly surjective families. (c) The stalk of a sheaf F is F_ξ := colim over étale neighbourhoods (U, ū) of F(U) = Point.sheafFiber; it is exact and commutes with colimits. (d) Functoriality: for g: X' → X (locally strongly sheafy) and a geometric point ξ' of X', g ∘ ξ' is a geometric point of X and ε_{g∘ξ'} ≅ ε_{ξ'} ∘ g^* for the base change g^* of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, so (g^{-1}F)_{ξ'} ≅ F_{g∘ξ'} naturally in F. (e) The image of ξ consists of generisations of x (Scholze 2013, footnote to Proposition 3.13). The conservativity of the family (ε_ξ) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points and strict localisations are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation. Higher rank is essential: rank-one geometric points do not detect sheaves supported on points of higher rank (test below; de Jong–van der Put §3.3 for the rigid analytic points).

Hypotheses

  • X locally strongly sheafy analytic; C algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean; C⁺ open bounded valuation subring of any rank.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points

Strict localizationconstructionplanetThe strict localisation at a geometric point

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X a geometric point with support x (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points). (i) The category N(ξ) of étale neighbourhoods of ξ — pairs (U, ū) with U ∈ X_ét and ū a lift of ξ to U, i.e. the category of elements of the fibre functor ε_ξ — is cofiltered and essentially small. The strict localisation X(ξ) is the cofiltered diagram N(ξ)^op → X_ét, (U, ū) ↦ U, regarded as a pro-object of X_ét ('X(ξ) = lim U'), together with its compatible lift ξ̃ of ξ. (ii) Values: for a presheaf F on X_ét, F(X(ξ)) := colim_{N(ξ)} F(U); for a sheaf this is the stalk F_ξ. Opens of U containing ū(s) give cofinal neighbourhoods (they contain the image of ū, which consists of generisations of ū(s)). (iii) The local rings: O_{X_ét, ξ} := O(X(ξ)) = colim O_U(U) = colim O_{U, ū(s)} and O⁺_{X_ét, ξ} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), with the ring map O_{X_ét, ξ} → C induced by the lifts and the valuation v_ξ pulled back from C⁺. (iv) Underlying space: |X(ξ)| := lim_{N(ξ)} |U|, with the map from |Spa(C, C⁺)| induced by the lifts. (v) Functoriality: g: X' → X and a geometric point ξ' of X' induce N(g ∘ ξ') → N(ξ') by base change, hence X'(ξ') → X(g ∘ ξ') and O_{X_ét, gξ'} → O_{X'_ét, ξ'}. The structure of X(ξ) for analytic X (strictly henselian local ring; X(ξ) is the spectrum of an algebraically closed affinoid field) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic.

Hypotheses

  • X locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation

Pro-étale siteconstructionplanetThe pro-étale site X_proét of a locally noetherian analytic adic space, with Scholze's corrected coverings

Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). The pro-étale site X_proét is the category of objects U ∈ pro-X_ét that are pro-étale over X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism), with all morphisms of pro-X_ét between them, equipped with the Grothendieck topology J_proét generated (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendieck) by the corrected coverings of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology: a family {f_i: U_i → U} is a covering iff |U| = ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|) and every f_i factors as U_i → W_i → U, a finite-étale tower U_i = lim_{μ<λ_i} U_{i,μ} → W_i (U_{i,0} = W_i, each U_{i,μ} → lim_{μ'<μ} U_{i,μ'} the pullback of a finite étale surjective morphism of X_ét; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) followed by an étale morphism W_i → U. A sieve on U is covering iff it contains a corrected covering family. Structure: X is final, X_proét has finite limits computed in pro-X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-finite-limits), every U has an underlying space |U| = lim |U_i|, quasi-compact opens of |U| are represented by subobjects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-quasicompact-opens), and all members of coverings are open maps. The correction restricts only the coverings: the underlying category is that of Scholze 2013, Definition 3.9; families of pro-étale maps with countable presentations are coverings exactly as before; J_proét is coarser than the printed topology and strictly coarser as soon as an open surjection of profinite sets without continuous section occurs over a geometric point. No arbitrary open surjection of profinite sets is assumed to split, the deleted Proposition 3.8 and the deleted last sentence of Proposition 3.13 are not used, and the existence of enough points is only the abstract statement for coherent topoi (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-topos-enough-points). X_proét is not the pro-étale site of a perfectoid space of ECD Definition 8.1(ii) (owned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D2) and not Mathlib's pro-étale topology on schemes.

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian analytic (Scholze's hypothesis 'locally noetherian' is needed for Lemma 3.10(vii); the analytic restriction matches the consumers).
  • Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.
  • Reading of the erratum's condition for Definition 3.9 (not displayed in the erratum): an étale factor is allowed (otherwise open covers are excluded; AdicSpacesPartII/E-R4-1) and the steps are finite étale surjections pulled back from X_ét, with which the erratum's 'for countable limits, the definitions are unchanged' is immediate. Whether steps pulled back from X_fét alone would also give that is not settled here: the argument of sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E7 was rejected on review (the closed disc over ℂ_p has nontrivial connected finite étale covers).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected

Yoneda-adic spacesconstructionplanetYoneda-adic spaces: generalized adic spaces as sheaves on complete Huber pairs (Scholze–Weinstein pre-adic spaces, Kedlaya–Liu preadic spaces)

Let CAff and J_rat be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site. For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff put Spa^Y(A, A⁺) := the J_rat-sheafification (mathlib:CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf) of h_{(A,A⁺)} = Hom_CAff((A, A⁺), −). A morphism of sheaves F → Spa^Y(A, A⁺) is an open immersion if there is an open U ⊂ Spa(A, A⁺) with F ≅ colim_{V ⊂ U rational} Spa^Y(O(V), O⁺(V)) over Spa^Y(A, A⁺); a morphism F → G of J_rat-sheaves is an open immersion if its base change along every Spa^Y(A, A⁺) → G is an open immersion in the previous sense. A Yoneda-adic space is a J_rat-sheaf F such that F = colim Spa^Y(A, A⁺) over the category of open immersions Spa^Y(A, A⁺) → F; YAdic is the full subcategory of Sh(CAffᵒᵖ, J_rat) on Yoneda-adic spaces. This is the category of adic spaces of Scholze–Weinstein [SW13, Definition 2.1.5], the pre-adic spaces of the Berkeley Lectures (Definition 3.4.1) and the preadic spaces of Kedlaya–Liu (Definition 8.2.3, on Tate pairs); ECD Definition 15.5 and Lemma 15.6 hold in this generality. The name 'Yoneda-adic' (Berkeley, Appendix to Lecture 3) is used because the anchor's 'pre-adic spaces' (Wedhorn's 𝒱^pre, anchor Layer 3.4) are a different category built from the structure presheaf. Every Yoneda-adic space has an underlying topological space |F| with |Spa^Y(A, A⁺)| = Spa(A, A⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-ind-ringed-description), open immersions into F correspond to open subsets of |F| (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions), and the anchor's adic spaces form a full subcategory (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces). The framework does not assume that any non-sheafy pair is sheafy.

Hypotheses

  • CAff, J_rat as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site; sizes as there.
  • The construction is needed because sheafiness is not known to be stable under finite étale extension (Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 8.2.18), so Spa of the finite étale algebras used in ECD §15 and in AdicEtaleGeometry:A4 need not be an adic space.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation

Strongly sheafy Tate rings and locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spacesdefinition

Let A be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (Tau Ceti Huber.IsTateRing A; every Huber ring in this stage is complete and Hausdorff). For n ≥ 0 write A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ for Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n A, again a complete Tate ring. A is strongly sheafy (Huber.IsStronglySheafy A) if A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is sheafy for every n ≥ 0, sheafy meaning the anchor's Huber.IsSheafyRing (Wedhorn Definition 8.26: the structure presheaf of Spa(R, R⁺) is a sheaf for every ring of integral elements R⁺) (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 4.1). A Huber pair (A, A⁺) is strongly sheafy when A is. An analytic adic space X (anchor Layer 5, every point analytic) is locally strongly sheafy (AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy X) if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A a complete strongly sheafy Tate ring. Stability properties that are part of the definition package: (a) A strongly sheafy implies A sheafy (n = 0) and A⟨S_1, …, S_m⟩ strongly sheafy; (b) every rational localisation of a strongly sheafy ring is strongly sheafy; (c) if A is sheafy and Spa(A, A⁺) has a finite rational covering by strongly sheafy rings, then A is strongly sheafy; consequently, on a locally strongly sheafy X every open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X has A strongly sheafy, and every open subspace of X is locally strongly sheafy; (d) finite étale A-algebras are strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy). Examples: complete strongly noetherian Tate rings (in particular affinoid algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field), complete Tate rings with a noetherian ring of definition, and complete Tate rings that are stably sheafy in the anchor's sense (Huber.IsStablySheafyRing: each A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is topologically of finite type over A); hence locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) are locally strongly sheafy. Perfectoid and sousperfectoid Tate rings belong to the class as well (their Tate algebras are sousperfectoid, hence stably uniform and sheafy); that membership is proved where those rings are constructed (PerfectoidSpaces and AdicSpacesPartII:R5 consume this node), not here. Non-example: a uniform Tate ring that is not sheafy (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Mihara) is not strongly sheafy. Sheafiness of A alone is not known to give (d) (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18); this is why the class is introduced.

Hypotheses

  • A complete Hausdorff Tate ring; A⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring.
  • Sheafiness is the anchor's ring-level notion Huber.IsSheafyRing (quantified over rings of integral elements).
  • X analytic: its affinoid charts can be chosen with Tate coordinate rings (anchor analytic locus).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair

Étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces by the local open-immersion/finite-étale descriptiondefinition

A morphism f: Y → X of analytic adic spaces is étale in A1's sense (AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f) if every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood U ⊆ Y such that f|_U factors as U →^{j} W →^{g} V →^{i} X with j an open immersion, g finite étale (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) and i an open immersion (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16; Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(iii); ECD Definition 6.2(ii) for perfectoid spaces). Equivalent local form: V can be taken to be a rational subset of an open affinoid of X, W = g⁻¹(V) affinoid with W → V the Spa of a finite étale pair, and U a rational subset of W; that is, locally f is Spa(C, C⁺) ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A → B finite étale and B → C a rational localisation (a 'standard affinoid étale' morphism, the form used in ECD 6.4 and 15.6 and in Scholze 2013 Lemma 5.2). Conventions: open immersions and finite étale morphisms are étale; étaleness is local on the source and on the target; no separatedness or quasi-compactness is imposed (two copies of a disc glued along an open subset map étale to the disc); the name distinguishes this notion from Huber's AdicSpace.Etale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale), with which it agrees on locally noetherian analytic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison); Huber's infinitesimal definition is not used on non-noetherian spaces.

Hypotheses

  • f a morphism of analytic adic spaces; no noetherian, sheafiness-of-covers or separatedness hypothesis.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism

Étale, finite étale and pro-étale morphisms of pro-objects of X_ét, and the underlying space |U| = lim |U_i|definition

Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). Write pro-X_ét := Pro(X_ét) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces, the dual of Mathlib's Ind): its objects are formal cofiltered systems U = (U_i)_{i∈I}, written U = lim U_i, of objects of X_ét indexed by small cofiltered categories I, and Hom(lim_i U_i, lim_j V_j) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(U_i, V_j) (Scholze 2013, Proposition 3.2). X_ét ⊂ pro-X_ét as constant systems (fully faithful, written c), X is a final object, and cofiltered limits exist in pro-X_ét (a double system is combined into a single one). The underlying space of U is |U| := lim_i |U_i| (limit of topological spaces); it is independent of the presentation and U ↦ |U| is a functor pro-X_ét → Top. A morphism f: U → V of pro-X_ét is: (a) étale (resp. finite étale) if there are a morphism V → V_0 with V_0 ∈ X_ét and an étale (resp. finite étale in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism) morphism U_0 → V_0 of X_ét with U ≅ U_0 ×_{V_0} V over V; here, for a presentation V = lim_j V_j through which V → V_0 factors, U_0 ×_{V_0} V := lim_j U_0 ×_{V_0} V_j (fibre products in X_ét); (b) surjective if |f| is surjective; (c) pro-étale if there are a small cofiltered category K and an isomorphism U ≅ lim_{k∈K} U_k over V with every U_k → V étale and every transition U_k → U_{k'} finite étale and surjective for k ≥ k' ≥ k_0 (some k_0 ∈ K); such data is a pro-étale presentation. An object U is pro-étale over X if U → X is pro-étale.

Hypotheses

  • X as above (Scholze's standing hypothesis restricted to analytic adic spaces, the case the consumers use).
  • Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.
  • Étale and finite étale morphisms of X_ét are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1; every morphism of X_ét is étale by cancellation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-smooth-cancellation).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism

Finite-étale towers: transfinite compositions of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (the erratum's corrected covering condition)definition

Let X be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism and W ∈ pro-X_ét. A finite-étale tower over W of length λ (an ordinal) is a functor μ ↦ U_μ from the opposite of the well-ordered set {μ : μ < λ} to pro-X_ét over W such that U_0 = W and, for every μ < λ, the canonical morphism U_μ → U_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} U_{μ'} (the limit over the empty set being W) is finite étale and surjective in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism, i.e. the pullback along some morphism U_{<μ} → V_0 of a finite étale surjective morphism V_0' → V_0 of X_ét. Its composite is lim_{μ<λ} U_μ → W. A morphism t: U → W of pro-X_ét is a finite-étale tower if it is isomorphic over W to the composite of such a tower. Inside pro-X_fét one requires V_0' → V_0 to be a morphism of X_fét; this is the pro-finite-étale tower of Scholze's erratum, item (1). Conventions: a step is allowed at every ordinal, including limit ordinals (Kerz's transfinite compositions); λ ≤ 1 gives isomorphisms and λ = 2 single finite étale surjections. Equivalently (re-indexing by inserting U_{<μ} before U_μ), t is a finite-étale tower iff its opposite lies in the class MorphismProperty.transfiniteCompositions of the opposite of the pullbacks of finite étale surjective morphisms of X_ét, computed in (pro-X_ét)ᵒᵖ with well-order-continuous shapes.

Hypotheses

  • X, W as stated; fibre products used in the steps exist by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change.
  • Surjective means surjective on underlying spaces; steps pulled back from X_ét (not only from X_fét) are allowed for towers inside X_proét, which is what keeps the countable case unchanged (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower-is-pro-etale).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower

The complete Huber pair of a finite étale algebra over a complete Tate pairconstruction

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on a complete Hausdorff Huber.IsTateRing A) and let B be a finite étale A-algebra (Mathlib Algebra.Etale A B and Module.Finite A B; an object of CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A). Construct the complete Tate Huber pair (B, B⁺) := Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B and the morphism ι: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺). (i) Topology: B is a finite projective A-module, and B carries the natural A-module topology (Mathlib moduleTopology A B); for any presentation B ⊕ Q ≅ Aⁿ it is both the subspace and the quotient topology from Aⁿ (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12). With it B is a complete Hausdorff topological ring, ι is continuous, every A-linear map from B to a topological A-module is continuous, and B is a Tate ring: if b_1, …, b_m generate B as an A-module, ϖ ∈ A⁺ is a pseudouniformiser and A₀ ⊆ A⁺ a ring of definition, then for N ≫ 0 the ϖ^N b_j are integral over A₀, B₀ := A₀[ϖ^N b_1, …, ϖ^N b_m] is a ring of definition with ideal of definition ϖB₀, and ι(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of B. (ii) Plus ring: B⁺ := the integral closure of ι(A⁺) in B; it is a ring of integral elements. (iii) ι is a finite morphism of complete Huber pairs (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); it induces the continuous map Spa(ι): Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti ValuationSpectrum.spaComap), whose fibre over x has at most rank_x(B) points; Spa(ι) is surjective when B is faithfully flat over A. (iv) Universal property: for every complete Huber pair (D, D⁺) with a morphism χ: (A, A⁺) → (D, D⁺), the morphisms of Huber pairs (B, B⁺) → (D, D⁺) under (A, A⁺) are exactly the A-algebra homomorphisms B → D; so B ↦ (B, B⁺) is a fully faithful functor from finite étale A-algebras to complete Huber pairs under (A, A⁺). (v) Base change and rational restriction: for every morphism (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) of complete Tate pairs, C ⊗_A B is finite étale over C, its natural C-module topology is the tensor-product topology, the canonical map C ⊗_A B → C ⊗̂_A B to the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product) is a topological isomorphism, and Huber.Pair.finiteEtale C⁺ (C ⊗_A B) is the completed tensor product of pairs (plus ring the integral closure of the image of C⁺ ⊗ B⁺); for a rational subset U = R(f/g) of Spa(A, A⁺), Spa(ι)⁻¹(U) is the rational subset R(ι(f)/ι(g)) and O(U) ⊗_A B ≅ B⟨ι(f)/ι(g)⟩ as topological rings, compatibly with plus rings. (vi) Comparison: if A is strongly noetherian or has a noetherian ring of definition, (B, B⁺) is the pair Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid, and Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is finite and étale in Huber's sense (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison, Huber 1.6.6(ii)). Sheafiness of (B, B⁺) is not part of this construction: it holds when A is strongly sheafy (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-strongly-sheafy) and is not known for A merely sheafy (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18). The comparison FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(A^u) with the uniformisation belongs to AdicEtaleGeometry:A4.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair; no sheafiness or noetherian hypothesis.
  • B finite étale over A as a ring (finite, flat, finitely presented, unramified); topology = natural module topology.
  • B⁺ is the integral closure of the image of A⁺, never B° (the two differ when A⁺ ≠ A°).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra

The small finite étale siteconstruction

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. The small finite étale site X_fét consists of the full subcategory AdicSpace.smallFiniteEtale X of adic spaces finite étale over X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism; all X-morphisms, which are finite étale by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation) with the topology generated by the jointly surjective families (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19). (i) X_fét has finite limits (fibre products by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; equalisers are open and closed subspaces by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), finite coproducts (disjoint unions) and an initial object ∅, and the jointly surjective families form a pretopology; (ii) for X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, global sections give an equivalence X_fét ≃ FÉt(A)^op (Mathlib CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A), with quasi-inverse B ↦ Spa(Huber.Pair.finiteEtale A⁺ B) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c); Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(a)); under it a finite family (B_i) is a covering iff ∏_i B_i is faithfully flat over A; (iii) the inclusion ι: X_fét → X_ét is fully faithful, preserves finite limits and coverings, and so defines a morphism of sites X_ét → X_fét; (iv) for g: X' → X, base change defines a morphism of sites X'_fét → X_fét compatible with (iii); (v) for connected X and a geometric point ξ, the fibre functor makes X_fét a Galois category (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category).

Hypotheses

  • X locally strongly sheafy analytic.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site

The Kedlaya–Liu étale and finite étale sites of an arbitrary analytic adic spaceconstruction

Let X be an analytic adic space, not necessarily locally strongly sheafy, regarded as an analytic Yoneda-adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation: sheaves on complete Huber pairs for the rational topology glued from the sheafified spectra Spa^Y(A, A⁺); on complete Tate pairs these are Kedlaya–Liu's preadic spaces and Scholze–Weinstein's adic spaces; the anchor's adic spaces form a full subcategory, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces). For morphisms of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces define finite étale and étale by the local descriptions of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism with Spa^Y in place of Spa (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.16 verbatim), and let X_ét^Y, X_fét^Y be Kedlaya–Liu's small étale and finite étale sites (Definition 8.2.19): objects all étale (resp. finite étale) morphisms Y → X of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces, coverings the set-theoretic (jointly surjective) families. Then: (i) fibre products exist (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-fibre-products), the two classes are stable under base change and composition, and the covering families form pretopologies (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.5, Lemma 8.2.17(c)); (ii) for every complete Tate pair (A, A⁺), sheafy or not, global sections give Spa^Y(A, A⁺)_fét^Y ≃ FÉt(A)^op (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.17(a)); (iii) if X is locally strongly sheafy, every object of X_ét^Y is (the image of) an adic space and X_ét^Y ≃ X_ét, X_fét^Y ≃ X_fét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site); (iv) geometric points define points of X_ét^Y and form a conservative family, by the proofs of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points (only Spa(C, C⁺), which is sheafy, is used); (v) this is the site Y_ét, Y_fét of ECD Lemma 15.6 for an analytic adic space Y over ℤ_p, the right-hand side of the comparison Y^◇_ét ≅ Y_ét owned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D6, in the generality ECD Definition 15.5 allows ('adic spaces as defined in [SW13, Section 2.1]').

Hypotheses

  • X analytic; Yoneda-adic spaces, Spa^Y, open immersions, fibre products and |−| as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation and its lemmas.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized

The sites G-fsets and G-pfsets of finite and profinite G-sets, with corrected coverings (Scholze Definition 3.4 with the erratum)construction

Let G be a profinite group. G-fsets is the category of finite discrete sets with continuous G-action, with coverings the jointly surjective families. G-pfsets is the category of profinite sets with continuous G-action and continuous G-maps; every object is a cofiltered limit of finite G-sets (quotients by open G-invariant equivalence relations), and G-pfsets ≃ Pro(G-fsets). A G-map S_1 → S is G-étale if it is the pullback of a map of finite G-sets along some G-map S → B with B finite, and a G-tower if S_1 = lim_{μ<λ} S_μ with S_0 = S and each S_μ → S_{<μ} := lim_{μ'<μ} S_{μ'} the pullback of a surjection of finite G-sets. A family {f_i: S_i → S} is a (corrected) covering if S = ⋃ f_i(S_i) and each f_i is a G-tower followed by a G-étale map. These coverings form a pretopology; the printed Definition 3.4 (all families of open maps) is replaced by it. For a topological G-module M, F_M(S) := Hom_cont,G(S, M) is a sheaf on G-pfsets. For trivial G, the underlying category is Profinite.

Hypotheses

  • G profinite; the erratum's 'similar condition' for Definition 3.4 is read with the G-étale factor so that a disjoint union is covered by its summands (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E6).
  • Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site

The pro-finite étale site X_profét, with Scholze's corrected coverings (Definition 3.3 with the erratum)construction

Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space, every point analytic, so X is locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X_ét is its small étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and X_fét its finite étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). X_profét is the category pro-X_fét := Pro(X_fét), a full subcategory of pro-X_ét and of X_proét, with |U| = lim |U_i|. A family {f_i: U_i → U} is a covering if |U| = ⋃ f_i(|U_i|) and each f_i factors as a pro-finite-étale tower U_i → W_i (steps pullbacks of finite étale surjections of X_fét; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-tower) followed by a morphism W_i → U that is the pullback of a morphism of X_fét along some U → V_0 with V_0 ∈ X_fét. These coverings form a pretopology. The printed Definition 3.3 (families of open morphisms) is replaced by this condition; the erratum states the condition with the tower only, which read literally would exclude the covering of a disjoint union by its summands (sourceIssues AdicEtaleGeometry/E6).

Hypotheses

  • X as stated; the tower steps and the second factor come from X_fét.
  • Size: a Grothendieck universe is fixed; X_ét is locally small, pro-objects are indexed by small cofiltered categories, so pro-X_ét is locally small, and sheaves take values in small sets.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-finite-etale-site-corrected

The rational-covering site on the opposite category of complete Huber pairsconstruction

CAff is the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff Huber rings, A⁺ a ring of integral elements) with morphisms tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom (continuous ring maps carrying A⁺ into B⁺). For (A, A⁺) ∈ CAff and rational subsets U_1, …, U_n (U_k = R(T_k/s_k) with T_k·A open; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset) covering Spa(A, A⁺), the family of rational localisations (A, A⁺) → (O(U_k), O⁺(U_k)) (anchor Layer 3.1: the completed A⟨T_k/s_k⟩ with the integral closure of the image of A⁺[T_k/s_k]) is a rational covering family of (A, A⁺)ᵒᵖ in CAffᵒᵖ; n = 0 is allowed exactly when Spa(A, A⁺) = ∅, i.e. A = 0. The rational covering families form a coverage on CAffᵒᵖ (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Coverage): for every morphism (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is a rational covering family of (B, B⁺) each member of which factors through a member of the given family. J_rat := Coverage.toGrothendieck is the rational topology; a presheaf of sets on CAffᵒᵖ is a J_rat-sheaf iff it satisfies the sheaf condition for all rational covering families (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheaf_coverage). The presheaf 𝒪: (A, A⁺) ↦ A is represented by (Z[T], Z) (discrete) and satisfies the sheaf condition at the rational covering families of (A, A⁺) and of all its rational localisations iff the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf of sets on rational covers; for complete Tate pairs this is sheafiness in the anchor's sense (Huber.IsSheafyPair), the topology being automatic by the open mapping theorem (anchor Layer 0.6).

Hypotheses

  • Complete means complete and Hausdorff (anchor convention 3).
  • Pullbacks of rational subsets along non-adic morphisms need not be rational; the coverage axiom only needs a rational refinement, which exists by quasi-compactness.
  • Size: CAff is formed from pairs in a fixed universe; sheaves take values in the next universe, where sheafification exists.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site

A2Separatedness, smooth charts, and classical analytic geometry

Smooth morphismdefinitionplanetSmooth morphisms of analytic adic spaces by local étale charts over relative balls (ECD 24.4)

Let f : Y' → Y be a morphism of analytic adic spaces with Y covered by open affinoids whose rings are complete and stably sheafy, so that the relative polydiscs B^n_Y exist (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc). f is locally étale over a relative ball (AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc f) if every y' ∈ Y' has an open neighbourhood U, an integer n ≥ 0 and a morphism g : U → B^n_Y that is étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (locally an open immersion, a finite étale morphism and an open immersion; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison), with f|_U = π ∘ g. This is the notion 'smooth' of ECD Proposition 24.4 for analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p, including non-noetherian ones such as spaces étale over a perfectoid or sousperfectoid base. Conventions: the charts are local on the source and n may vary with y'; étale is A1's local description, which on locally noetherian spaces is Huber's étale (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation); on locally noetherian analytic spaces the class equals Huber's smooth morphisms (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-local-ball-charts), and on general bases Huber's infinitesimal definition is not used. Lean name: AdicSpace.IsLocallyEtaleOverPolydisc.

Hypotheses

  • Y analytic and covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids; Y' analytic.
  • Étale in the local-description sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts

Dimension of adic spacesdefinitionplanetDimension, pure dimension and relative dimension of adic spaces (Huber 1.8.1)

Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5); its underlying space is locally spectral, hence sober and T0. The dimension of X is dim X := topologicalKrullDim |X| ∈ ℕ∞ ∪ {⊥} (Mathlib topologicalKrullDim: the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets), which is the supremum of the lengths d of chains of specializations x₀ ≻ x₁ ≻ ⋯ ≻ x_d of pairwise distinct points of X (Huber 1996, Definition 1.8.1, as stated in Zavyalov, Definition 3.1); dim ∅ = ⊥. X is of pure dimension d if every nonempty open subset of X has dimension d. For a morphism f : X → Y of analytic adic spaces, the relative dimension is dim f := sup_{y ∈ Y} dim f⁻¹(y), where f⁻¹(y) ⊆ X carries the subspace topology, and f is of relative pure dimension d if every nonempty fibre f⁻¹(y) is of pure dimension d. Conventions: the dimension is that of the topological space, not the Krull dimension of a ring of functions — Spa(K, K⁺) for a complete rank-one field K and a valuation ring K⁺ ⊆ K° of rank r has dimension r − 1 while K has Krull dimension 0; the fibre is the subspace f⁻¹(y), and its comparison with the adic fibre over rank-one points is AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres. This topological relative dimension is distinct from R0's rank of Ω_{X/Y} (API AdicSpace.Smooth.relativeDimension); they agree for smooth morphisms by AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-pure-relative-dimension. Lean name: AdicSpace.dim.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space; for dim f, f a morphism of analytic adic spaces.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces

Relative closed unit ballconstructionplanetThe relative closed unit polydisc B^n_X over an adic space

Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5) covered by open affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B complete and stably sheafy (for instance X locally noetherian), and n ≥ 0. The relative closed unit polydisc of dimension n is B^n_X := X ×_{Spa(ℤ, ℤ)} Spa(ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ], ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ]) (both rings discrete), which exists because Spa(ℤ[T], ℤ[T]) → Spa(ℤ, ℤ) is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence (a)); it comes with the projection π : B^n_X → X and the coordinates T₁, …, Tₙ ∈ O⁺(B^n_X). Properties: (a) charts — over an open affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X, π⁻¹(Spa(B, B⁺)) = Spa(B⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩, B⁺⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩), where B⟨T⟩ is the completed ring of restricted power series (Tau Ceti restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion) and B⁺⟨T⟩ the series with all coefficients in B⁺; B⁺⟨T⟩ is integrally closed in B⟨T⟩, so it is Huber's plus ring and ECD's B^n_Y; (b) universal property — for an adic space Z over X, Hom_X(Z, B^n_X) ≅ O⁺_Z(Z)ⁿ by pulling back T₁, …, Tₙ; (c) base change — B^n_X ×_X X' ≅ B^n_{X'} for X' → X with X' of the same kind, and B^{m+n}_X ≅ B^m_X ×_X B^n_X; (d) π is quasi-compact, separated and smooth with Ω_{B^n_X/X} free on dT₁, …, dTₙ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/restricted-power-series-smooth), and B^n_X is locally noetherian (resp. analytic) when X is; (e) for X locally noetherian and analytic, B^n_X is the open subspace {|T₁|, …, |Tₙ| ≤ 1} of the relative affine space A^n_ℤ ×_{Spec ℤ} X (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification). Conventions: the plus ring is B⁺⟨T⟩, not the power-bounded subring B⟨T⟩°: over Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ ⊊ K° the fibre is Spa(K⟨T⟩, K⁺⟨T⟩), whereas Tau Ceti's closedPolydisc over K uses K⟨T⟩° = K°⟨T⟩; the radius is 1, and polydiscs of radius |ϖ|^{−k} are the rational subsets {|ϖᵏTᵢ| ≤ 1} of the relative affine space. Lean name: AdicSpace.relativePolydisc.

Hypotheses

  • X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (so that the fibre product exists as an adic space).
  • Discrete topology on ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ] with plus ring ℤ[T₁, …, Tₙ].

AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc

Relative torusconstructionplanetThe relative torus T^n_X ⊆ B^n_X

Let X be as in AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc and n ≥ 0. The relative torus is the open subspace T^n_X := {|T₁ ⋯ Tₙ| ≥ 1} = {|T₁| = … = |Tₙ| = 1} of B^n_X; over an affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X it is the rational subset R(1/(T₁ ⋯ Tₙ)) of Spa(B⟨T⟩, B⁺⟨T⟩), with coordinate ring B⟨T₁^{±1}, …, Tₙ^{±1}⟩ and plus ring B⁺⟨T^{±1}⟩; equivalently T^n_X = X ×_{Spa ℤ} Spa(ℤ[T^{±1}], ℤ[T^{±1}]). Properties: (a) universal property — Hom_X(Z, T^n_X) ≅ ((O⁺_Z(Z))^×)ⁿ, the units of O_Z(Z) that lie in O⁺_Z(Z) with inverse in O⁺_Z(Z); (b) T^n_X → X is smooth (an open subspace of B^n_X), T^n_X ×_X X' ≅ T^n_{X'}, T^{m+n}_X ≅ T^m_X ×_X T^n_X, and T^n_X is a commutative group object over X (coordinatewise multiplication); (c) over Spa(K, K°) it is Scholze's Tⁿ = Spa(K⟨T^{±1}⟩, K°⟨T^{±1}⟩); (d) for a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ of O(X), Tᵢ ↦ 1 + ϖTᵢ identifies B^n_X with the rational subset {|Tᵢ − 1| ≤ |ϖ|} of T^n_X (Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 5.2, with ϖ = p); (e) B¹_X is covered by T¹_X and its translate {|T − 1| = 1} (ECD, proof of Proposition 24.4). Conventions: T^n_X is the unit polyannulus, not the analytified torus (G_m^n)^{ad} (which is not quasi-compact over a field). Lean name: AdicSpace.relativeTorus.

Hypotheses

  • X covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids; for (d), ϖ a topologically nilpotent unit (X analytic, locally).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-torus

A3The nonnoetherian affinoid étale approximation input

Stably pseudocoherent moduledefinitionplanetStrictly and stably pseudocoherent modules over a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definitions 1.2.13 and 2.4.1)

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu's adic Banach ring: A complete Hausdorff with a pseudouniformiser ϖ, A⁺ a ring of integral elements). An A-module M is strictly m-pseudocoherent (resp. strictly m-fpd) if it is m-pseudocoherent (resp. m-fpd) (A3/pseudocoherent-module) and complete — in particular Hausdorff — for its natural topology (A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness). M is stably m-pseudocoherent (resp. stably m-fpd) if it is m-pseudocoherent (resp. m-fpd) and for every rational localisation (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) — B = A⟨T/s⟩ the completed localisation at a rational subset R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) (anchor Layer 3; Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization) — the algebraic tensor product M ⊗_A B is complete for its natural topology as a B-module. 'Stably pseudocoherent' means stably ∞-pseudocoherent. Pinned conventions: tensor products are algebraic, and the definition asks that they already be complete (no completed tensor product is formed); the identity localisation is included, so stably implies strictly; the plus ring enters only through the set of rational subsets; no sheafiness is assumed in the definition. Lean names: Huber.IsStrictlyPseudoCoherent, Huber.IsStablyPseudoCoherent, Huber.IsStablyFPD.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair
  • m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}; the natural topology is that of A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness

AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module

Standard étale presentationdefinitionplanetStandard étale presentations of complete Huber pairs over a complete Tate pair

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ and X = Spa(A, A⁺). A standard étale presentation of a complete Huber pair (C, C⁺) over (A, A⁺) is a tuple (N, F, k, π) consisting of N ≥ 0, F = (F₁, …, F_N) ∈ A⁺⟨T₁, …, T_N⟩^N, k ≥ 0 and a morphism of Huber pairs π: (A⟨T⟩, A⁺⟨T⟩) → (C, C⁺) over (A, A⁺) such that (i) π is surjective, ker π is the closure of the ideal (F₁, …, F_N), and C⁺ is the integral closure of π(A⁺⟨T⟩) — so (C, C⁺) is the quotient pair A⟨T⟩/closure((F)) (Tau Ceti Pair.quotient); (ii) the Jacobian J_F := det(∂Fᵢ/∂T_j) ∈ A⁺⟨T⟩ (termwise partial derivatives) maps to a unit of C with ϖᵏ·π(J_F)^{−1} ∈ C⁺ (the Jacobian inverse is bounded by |ϖ|^{−k}). The associated affinoid V(F) := Spa(C, C⁺) → B^N_X is the standard étale locus. A presentation is in explicit-inverse form with exponent k' if N = N' + 1, T = (T', S) and F = (F', S·J_{F'} − ϖ^{k'}); then J_F = J_{F'}², |J_{F'}| ≥ |ϖ^{k'}| on V(F), condition (ii) holds with k = 2k', and every presentation can be put in this form (API withInverse). Pinned conventions: the number of equations equals the number of variables and all variables have weight 1 (the Tate case of Huber's presentations A⟨X⟩_{T₁,…,T_n}, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-presentation-perturbation); coefficients lie in A⁺ (rescaling by powers of ϖ does not change the ideal); the plus ring is always the integral closure of the image; rational subsets of B^N_X are absorbed by extra variables (A3/standard-presentation-basic-pieces); no sheafiness is part of the definition. Lean name: Huber.StandardEtalePresentation A A⁺ C C⁺.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair; (C, C⁺) complete Huber pair over it

AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/standard-etale-presentation

Pseudocoherent and finite-projective-dimension modules over a commutative ring (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.1.1)definition

Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module and m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. M is m-pseudocoherent if it admits a resolution ⋯ → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 by projective R-modules in which P_i is finitely generated for every i ≤ m; M is pseudocoherent if it is ∞-pseudocoherent. M is m-fpd if it admits a resolution 0 → P_m → ⋯ → P_0 → M → 0 by finitely generated projective R-modules of length at most m, and fpd if it is m-fpd for some m. Pinned conventions: m-pseudocoherence is a property of the module only (no topology); 0-pseudocoherent means finitely generated (Mathlib Module.Finite) and 1-pseudocoherent means finitely presented (Mathlib Module.FinitePresentation); for m ≥ 2 the condition is strictly stronger than finite presentation over non-coherent rings (such as perfectoid rings and their Tate algebras). This is the pseudo-coherence of SGA 6 (Stacks Project Tag 064N), not the notion of Hartshorne's Exercise I.2.11. Every fpd module is pseudocoherent. Lean names: Module.IsPseudoCoherent R M m, Module.IsFPD R M m.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative; M an arbitrary R-module
  • m ranges over ℕ ∪ {∞}; the m-fpd condition asks for finitely generated projective terms and length ≤ m

AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/pseudocoherent-module

Pseudoflat modules over a complete Tate Huber pair (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.4.4)definition

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair and m ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. A topological A-module B is m-pseudoflat if Tor₁^A(P, B) = 0 for every stably m-pseudocoherent A-module P (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module); pseudoflat means ∞-pseudoflat. Equivalent forms (Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 2.4.5): Tor₁^A(M, B) = 0 for every strictly m-pseudocoherent M implies m-pseudoflatness; and m-pseudoflatness is equivalent to injectivity of M ⊗_A B → N ⊗_A B for every short exact sequence 0 → M → N → P → 0 with N finite projective and P stably m-pseudocoherent. A complete metrizable A-module B is pro-projective if it carries a filtered family of continuous A-linear projectors πₖ with finite projective images and πₖ(v) → v for all v (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.4.6). Pinned conventions: Tor is algebraic; only Tor₁ is required (higher Tor need not vanish); 2-pseudoflat implies m-pseudoflat for all m ≥ 2, in particular pseudoflat. Lean names: Huber.IsPseudoFlat A B m, Huber.IsProProjective A B.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) complete Tate Huber pair; B a topological A-module (for rational localisations, an A-algebra)

AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/pseudoflat-module

Pseudocoherent and fpd sheaves of O-modules on adic spaces (Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 2.5.3)definition

Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5) covered by affinoid opens Spa(B, B⁺) with (B, B⁺) a sheafy complete Tate Huber pair. A sheaf F of O_X-modules is pseudocoherent (resp. fpd) if X has a covering by such affinoid opens U = Spa(B, B⁺) with F|_U ≅ M̃ for a stably pseudocoherent (resp. stably fpd) B-module M (A3/stably-pseudocoherent-module, A3/pseudocoherent-tate-acyclicity). By A3/rational-localisation-pseudoflat the condition passes to open subspaces and to rational subsets of the chosen affinoids. Pinned conventions: F is a sheaf of O_X-modules on the analytic (not étale) topology; the modules are stably, not merely strictly, pseudocoherent; in AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 the spaces X are rational subsets of relative balls B^N_X over affinoid perfectoid X, which are sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings) and hence sheafy. Lean names: AdicSpace.IsPseudoCoherentSheaf F, AdicSpace.IsFPDSheaf F.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space with a basis of affinoids Spa(B, B⁺), (B, B⁺) sheafy complete Tate
  • F a sheaf of O_X-modules

A4Analytic adic presentations for diamondification

Ring with no nonsplit finite étale coversdefinitionplanetRings with no nonsplit finite étale covers

Let R be a commutative ring. A finite étale R-algebra T (Mathlib Algebra.Etale R T together with Module.Finite R T) is *totally split* if there are finitely many idempotents e₁, …, e_m ∈ R (m ≥ 0, repetitions and zero allowed) and an isomorphism of R-algebras T ≅ ∏_{j=1}^{m} R/(1 − e_j)R. The ring R *has no nonsplit finite étale covers* (Lean: the class IsFiniteEtaleSplit R) if every finite étale R-algebra is totally split. Equivalent characterisation: every finite étale R-algebra T that is faithfully flat over R (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat R T; for T finite étale this says that the rank of T is ≥ 1 at every prime of R) admits an R-algebra homomorphism T → R. Consequence used in ECD §15: if P ∈ R[X] is monic of degree d ≥ 1 and the class of P′ is a unit of R[X]/(P) (so that (P, 1) is a Mathlib StandardEtalePair), then P has a root in R, because R[X]/(P) is étale and free of rank d, hence a faithfully flat finite étale R-algebra. For a field K the condition is equivalent to K being separably closed (Mathlib IsSepClosed K). If a ring homomorphism φ : R → R′ induces, by base change, an equivalence between the categories of finite étale algebras, then R has no nonsplit finite étale covers if and only if R′ has none. Pinned conventions: 'split' means totally split over R itself (not after a further faithfully flat extension); the zero algebra is totally split (m = 0); no topology is involved.

Hypotheses

  • R an arbitrary commutative ring; the zero ring is allowed (it has no nonsplit finite étale covers).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring

Finite étale torsor towerconstructionplanetThe cofiltered system of finite étale torsors with no remaining nonsplit finite étale covers (ECD Lemma 15.3, first part)

Let A be a commutative ring. A *finite étale torsor tower* over A (Lean: the structure FiniteEtaleTorsorTower A) consists of a directed set I; for i ∈ I a finite group G_i and an A-algebra A_i with a G_i-action making it a finite étale G_i-torsor over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor); for i ≤ j a surjective homomorphism π_{ij} : G_j → G_i and an A-algebra homomorphism ι_{ij} : A_i → A_j with ι_{ij}(π_{ij}(g)·a) = g·ι_{ij}(a), both functorial in i ≤ j ≤ k (π_{ii} = id, π_{ik} = π_{ij} ∘ π_{jk}, and likewise for ι); such that the direct limit A_∞ := colim_i A_i (Mathlib Ring.DirectLimit) has no nonsplit finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring). Its group is the profinite group G := lim_i G_i (Mathlib ProfiniteGrp), which acts on A_∞ by A-algebra automorphisms with open stabilisers. Construction (Lean: FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.canonical A), showing that every ring has a tower: choose a set T of representatives of the isomorphism classes of finite étale A-algebras and, for each S ∈ T, a splitting torsor A → P(S) under a finite group G(S) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/splitting-torsor-of-finite-etale-algebra); index by the finite subsets F ⊆ T ordered by inclusion, with G_F := ∏_{S ∈ F} G(S), A_F := ⊗_{S ∈ F} P(S) (tensor product over A; A_∅ = A), π the projections and ι the inclusions of tensor factors. Properties: every finite étale A-algebra becomes totally split over some A_i; A_j is a (ker π_{ij})-torsor over A_i, so all transition maps are injective and faithfully flat; (A_∞)^G = A; and a ⊗ b ↦ (g ↦ a·g(b)) is an isomorphism A_∞ ⊗_A A_∞ ≅ LC(G, A_∞) onto the locally constant maps (Mathlib LocallyConstant). Pinned conventions: G_i acts on the left and π_{ij} goes from the larger index to the smaller; no topology is involved (the topological completion is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair).

Hypotheses

  • A an arbitrary commutative ring (the torsor tower is purely algebraic).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower

Completed torsor towerconstructionplanetThe uniform completion (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) of a finite étale torsor tower over a complete Tate pair

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformizer, and T a finite étale torsor tower over the ring A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower) with levels A_i, groups G_i and G = lim G_i. (a) Levels: (A_i, A_i⁺) is the Huber pair of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (A_i with its natural topology as a finite projective A-module, a complete Tate ring; A_i⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ in A_i); the transition maps ι_{ij} and the action of G_i are morphisms of Huber pairs. (b) Colimit: A_∞ = colim A_i carries the unique ring topology in which A_∞^♮ := colim_i A_i° (a subring, A_i° the power-bounded subring, Tau Ceti powerBoundedSubring) is open and carries its ϖ-adic topology; with A_∞⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺ this is a Tate Huber pair (A_∞, A_∞⁺) with ring of definition A_∞^♮, and it is uniform: A_∞° ⊆ ϖ⁻¹A_∞^♮. (c) Completion: the completed tower pair is (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) := the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of (A_∞, A_∞⁺); since A_∞ is uniform it is the Hausdorff completion (Tau Ceti IsTateRing.completion), Â_∞ is a complete uniform Tate ring with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion of A_∞^♮, and Â_∞⁺ is the closure of the image of colim_i A_i⁺ — this is ECD's 'uniform completion Â_∞ of A_∞' with 'Â_∞⁺ the closure of lim A_i⁺'. (d) G acts on (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) by automorphisms of Huber pairs over (A, A⁺), continuously (the action map G × Â_∞ → Â_∞ is continuous for the profinite topology of G). (e) Universal property: for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded, morphisms of Huber pairs (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) → (B, B⁺) correspond bijectively to families of morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (B, B⁺) compatible with the ι_{ij}. Lean: FiniteEtaleTorsorTower.completion T P for P the Huber pair (A, A⁺). Pinned conventions: the colimit topology is the one of the Berkeley lectures (colim A_i° open and bounded), not the colimit of chosen rings of definition; completeness of A is part of the hypotheses (it is needed for the levels (a) and for AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower).

Hypotheses

  • A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with a ring of integral elements A⁺; ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformizer.
  • T a finite étale torsor tower over the underlying ring of A.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair

Perfectoid torsor presentationconstructionplanetPerfectoid torsor presentation of a complete Tate ℤ_p-pair: a perfectoid cover and its induced perfectoid equivalence relation

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent. A *perfectoid torsor presentation* of (A, A⁺) (Lean: the structure Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation P for P the pair (A, A⁺)) consists of a profinite group G (Mathlib ProfiniteGrp), a complete Huber pair (Ã, Ã⁺) with Ã a perfectoid Tate ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), a continuous action of G on (Ã, Ã⁺) by automorphisms of Huber pairs, and a G-invariant morphism of Huber pairs q : (A, A⁺) → (Ã, Ã⁺), such that (a) the map b ⊗ b′ ↦ (g ↦ b·g(b′)) induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs from the uniform completed tensor product Ã ⊗̂ᵘ_A Ã (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) onto (C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)); (b) Spa(q) : Spa(Ã, Ã⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is spectral (in particular quasi-compact), surjective and open, with fibres exactly the G-orbits, so that it induces a homeomorphism |Spa(Ã, Ã⁺)|/G ≅ |Spa(A, A⁺)|. The *perfectoid cover* is X̃ = Spa(Ã, Ã⁺); the *induced perfectoid equivalence relation* is R̃ = Spa(C^0(G, Ã), C^0(G, Ã⁺)) ≅ G × X̃ with the two maps s, t : R̃ ⇉ X̃ induced by b ↦ (g ↦ b) and b ↦ (g ↦ g·b), identity X̃ → R̃ (evaluation at 1) and composition induced by C^0(G, Ã) → C^0(G × G, Ã) — the action groupoid of G on X̃, with all objects affinoid perfectoid. Construction (Huber.PerfectoidTorsorPresentation.ofTower): for a finite étale torsor tower T over A (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower), take G = lim G_i and (Ã, Ã⁺) = (Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-pair); it is perfectoid by AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion, (a) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product and (b) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower; for presentations from towers, finite étale A-algebras are equivalent to finite étale Ã-algebras with descent data over C^0(G, Ã) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-effective-descent-along-tower). This is the generalized-affinoid presentation used in ECD §15: (A, A⁺) need not be sheafy, while X̃ and R̃ are affinoid perfectoid. Pinned conventions: R̃ is an equivalence relation only in the category of v-sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks D6); on underlying sets |R̃| → |X̃| ×_{|Spa A|} |X̃| is surjective but not injective; the quasi-compactness in (b) is part of the definition, and a map that is merely surjective on points is not a presentation.

Hypotheses

  • A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with p topologically nilpotent; A⁺ any ring of integral elements; no sheafiness of (A, A⁺).

AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation

Finite étale G-torsors of commutative ringsdefinition

Let G be a finite group, A a commutative ring and B a commutative A-algebra on which G acts by A-algebra automorphisms (Mathlib MulSemiringAction G B with SMulCommClass G A B). B is a *finite étale G-torsor over A* (Lean: Algebra.IsFiniteEtaleTorsor G A B) if B is a finite étale and faithfully flat A-algebra and the Galois map γ : B ⊗_A B → Map(G, B) = ∏_{g ∈ G} B, γ(b ⊗ b′)(g) = b·g(b′), is bijective (geometrically: Spec B → Spec A is a torsor under the constant finite group scheme G). Consequences: B is finite projective of constant rank |G|; A → B is injective and B^G = A (Mathlib Algebra.IsInvariant A B G); if A ≠ 0 the action is faithful, so Mathlib's IsGaloisGroup G A B holds; more generally γ induces B^{⊗(k+1)} ≅ Map(G^k, B) for k ≥ 0. Constructions: the trivial torsor Map(G, A) with (h·f)(g) = f(gh); the tensor product B ⊗_A B′ of a G-torsor and a G′-torsor is a (G × G′)-torsor; base change along any ring homomorphism A → A′ preserves torsors; if π : G′ → G is surjective and B → B′ is an A-algebra map from a G-torsor to a G′-torsor with g′·ι(b) = ι(π(g′)·b), then B′ is a (ker π)-torsor over B, so ι is faithfully flat and injective. For A = K a field and B a field, B is a G-torsor over K iff B/K is a finite Galois extension and G → Gal(B/K) is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: G acts on the left; the Galois map is b ⊗ b′ ↦ (b·g(b′))_g; faithful flatness is part of the definition (this excludes B = 0 over A ≠ 0).

Hypotheses

  • G finite; A, B commutative; G acts by A-algebra automorphisms of B.

Classical Serre Modularity

Galois representations and modularity · 3 constructions · 2 planets

R33.2Good-dihedral auxiliary ramification

Paso 2: the good-dihedral prime NconstructionplanetPaso 2: inserting the good-dihedral prime N

Let {ρ^{(1)}_ℓ} be the weight-2 system of Paso 1, with coefficient field K and ramification set S₁. Choose a prime q ≡ 1 mod 4, q > 5, larger than every prime of S₁ and split in K. Either ρ^{(1)}_q is modular (solvable residual image: R33.1/solvable-residual-termination, with ρ̄^{(1)}_q not bad dihedral since k = 2 and q > 5), or ρ̄^{(1)}_q : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽_q) — 𝔽_q-valued because q splits in K — has non-solvable image. Choose N ∉ S₁ by Lemma 1.15 (= KW I Lemma 8.2, R27.1): Tr ρ̄^{(1)}_q(Frob_N) = 0 and χ̄_q(Frob_N) = −1, so ρ̄^{(1)}_q|_{D_N} is, up to twist, diag(χ̄_q, 1), and q | N + 1. Theorem 1.9(4) gives a lift ρ^{(2)}_q, crystalline of weight 2 at q, whose inertial type at N is that of τ_N = Ind κ (R33.2/dihedral-local-type-at-n): ρ^{(2)}_q(I_N) is cyclic of order q, acting through κ ⊕ κ^N, and the projective image of D_N is dihedral of order 2q. The image of D_N itself is infinite, since det ρ^{(2)}_q(Frob_N) = ψ(N)·N is not a root of unity; by Theorem 1.4, ρ^{(1)}_q is modular iff ρ^{(2)}_q is, and Theorem 1.11 puts ρ^{(2)}_q in an almost strictly compatible system {ρ^{(2)}_ℓ} with ramification set S = S₁ ∪ {N}.

Hypotheses

  • Theorem 1.9 requires absolute irreducibility over ℚ(ζ_q) (non-solvable image gives it) and allows prescribing any compatible type at primes of Σ
  • Lemma 1.15 is stated for 𝔽_q-valued ρ̄, matching the rationality correction to KW I Lemma 8.2; this is why q is taken split in K
  • the attributions of Theorem 1.9(4) split: partial results in KW I Theorem 5.1, the general case Gee and Snowden Theorem 7.2.1 (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3)
  • N ≡ 1 mod 8 and N ≡ 1 modulo every prime ≤ q − 1 (Lemma 1.15(2)) are what Lemma 2.1 needs later
  • DP p. 11 speaks of a lift "with such a dihedral image of order 2q at the prime N"; only the inertial type and the projective image have that form (source issue ClassicalSerreModularity/E8), and Lemma 2.1 uses only the inertial type

ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.2/dp-lift-existence-and-good-dihedral-insertion

The dihedral local type Ind κ at the auxiliary prime Nconstruction

Let q be an odd prime and N a prime with q | N + 1 (so q ∤ N − 1). Let ℚ_{N²} be the unramified quadratic extension of ℚ_N; its residue field is 𝔽_{N²}, whose unit group has order N² − 1 = (N − 1)(N + 1). By local class field theory there is a character κ : G_{ℚ_{N²}} → ℤ̄_q^× of order q whose restriction to the inertia group I_N factors through 𝔽_{N²}^× and not through 𝔽_N^× (niveau 2), normalised by κ(Art(N)) = 1, that is, trivial on the Frobenius of G_{ℚ_{N²}} attached to the uniformiser N. Its induction τ_N = Ind_{G_{ℚ_{N²}}}^{G_{ℚ_N}} κ is irreducible, τ_N|_{I_N} ≅ κ ⊕ κ^N, and its image is dihedral of order 2q. Without the normalisation, κ(Art(N)) = ζ ≠ 1 is a scalar in the image, which then has order 2q²; the projective image is dihedral of order 2q in either case, and the inertial type depends only on κ|_{I_N}. Its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is unramified (κ̄ = 1, as 𝔽̄_q^× has no element of order q) with zero trace at Frobenius. The same construction with coefficients in ℤ̄_p for p ≠ q stays irreducible after reduction.

Hypotheses

  • q odd and q | N + 1; the source prints "residue field has order (N − 1)(N + 1)" and "restriction to the inertia group at q" (source issues ClassicalSerreModularity/E4 and E5)
  • κ exists because 𝒪_{ℚ_{N²}}^× → 𝔽_{N²}^× has a cyclic quotient of order q (q | N² − 1), extended to G_{ℚ_{N²}} by local class field theory
  • level 2 is essential: a character of order q factoring through 𝔽_N^× would make Ind κ reducible on inertia
  • the normalisation κ(Art(N)) = 1 is needed for the image of τ_N to be dihedral of order 2q; the source (Paso 2) speaks of a dihedral representation, which is true for every κ in the sense of being induced, and only the inertial type of τ_N is used by the nodes that consume it

R33.3The prime two and the auxiliary prime

Lemma 2.3: the order-three type at 2constructionplanetLemma 2.3: the order-three local type at 2, reached by a congruence at 3

Let {ρ_ℓ} be an almost strictly compatible system with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, unramified at 3, whose Weil–Deligne representation at 2 is a twist of Steinberg, and with ρ̄₃ of non-solvable image. Let χ′ be a character of G_{ℚ₄} (ℚ₄ the unramified quadratic extension of ℚ₂) of order 3 and niveau 2, and ρ̃₂ = Ind_{G_{ℚ₄}}^{G_{ℚ₂}} χ′ (3-adic), so ρ̃₂|_{I₂} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′² with trivial monodromy. Then ρ̄₃|_{D₂} ≅ (χ̄₃ ∗; 0 1) up to twist, and ρ̄₃ and ρ̃₂ have the same reduction on I₂ and zero trace at Frobenius; Theorem 1.9(4) gives a crystalline weight-2 lift ρ′₃ of ρ̄₃ with inertial type ρ̃₂|_{I₂} at 2 (and the previous types elsewhere), and Theorem 1.11 a system {ρ′_ℓ} with the same Hodge–Tate weights and ramification set, congruent to {ρ_ℓ} at 3, whose type at 2 comes from an order-3 character. Modularity of one system is equivalent to modularity of the other (Theorem 1.4 at 3).

Hypotheses

  • Lemma 2.3 needs the system unramified at 3, Steinberg (up to twist) at 2, and non-solvable residual image at 3
  • k(ρ̄₃) = 2: the system is unramified at 3 with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, so ρ₃ is crystalline at 3 and ρ̄₃ is finite flat; this is what allows a crystalline lift at 3
  • the construction is DP Paso 2's with (q, N) = (3, 2): 3 | 2 + 1
  • KW I build the same order-3 type at 2 with their Theorem 5.1(4) in the proof of (D_1) (R27.5)

Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching

Commutative algebra · 2 definitions · 1 planet

R03.6Support, components and descent

Nearly faithful moduledefinitionplanetNearly faithful modules

Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is nearly faithful over R if Ann_R(M) ⊆ nilradical(R), that is, every element of R that kills M is nilpotent; equivalently √Ann_R(M) = √0. The definition carries no Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis. Characterisations, each an item of the API: (a) if Ann_R(M) is finitely generated, in particular if R is Noetherian, M is nearly faithful iff Ann_R(M) is a nilpotent ideal (Taylor's Definition 2.1); (b) if every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M), M is nearly faithful, for every M; if M is finite, M is nearly faithful iff Supp_R(M) = Spec R iff every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M) (the lemmas nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ and nearly-faithful-iff-minimal-primes-mem-support); (c) a faithful module is nearly faithful; (d) if R is reduced, M is nearly faithful iff M is faithful.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative; M an arbitrary R-module.
  • (a) needs Ann_R(M) finitely generated, which holds when R is Noetherian; without it the nilpotent form is strictly stronger (Stacks Example 0EGG).
  • (b) needs M finite for 'nearly faithful ⇒ Supp M = Spec R'; 'every minimal prime in Supp M ⇒ nearly faithful' holds for every M.
  • (d) needs R reduced.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.6/nearly-faithful

Modules supported on a union of irreducible componentsdefinition

Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is supported on components of Spec R if every prime minimal over Ann_R(M) is a minimal prime of R. For finite M this says exactly that Supp_R(M), which equals the closed set V(Ann_R M), is a union of irreducible components of Spec R, namely Supp M = ⋃_{𝔭 ∈ Min(R) ∩ Supp M} V(𝔭). The notion is used for finite modules; for a module that is not finite Supp M can differ from V(Ann M). A nearly faithful module is supported on components, all of them occurring.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative.
  • The characterisation by irreducible components needs M finite, so that Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2).

Cyclotomic completions and classical Habiro rings

Commutative algebra · 4 definitions · 10 constructions · 6 planets

HC.1The directed system and its topology

The S-cyclotomic completionconstructionplanet

For a commutative ring R and S ⊆ ℕ_{>0}, the S-cyclotomic completion R[q]^S is the ring of compatible families (x_f)_{f∈Φ*_S(R)}, x_f ∈ R[q]/(f), such that x_g maps to x_f under the canonical surjection R[q]/(g) → R[q]/(f) whenever f ∣ g; that is, R[q]^S = lim_{f∈Φ*_S} R[q]/(f) (Habiro (1.1) and (3.1)). It is an R[q]-algebra and an R-algebra. It comes with surjective projections π_f : R[q]^S → R[q]/(f), with the map ι : R[q] → R[q]^S, p ↦ (p mod f)_f, satisfying π_f ∘ ι = the quotient map, and with extensionality: x = y as soon as π_f(x) = π_f(y) for every f. Degenerate cases: R[q]^∅ = 0, because the only index is 1 and R[q]/(1) = 0, and in general the least index 1 contributes the zero ring as initial stage. The map ι is injective if and only if S ≠ ∅ or R = 0; no other injectivity is asserted here, and the injectivity of the restriction maps between completions is HC.4. For n ∈ S and R ≠ 0, Φ_n is not a unit of R[q]^S, because π_{Φ_n} sends it to 0 in the non-zero ring R[q]/(Φ_n); in particular R[q]^S is not a field, and no formal division by Φ_n exists.

Hypotheses

  • R is commutative and unital; S ⊆ ℕ_{>0} is arbitrary, possibly empty or infinite.
  • The index set is Φ*_S(R) of HC.1/the-cyclotomic-index-monoid, a set of monic polynomials directed by divisibility.
  • The only hypothesis for injectivity of ι is S ≠ ∅ (or R = 0); it is unrelated to the adjacency conditions of HC.4.

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions:HC.1/the-cyclotomic-completion

The cyclotomic index monoiddefinitionadded in review

For a commutative ring R and a set S of positive integers, the cyclotomic index monoid Φ*_S(R) is the submonoid of the multiplicative monoid of R[q] generated by the cyclotomic polynomials Φ_n(q) ∈ R[q], n ∈ S (Mathlib's cyclotomic n R, the image of the integral cyclotomic polynomial). It is a set of polynomials, not of exponent vectors: over F_2, Φ_2 = q + 1 = q − 1 = Φ_1, so Φ*_{1}(F_2) = Φ*_{2}(F_2). Its elements are monic, hence non-zero-divisors of R[q]; it is directed by divisibility (f and g divide fg); it is monotone in S; a ring map h : R → R' maps Φ*_S(R) into Φ*_S(R'); for finite S the powers (∏_{n∈S} Φ_n)^j are cofinal in it; and it has a cofinal divisibility chain g_0 ∣ g_1 ∣ ⋯, for instance g_N = ∏_{n∈S, n≤N} Φ_n^N. Its least element is the empty product 1, and Φ*_∅(R) = {1}.

Hypotheses

  • R is commutative and unital; S ⊆ ℕ_{>0} is arbitrary, possibly empty or infinite. In Lean S : Set ℕ, and 0 ∈ S is harmless because Mathlib's cyclotomic 0 R is 1.
  • Divisibility is a preorder on Φ*_S(R); nothing here needs antisymmetry.

Added during review; not yet independently checked

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions:HC.1/the-cyclotomic-index-monoid

The factorial polynomials (q; q)_Ndefinitionadded in review

For N ≥ 0 the factorial polynomial is P_N(q) = (q; q)_N = ∏_{i=1}^{N}(1 − q^i) ∈ R[q], with P_0 = 1 and P_{N+1} = P_N·(1 − q^{N+1}). Its constant term is 1 and its leading coefficient is (−1)^N. So P_N is not monic for odd N, while (−1)^N P_N = ∏_{i=1}^{N}(q^i − 1) is monic, of degree N(N+1)/2 when R ≠ 0. Grouping q^i − 1 = ∏_{d∣i} Φ_d gives (−1)^N P_N = ∏_{d=1}^{N} Φ_d^{⌊N/d⌋}, so (−1)^N P_N ∈ Φ*_{ℕ>0}(R) and P_N generates the same ideal. P_M ∣ P_N for M ≤ N, and P_N is compatible with every ring map.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative and unital; the degree formula needs R ≠ 0.
  • The polynomial P_N ∈ R[q] is named by the HC.1 stage text; the power-series q-Pochhammer symbols and q-factorials are planned in QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.0 (see restructure: PLAN-HABIRO decision D11).

Added during review; not yet independently checked

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions:HC.1/the-factorial-polynomials

The topology of the completion, its completeness and its universal propertyconstructionadded in review

Give R[q]^S the inverse-limit topology, induced from the product of the discrete rings R[q]/(f), f ∈ Φ*_S. Its open ideals f·R[q]^S = ker π_f form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0, so the topology is linear and R[q]^S is a topological ring; R[q]^S is complete and separated for it (Tau Ceti's IsCompleteSeparated), ι has dense image, and R[q]^S ≅ lim_f R[q]^S/(f). Universal property: give R[q] the linear topology whose basic open ideals are (f), f ∈ Φ*_S. For every topological commutative ring T that is complete and separated for the group uniformity of its topology, and every ring map φ : R[q] → T continuous for that topology (for every neighbourhood U of 0 there is f ∈ Φ*_S with φ((f)) ⊆ U), there is exactly one continuous ring map ψ : R[q]^S → T with ψ ∘ ι = φ. Equivalently R[q]^S is the separated completion of R[q] for the Φ*_S-topology, and the universal property is that of Mathlib's UniformSpace.Completion.

Hypotheses

  • T complete and separated for the group uniformity of its topology.
  • φ continuous for the Φ*_S-linear topology on R[q], not for an adic topology.

Added during review; not yet independently checked

Functoriality in the coefficient ring and restriction in the order setconstruction

Coefficient change: a ring map h : R → R' sends Φ_n over R to Φ_n over R' (map_cyclotomic), hence Φ*_S(R) into Φ*_S(R'), and induces a continuous ring map h^S : R[q]^S → R'[q]^S with π_{h(f)} ∘ h^S = (R[q]/(f) → R'[q]/(h(f))) ∘ π_f and h^S ∘ ι = ι ∘ h_q, and with id^S = id and (h' ∘ h)^S = h'^S ∘ h^S. Restriction: for S' ⊆ S, Φ*_{S'} ⊆ Φ*_S and the identity of R[q] induces a continuous ρ_{S,S'} : R[q]^S → R[q]^{S'} with ρ_{S,S} = id, ρ_{S',S''} ∘ ρ_{S,S'} = ρ_{S,S''} and ρ_{S,S'} ∘ ι = ι, so S ↦ R[q]^S is a presheaf of rings on the discrete set ℕ_{>0} with R[q]^∅ = 0. The two functorialities commute: h^{S'} ∘ ρ_{S,S'} = ρ_{S,S'} ∘ h^S. Injectivity and surjectivity of h^S are HC.1/coefficient-change-injective-and-surjective; injectivity of ρ is HC.4. Base change: on each finite quotient R[q]/(f) ⊗_R R' = R'[q]/(h(f)), since R[q]/(f) is free of rank deg f; but R' ⊗_R R[q]^S → R'[q]^S need not be surjective even for flat R'. For R = ℤ, R' = ℚ and S = {1}, the element exp(q − 1) = Σ_k (q − 1)^k/k! of ℚ[q]^{1} = ℚ[[q − 1]] is not of the form x/m with x ∈ ℤ[[q − 1]] and m ≥ 1.

Hypotheses

  • Ring maps are unital; restriction is along an inclusion S' ⊆ S.
  • The base-change statement is a counterexample, not an assumption; no flatness hypothesis makes this completion commute with base change.
