V.6Explicit elements and certificates

Five-term certificatedefinitionplanetA five-term certificate

For a field F, a five-term certificate is a pair (a, k) of a finitely supported function a from admissible pairs — (x, y) with x, y in F − {0, 1} and x ≠ y — to Z, and an integer k. Its evaluation is Σ a(x, y) · R(x, y) + k[1] in the free abelian group on F − {0}, where R(x, y) = [x] − [y] + [y/x] − [(1 − x^{−1})/(1 − y^{−1})] + [(1 − x)/(1 − y)] is the five-term element of V.3/five-term-relation. A certificate is valid for ξ when its evaluation equals ξ; this is a decidable equality in the free abelian group when F has decidable equality. Certificates form an abelian group under pointwise addition, and evaluation is a homomorphism. The certificate is Suslin's normalisation (K-book VI.5.1); a certificate in CGZ's normalisation over the projective line is a different object, compared through V.3/cgz-convention-comparison.

Hypotheses

  • F is a field.
  • Each pair in the list is admissible for the five-term relation.

K3BlochGroups:V.6/five-term-certificate

Bloch element constructorconstructionplanetConstructing a Bloch element from field data

Construct an element of B(F) from a finitely supported integer combination ξ of elements of F − {0} together with a proof that the boundary of the class of ξ vanishes in the antisymmetric tensor quotient ∧̃²F^×, or together with a vanishing-boundary certificate of V.6/boundary-certificate. The construction refuses input whose boundary has not been shown to vanish in ∧̃²F^×; it does not pass to the exterior square or to another quotient where the boundary happens to die. It is Suslin's convention of V.3; inputs using the symbols [0] or [∞] of CGZ's convention are not accepted.

Hypotheses

  • F is a field.
  • The input is a finitely supported integer combination of nonzero elements of F.

K3BlochGroups:V.6/bloch-element-constructor

A vanishing-boundary certificatedefinitionadded in review

Let F be a field and ξ = Σ n_x [x] a finitely supported integer combination of elements x ∈ F − {0, 1}. A vanishing-boundary certificate for ξ consists of a root of unity ζ_0 ∈ F^× with its exact order m_0 ≥ 1, elements g_1, …, g_s ∈ F^×, and for each x in the support exponent vectors e(x), f(x) ∈ Z/m_0 × Z^s with x = ζ_0^{e_0} ∏ g_j^{e_j} and 1 − x = ζ_0^{f_0} ∏ g_j^{f_j} (equalities in F). Its boundary is Σ n_x e(x) ∧ f(x) in ∧̃²(Z/m_0 × Z^s) ≅ Z/gcd(m_0, 2) ⊕ (Z/m_0)^s ⊕ (Z/2)^s ⊕ Z^{s(s−1)/2}, with components Σ n_x e_0 f_0 mod gcd(m_0, 2), Σ n_x (e_0 f_j − e_j f_0) mod m_0, Σ n_x e_j f_j mod 2 and Σ n_x (e_j f_k − e_k f_j) for j < k. The certificate is valid when all components vanish. A valid certificate proves ∂ξ = 0 in ∧̃²F^×; if ζ_0 and the g_j generate a direct summand of F^× on which they are a basis, the converse holds.

Hypotheses

  • F is a field; ξ is supported on F − {0, 1}.
  • ζ_0 has exact order m_0; the displayed factorisations hold in F.

Added during review; not yet independently checked

K3BlochGroups:V.6/boundary-certificate

Valid classes attached to a root of unityconstructionadded in review

Let ζ ∈ F be a root of unity of exact order m ≥ 2. (i) For n ≥ 1 prime to m, define ⟦ζ⟧_n ∈ B(F)/nB(F) as u · (m[ζ]) with u m ≡ 1 mod n; it does not depend on u and maps to the class of [ζ] in P(F)/nP(F). (ii) Define ⟦ζ⟧[1/m] ∈ B(F) ⊗ Z[1/m] as m^{−1} ⊗ m[ζ]; it maps to [ζ] ⊗ 1 in P(F) ⊗ Z[1/m]. (iii) For a prime p not dividing m, define the class in B(F) ⊗ Z_p in the same way. When [ζ] ∈ B(F) (V.6/root-of-unity-symbol) each class is the image of [ζ]; otherwise none is the image of an element [ζ] of B(F). These are the substitutes the consumers use in place of [ζ].

Hypotheses

  • F is a field; ζ ∈ F has exact order m ≥ 2.
  • n is prime to m, respectively p does not divide m.

Added during review; not yet independently checked

Foundations of adic spaces, Part II: analytic and formal geometry

p-adic Hodge theory and p-adic geometry · 69 definitions · 64 constructions · 26 planets

R0Morphisms and admissible affinoid products

Proper morphismdefinitionplanetProper morphism of adic spaces

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is proper if it is of +weakly finite type (quasi-compact and locally of +weakly finite type, R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally closed (R0/universally-closed-morphism) (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(ii)). Conventions: (1) the finiteness condition is '+weakly finite type', which includes quasi-compactness and the plus-ring condition O_X⁺(U) = integral closure of O_Y⁺(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)°°] for a finite E; it is neither 'locally of finite type' (Mathlib's IsProper for schemes) nor 'weakly finite type'. (2) Properness of rigid analytic varieties in Kiehl's sense (Conrad AWS, Definition 3.2.3) is a different definition; the comparison is AdicSpacesPartII:R1/proper-separated-comparisons. (3) Because separatedness (R0/separated-morphism) needs X ×_Y X to exist, the predicate is stated for X covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (automatic under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), where every adic space is locally of noetherian type).

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism

Finite morphismdefinitionplanetFinite morphism of adic spaces

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is finite if every y ∈ Y has an open affinoid neighbourhood V ⊆ Y such that f⁻¹(V) is affinoid and the induced morphism of complete Huber pairs (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(f⁻¹V), O_X⁺(f⁻¹V)) is finite (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom) (Huber 1996, 1.4.4). Huber states that then f⁻¹(V) is affinoid and finite over V for every open affinoid V ⊆ Y ([Hu4, 3.6.20, 3.12.12]); in this library that global form is proved for V = Spa(A, A⁺) with A a strongly noetherian complete Tate ring (Zavyalov, Quotients, Theorem B.2.18) and is recorded as a gap in general.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism

Étale morphismdefinitionplanetÉtale morphism of adic spaces

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is étale if it is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is bijective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Equivalently, f is smooth (R0/smooth-morphism) and unramified (R0/unramified-morphism). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism. Conventions: this is Huber's infinitesimal definition; the Kedlaya–Liu and Scholze–Weinstein definition ('locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map') agrees with it for analytic adic spaces by R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation, and the algebraic notion Algebra.Etale of Mathlib applied to coordinate rings does not (a rational embedding is étale but its ring map is not of finite type).

Hypotheses

  • f locally of finite presentation
  • lifting tested against square-zero thickenings of affinoid pre-adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale

Completed tensor productconstructionplanetThe completed tensor product of Huber pairs along adic homomorphisms

Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Pair) and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Pair.Hom) whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Choose a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and rings of definition B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺ with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀, g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ such that f(I)B₀ and g(I)C₀ are ideals of definition. Let E := B ⊗_A C (Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct, B and C being A-algebras through f and g), let F ⊆ E be the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀ (a subring), and give E the group topology for which {Iⁿ·F : n ≥ 0} is a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0, where Iⁿ·F is the additive subgroup generated by the products of images of elements of Iⁿ with elements of F. Then E is a Huber ring with pair of definition (F, I·F), the maps inl : b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and inr : c ↦ 1 ⊗ c are adic, the topology does not depend on the choice of (A₀, I, B₀, C₀), and E⁺ := the integral closure in E of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is a ring of integral elements of E. The *completed tensor product* is the complete Hausdorff Huber pair B ⊗̂_A C := (Ê, Ê⁺), where Ê is the Hausdorff completion of E (Tau Ceti IsHuberRing.completion) and Ê⁺ is the closure of the image of E⁺; it carries the morphisms of Huber pairs inl : (B, B⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, inr : (C, C⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C with inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g. It is a Tate ring whenever B or C is. Pinned conventions: B ⊗̂_A C always means this completed pair; the plus ring is the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ (not the image itself), then closed up in the completion; no uniformisation is performed; the construction is not defined unless both f and g are adic. Lean name: Huber.Pair.completedTensor f g hf hg.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) Huber pairs; B and C need not be complete.
  • f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.
  • The ring homomorphisms underlying f and g are adic.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product

The supremum seminorm of a K-affinoid algebradefinition

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one and A a K-affinoid algebra. Max A is the set of maximal ideals of A (Mathlib MaximalSpectrum A); for x ∈ Max A with ideal m_x and f ∈ A, |f(x)| is the absolute value of f mod m_x in the finite extension A/m_x of K (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite), for the unique extension of |·|. The supremum seminorm of f ∈ A is |f|_sup = sup_{x ∈ Max A} |f(x)| (and |f|_sup = 0 when A = 0). It is finite: |f|_sup ≤ |f|_π for the residue norm |f|_π = inf{‖g‖ : π(g) = f} of every presentation π : K⟨X⟩ → A (‖·‖ the Gauss norm). It is a power-multiplicative K-algebra seminorm (|f + g|_sup ≤ max(|f|_sup, |g|_sup), |fg|_sup ≤ |f|_sup|g|_sup, |λf|_sup = |λ||f|_sup for λ ∈ K, |fⁿ|_sup = |f|_supⁿ), it is contracted by every K-algebra homomorphism φ : A → B of K-affinoid algebras (|φ(f)|_sup ≤ |f|_sup), it is a norm iff A is reduced, and on a Tate algebra K⟨X⟩ it is the Gauss norm. Lean name: Huber.Affinoid.supNorm : A → ℝ≥0.

Hypotheses

  • K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one
  • A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-supremum-seminorm

Huber rings of noetherian type (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)definition

Let A be a commutative topological ring which is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti IsHuberRing A). A is *of noetherian type* if (i) A admits a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition A) whose ring of definition A₀ is a noetherian ring, or (ii) A is a Tate ring (IsTateRing A) and strongly noetherian in Tau Ceti's sense (IsStronglyNoetherian A: every completed restricted power-series ring A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩, k ≥ 0, is a noetherian ring). This is the hypothesis Huber places on affinoid rings in Theorem 2.2 and Propositions 3.6–3.8 of the 1994 paper ('has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). Conventions: the predicate concerns the topological ring only (no plus ring); completeness is not part of it, and every result that needs a complete ring assumes completeness and the Hausdorff property separately. Clause (i) does not say that A is a noetherian ring: every discrete ring is of noetherian type because its prime subring (the image of ℤ) is an open noetherian subring with ideal of definition 0. For a Tate ring clause (i) implies clause (ii) (a Tate ring with a noetherian ring of definition is strongly noetherian), so for Tate rings the predicate is exactly strong noetherianness; the converse implication fails: ℂ_p is strongly noetherian but has no noetherian ring of definition (a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ O_{ℂ_p} contains some p^N·O_{ℂ_p}, and the A₀-ideal p^N·𝔪_{ℂ_p} is not finitely generated). Lean name: Huber.IsNoetherianType A (a Prop-valued class).

Hypotheses

  • A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring and a Huber ring (IsHuberRing A).

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring

Adic homomorphisms of Huber ringsdefinition

Let A and B be Huber rings. A ring homomorphism φ : A → B is *adic* if there exist a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and a ring of definition B₀ of B such that φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and the ideal φ(I)·B₀ of B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀ (it is finitely generated, and the subspace topology of B₀ is the φ(I)B₀-adic topology); equivalently, there is a Tau Ceti pair of definition Q of B with φ(P.ringOfDefinition) ⊆ Q.ringOfDefinition and Q.idealOfDefinition equal to the ideal of Q.ringOfDefinition generated by φ(P.idealOfDefinition). Every adic homomorphism is continuous. Lean name: Huber.IsAdicHom φ (a Prop). Huber 1994 recalls this definition from his 1993 paper; Wedhorn records it as Definition 6.23.

Hypotheses

  • A, B are Huber rings (Tau Ceti IsHuberRing).
  • φ : A →+* B is a ring homomorphism.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism

Adic morphisms of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *adic* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) induced by f is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Equivalently (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus) f maps analytic points to analytic points, and then the ring maps O_Y(V) → O_X(U) are adic for all open affinoids with f(U) ⊆ V. Here a point is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U whose ring O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit; on Spa(A, A⁺) this means that its support is not open (Tau Ceti ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint). Every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic. Lean name: AdicSpace.IsAdic f (a MorphismProperty of the anchor's category).

Hypotheses

  • f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism

Morphisms locally of weakly finite type and the finite-type hierarchydefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsTopologicallyFiniteType, which is Huber 1994's and Wedhorn 6.29(i)'s notion; no condition on the plus rings); f is *of weakly finite type* if moreover f is quasi-compact. Hierarchy (Huber 1996 after 1.2.1): locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) ⇒ locally of finite type ⇒ locally of +weakly finite type (R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) ⇒ locally of weakly finite type ⇒ adic (R0/adic-morphism). Here 'locally of finite type' is the anchor's Layer 5.2 notion — the ring map (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a map of pairs, i.e. presented by a quotient mapping out of a weighted restricted power-series pair A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_M — which is exactly Huber 1994's Definition following Lemma 3.5; this node does not redefine it. Comparison with Tau Ceti: the ring-level condition is Tau Ceti's IsTopologicallyFiniteType, whose weight families satisfy IsWeightFamily, equivalent for Huber rings to Huber's 'M_i·A open' by Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1 = Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 (the anchor's Layer 0.4 equivalence), and whose completeness hypothesis on the target is automatic here since O_X(U) is complete. Lean names: AdicSpace.LocallyOfWeaklyFiniteType f, AdicSpace.IsWeaklyFiniteType f.

Hypotheses

  • f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes

Morphisms locally of +weakly finite typedefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of +weakly finite type* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsTopologicallyFiniteType) and there is a finite set E ⊆ O_X(U) (necessarily contained in O_X⁺(U)) such that O_X⁺(U) is the smallest ring of integral elements of O_X(U) containing E and the image of O_Y⁺(V), i.e. the integral closure in O_X(U) of the subring generated by the image of O_Y⁺(V), E and the topologically nilpotent elements O_X(U)°° (Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1(ii)). It is *of +weakly finite type* if moreover quasi-compact. This is the finiteness condition in Huber's definitions of proper morphisms (proper = of +weakly finite type, separated, universally closed; Huber 1996 Definition 1.3.2(ii)) and of partially proper morphisms (locally of +weakly finite type, separated, universally specializing; Definition 1.3.3(ii)). Lean names: AdicSpace.LocallyOfPlusWeaklyFiniteType f, AdicSpace.IsPlusWeaklyFiniteType f.

Hypotheses

  • f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/plus-weakly-finite-type

Morphisms locally of finite presentationdefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces is *locally of finite presentation* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that (O_Y(V), O_Y⁺(V)) → (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs (anchor Layer 5.2) and, whenever O_Y(V) carries the discrete topology, O_X(U) is a finitely presented O_Y(V)-algebra (Mathlib RingHom.FinitePresentation). This is Huber 1996 Definition 1.2.1(v) verbatim; the discrete case is the only one in which the condition adds anything. Consequences: over an analytic Y, locally of finite presentation = locally of finite type; over Y whose discrete affinoid rings are noetherian rings (for instance t(𝔜) for a locally noetherian formal scheme 𝔜) the two notions agree as well; they differ over discrete non-noetherian affinoids. Warning: unlike local finite type, local finite presentation is not stable under arbitrary base change (a non-discrete base chart imposes nothing, a discrete chart after base change does); R0/base-change-stability (iv) gives the correct hypotheses. (Huber 1996 Corollary 1.2.3(i) states unconditional stability under the book's standing hypothesis (1.1.1), which excludes such examples.) Lean name: AdicSpace.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.

Hypotheses

  • f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-finite-presentation

Locally noetherian adic spaces (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)definition

An adic space X (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *locally noetherian* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U whose complete Hausdorff ring O_X(U) is of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring): it has a noetherian ring of definition, or it is a strongly noetherian Tate ring. This is the hypothesis of Huber 1994 Propositions 3.6–3.8 ('every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood U such that O(U) has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). The condition places no restriction on plus rings. Conventions: a locally noetherian analytic adic space is one locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (the setting of Zavyalov's foundational results); because every discrete ring is of noetherian type, every discretely ringed adic space is locally noetherian in this sense, and results that need honest noetherian rings (for instance on coherent sheaves) must add that hypothesis. Lean name: AdicSpace.IsLocallyNoetherian X (a class).

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space

Closed adic subspaces cut out by ideal sheaves; closed, open and locally closed embeddingsdefinition

Let X be an adic space (the anchor's category). (1) Affinoid model: for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺) and a closed ideal J ⊆ A with A/J sheafy, the quotient pair A/J := (A/J, integral closure of the image of A⁺) (Tau Ceti Pair.quotient; Huber's (A^▷/J, (A⁺/(J ∩ A⁺))^c)) gives Spa(A/J) → Spa(A), a homeomorphism onto the closed set {v : J ⊆ supp v} (Tau Ceti Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom, range_spaComap_quotientHom). (2) An ideal sheaf 𝓘 ⊆ O_X (a sheaf of ideals of the underlying sheaf of rings) is *admissible* if X has a cover by open affinoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) such that J_U := 𝓘(U) is a closed ideal of A, A/J_U is sheafy, and for every rational W ⊆ U the ideal 𝓘(W) is the kernel of O_X(W) → O_{Spa(A/J_U)}(W ∩ V(J_U)). The *closed adic subspace* V(𝓘) is (Z, O_Z, (v_z)) with Z = {x ∈ X : 𝓘_x ≠ O_{X,x}}, O_Z = (O_X/𝓘)|_Z topologised on each such U as the structure sheaf of Spa(A/J_U) (so O_X(U) → O_Z(U ∩ Z) is continuous and open), and v_z induced through O_{X,z} → O_{X,z}/𝓘_z; it is an adic space with V(𝓘) ∩ U ≅ Spa(A/J_U) over U, and the inclusion ι : V(𝓘) → X is a morphism of adic spaces. V(𝓘) is retained as an adic space (a ringed space with valuations), never replaced by the closed subset Z. (3) A morphism h : T → X is a *closed embedding* if it is isomorphic over X to ι : V(𝓘) → X for an admissible 𝓘; an *open embedding* if it is an isomorphism onto an open subspace; a *locally closed embedding* if it factors as a closed embedding into an open subspace U ⊆ X followed by the inclusion of U. Comparison with the anchor (Layer 5.1): closed embeddings are exactly the anchor's closed immersions (affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy), with 𝓘 = ker(O_X → h_*O_T); this node adds the ideal-sheaf description, the universal property and locally closed embeddings, and does not redefine closed immersions. On a locally noetherian X every ideal of an affinoid ring of noetherian type is closed and A/J is of noetherian type, hence sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed, R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy); the identification of admissible ideals with coherent ideals is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-ideal-closed-subspace. Lean names: AdicSpace.closedSubspace 𝓘, AdicSpace.IsLocallyClosedImmersion.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space; 𝓘 an admissible ideal sheaf.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings

The norm of a Tate ring attached to a ring of definition, a pseudouniformiser and a radiusdefinition

Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti IsTateRing A). A *norm datum* d = (A₀, ϖ, r) on A consists of a ring of definition A₀ (the ringOfDefinition of a Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition A), a pseudouniformiser ϖ of A lying in A₀ (Tau Ceti IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ: a topologically nilpotent unit; A₀ contains one by Wedhorn Proposition 6.14) and a real number r with 0 < r < 1. The *norm of A attached to d* is α_d : A → ℝ≥0, α_d(x) := inf{ rⁿ : n ∈ ℤ, ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ } (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4). The exponent set is nonempty and downward closed, so α_d(x) = r^{N(x)} with N(x) = sup{ n ∈ ℤ : x ∈ ϖⁿA₀ } ∈ ℤ ∪ {+∞} (r^{+∞} := 0). Then α_d is a nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib RingSeminorm A with IsNonarchimedean), α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d(ϖx) = r·α_d(x); its closed balls are {α_d ≤ rⁿ} = ϖⁿA₀ (n ∈ ℤ), so it defines the topology of A; it vanishes exactly on the closure of {0} = ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, so it is a norm iff A is Hausdorff, and (A, α_d) is a Banach ring in Kedlaya–Liu's sense iff A is moreover complete. Pinned conventions: ϖ must lie in A₀; the function depends on d, and only its equivalence class (for fixed ϖ and r) and the topology it defines are canonical. Lean names: Huber.TateNormDatum A for d and Huber.tateNorm d for α_d.

Hypotheses

  • A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti IsTateRing).
  • A₀ is the ring of definition of a Tau Ceti PairOfDefinition A, and ϖ ∈ A₀ is a pseudouniformiser of A.
  • r is a real number with 0 < r < 1.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm

The spectral seminorm of a Tate ringdefinition

Let A be a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). The *spectral seminorm* of (A, d) is |x|_sp := lim_{n→∞} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} = inf_{n≥1} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.9; the limit exists by Fekete's lemma), which is Mathlib's smoothingSeminorm α_d (defined because α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d is nonarchimedean). It is a power-multiplicative nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib IsPowMul: |xⁿ|_sp = |x|_spⁿ for n ≥ 1) with |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x). It does not change when A₀ is replaced by another ring of definition containing ϖ (equivalent norms have the same spectral seminorm), and replacing r by r' raises it to the power log r'/log r. Intrinsic properties: |x|_sp < 1 iff x is topologically nilpotent; |x|_sp ≤ 1 for every power-bounded x; the kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0} is the ideal ⋂ₙ ϖⁿ·A°° (A°° the topologically nilpotent elements), it contains the nilradical and the closure of {0}; |1|_sp = 1 if A is Hausdorff and nonzero. Functoriality: if φ : A → B is a continuous ring homomorphism of Tate rings and B carries a datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ (such B₀ exists because φ is adic), then |φ(x)|_sp ≤ |x|_sp. Pinned convention: the Gel'fand-spectrum formula |x|_sp = max_{β ∈ M(A)} β(x) (Berkovich) is not part of this node; it is the input of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm. Lean name: Huber.spectralSeminorm d.

Hypotheses

  • A is a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm).

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm

The spectral topology of a Tate ringdefinition

Let A be a Tate ring. The *spectral topology* on A is the topology defined by a spectral seminorm |·|_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm): the ring topology whose neighbourhoods of 0 are generated by the balls {x : |x|_sp < ε}, ε > 0. For every pseudouniformiser ϖ of A the sets ϖⁿ·A°° (n ≥ 0; A°° the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for it; in particular it does not depend on the norm datum. Write A_sp for A with this topology (Lean: the type synonym Huber.SpectralTop A, with the ring equivalence toSpectralTop : A ≃+* SpectralTop A). Then: (i) the identity A → A_sp is continuous; (ii) A_sp is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ and pair of definition (A_sp,≤1, ϖ·A_sp,≤1), where A_sp,≤1 = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1}; (iii) the topologically nilpotent elements of A_sp are those of A, and A_sp° = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1} is bounded, so A_sp is uniform (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate); (iv) every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A is a ring of integral elements of A_sp, giving a Tau Ceti Pair on A_sp and a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺); (v) every continuous ring homomorphism φ : A → B of Tate rings is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp; (vi) the identity A → A_sp is a homeomorphism iff A° is bounded, i.e. iff A is uniform. Lean name: Huber.SpectralTop A.

Hypotheses

  • A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti IsTateRing).

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology

Separated morphism of adic spacesdefinition

Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces (the category of the AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5) that is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), with X covered by open affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete and stably sheafy (anchor Huber.IsStablySheafyRing; automatic if Y is so covered, Wedhorn Remark 8.55(2), and for X locally noetherian). Such an f is adic, so the fibre product X ×_Y X exists in the category of adic spaces (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b) with g = f, the second factor X being covered by stably sheafy affinoids) and the diagonal Δ_f: X → X ×_Y X is the morphism with both projections equal to the identity. The morphism f is separated if the image Δ_f(|X|) is a closed subset of the underlying space |X ×_Y X| of the adic fibre product (Huber 1996, 1.3.1). Conventions: (1) X ×_Y X is the fibre product of adic spaces, never the topological fibre product |X| ×_{|Y|} |X|; the comparison map |X ×_Y X| → |X| ×_{|Y|} |X| is surjective and in general not injective (R0/fibre-product-points). (2) Separatedness is only defined for morphisms locally of weakly finite type whose source is covered by stably sheafy affinoids; no separatedness predicate is attached to a morphism outside that class. Huber states Definition 1.3.1 without the second condition because his standing hypothesis (1.1.1) makes every adic space locally of noetherian type, hence stable (Wedhorn Corollary 8.35); without it X ×_Y X need not exist. (3) By R0/diagonal-locally-closed the diagonal is a locally closed embedding, so a separated f has Δ_f a closed embedding (closed adic subspace in the sense of R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) whenever X, Y are locally strongly noetherian analytic adic spaces and f is locally of finite type (Zavyalov, Quotients, Corollary B.7.4).

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y is a morphism of adic spaces, locally of weakly finite type
  • X is covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (so that X ×_Y X exists); automatic if Y is, and under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1)
  • Closedness is tested in the underlying topological space of the adic fibre product X ×_Y X

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism

Universally closed morphism of adic spacesdefinition

Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces that is locally of weakly finite type. The morphism f is universally closed if, for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y and every pullback square of f along g in the category of adic spaces, with base change f': X' → Y', the continuous map |f'|: |X'| → |Y'| is a closed map (Huber 1996, 1.3.2(i)). Such pullbacks exist whenever Y' is covered by open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings (R0/fibre-products-existence, case (b)), in particular always under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1); the pullback along g = id_Y always exists (X' = X), so a universally closed f has |f| closed. The condition is independent of the choice of pullback (pullbacks are unique up to unique isomorphism), so quantifying over pullback squares (the shape of Mathlib's MorphismProperty.universally) is the same as quantifying over the base changes X ×_Y Y' that exist. Conventions: base change is only taken along adic morphisms, which is the class along which Huber's fibre product (b) exists; over an analytic Y every morphism is adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), so there the condition is 'closed after every base change'.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y locally of weakly finite type
  • Test morphisms g: Y' → Y range over all adic morphisms of adic spaces, and the condition is imposed on every pullback square of f along g (such squares exist when Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids)

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-morphism

Universally specializing morphism of adic spacesdefinition

Let f: X → Y be a morphism of adic spaces. For x ∈ X, f is specializing at x if for every specialization y' of f(x) (that is, y' ∈ closure{f(x)} in |Y|) there is a specialization x' of x with f(x') = y'. If f is locally of weakly finite type, f is universally specializing at x₀ ∈ X if for every adic morphism g: Y' → Y, every pullback square of f along g in the category of adic spaces with base change f': X' → Y' and projection p: X' → X, and every point x₀' ∈ X' with p(x₀') = x₀, the base change f' is specializing at x₀'; f is universally specializing if it is so at every point (Huber 1996, Definition 1.3.3(i)). Such pullbacks exist whenever Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids (R0/fibre-products-existence (b)), in particular always under Huber's standing hypothesis (1.1.1). Convention: 'f specializing at every point' is exactly Mathlib's SpecializingMap for the continuous map |f|.

Hypotheses

  • f locally of weakly finite type for the 'universally' version
  • Base change along adic morphisms only, over every pullback square (such squares exist when Y' is covered by complete stably sheafy affinoids)

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-specializing-morphism

Partially proper morphism of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is partially proper if it is locally of +weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes), separated (R0/separated-morphism) and universally specializing (R0/universally-specializing-morphism) (Huber 1996, 1.3.3). Conventions: partial properness is a relative notion for morphisms; an open subspace U ⊆ X is partially proper over X only in special cases (the inclusion of the open unit disc into the closed disc is, the inclusion of the closed disc into P¹ is not). The Kedlaya-Liu notion of a partially proper open subset (inverse image of an open subset of the real quotient) is a different definition, compared only through its uses.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism

Valuation rings of an analytic adic space and their centresdefinition

Let X be an analytic adic space. For x ∈ X let k(x) be the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x}, k(x)⁺ ⊆ k(x) the valuation ring of the valuation v_x, and κ(x) = (k(x)^∧, k(x)⁺^∧) the completed residue affinoid field with its canonical morphism ι_x: Spa κ(x) → X (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 5; see requests). A valuation ring of X is a pair (x, A) with x ∈ X and A a valuation ring of the field k(x) such that A ⊆ k(x)⁺; X_v denotes the set of valuation rings of X (Huber 1996, 1.3.5). Since A ⊆ k(x)⁺ are valuation rings of the same field, A contains the maximal ideal of k(x)⁺, so A is open in k(x) and its closure Â in k(x)^∧ is a valuation ring making (k(x)^∧, Â) an affinoid field (Hübner, §2) with a canonical morphism j: Spa κ(x) → Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). For a morphism g: Spa κ(x) → Z to an adic space Z, a point z ∈ Z is a centre of (x, A) on Z with respect to g if there is a morphism c: Spa(k(x)^∧, Â) → Z with c ∘ j = g and c(s) = z, s the closed point of Spa(k(x)^∧, Â). A centre of (x, A) on X means a centre with respect to ι_x; for a morphism f: X → Y, a centre of (x, A) on Y means a centre with respect to f ∘ ι_x. Topology: X_v carries the topology generated by the sets D(U, h) = {(x, A) ∈ X_v : x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A} for U ⊆ X open and h ∈ O_X(U), h(x) the image of h in k(x).

Hypotheses

  • X analytic (every point analytic)
  • A ranges over valuation rings of k(x) contained in k(x)⁺ (not over all valuation rings of k(x))
  • The subbasic sets D(U, h) = {(x, A) : x ∈ U, h(x) ∈ A} are exactly Huber's (1.3.11)

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres

Finite morphism of complete Huber pairsdefinition

Let (A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) be complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff Huber rings A, B) and φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs (tauceti Huber.Pair.Hom: continuous, φ(A⁺) ⊆ B⁺). The morphism φ is finite if it is of topologically finite type as a morphism of affinoid rings (Huber 1994, §3: φ factors through a quotient mapping A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B, i.e. a surjective continuous open ring map with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring) and the ring maps A → B and A⁺ → B⁺ are integral (Huber 1996, 1.4.2). Consequences: B⁺ is the integral closure of φ(A⁺) in B (always); B is a finite A-module carrying the natural A-module topology when A is Tate (Zavyalov, Quotients, B.2.9 and B.3.4). Huber (1.4.2) states these consequences under his standing noetherian assumption (1.1.1), referring to [Hu4, 3.12.10] (unread); outside the Tate case they are not claimed here. For complete Tate pairs, φ is finite if and only if A → B is module-finite (Mathlib RingHom.Finite) and A⁺ → B⁺ is integral.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺) complete (Hausdorff) Huber pairs
  • φ a morphism of Huber pairs

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-huber-pair-hom

Locally quasi-finite and quasi-finite morphisms of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is locally quasi-finite if it is locally of weakly finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every y ∈ Y the fibre f⁻¹(y) is a discrete subspace of |X|; it is quasi-finite if moreover it is quasi-compact (Huber 1996, 1.5.1). Conventions: discreteness is of the fibre with the subspace topology of |X| (not of the fibre adic space X ×_Y Spa κ(y)); for f of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces quasi-finite is equivalent to finiteness of all fibres (R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria).

Hypotheses

  • f locally of weakly finite type

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/quasi-finite-morphism

Flat morphism of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is flat if for every x ∈ X the local homomorphism of stalks O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x} is flat (Mathlib Module.Flat) (Huber 1996, 1.7.5(b); Zavyalov, Quotients, Definition B.4.1). Stalks are colimits of rings, with no topology (AdicSpaces anchor, Layer 3.3). Conventions: flatness is stalkwise; for morphisms of strongly noetherian Tate affinoids it implies flatness of O_Y(Y) → O_X(X) (Zavyalov B.4.3), and for affinoids of topologically finite type over a nonarchimedean field the two are equivalent (Zavyalov B.4.3, B.4.6); in general the converse is not known (Zavyalov B.4.9) and is not asserted.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/flat-morphism

Unramified morphism of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is unramified if it is locally of finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is injective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism.

Hypotheses

  • f locally of finite type
  • lifting tested against all square-zero thickenings Spa(A/I) → Spa A of affinoid pre-adic spaces over Y

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/unramified-morphism

Smooth morphism of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism f: X → Y of adic spaces is smooth if it is locally of finite presentation (R0/locally-finite-presentation) and for every complete Huber pair A, every closed ideal I ⊆ A with I² = 0 and every morphism Spa A → Y, the restriction map Hom_Y(Spa A, X) → Hom_Y(Spa(A/I), X) is surjective (Huber 1996, 1.6.5). Test objects: A ranges over complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti Huber.Pair on complete Hausdorff rings), Spa A is the affinoid pre-adic space of the AdicSpaces anchor (Layer 3.4; A need not be sheafy), and morphisms Spa A → Y are morphisms of pre-adic spaces; I ⊆ A is a closed ideal with I² = 0 and A/I is the quotient Huber pair (tauceti Huber.Pair.quotient), whose plus ring is A⁺/I because I ⊆ A°° ⊆ A⁺. Huber allows non-complete affinoid rings and arbitrary square-zero I; since Spa A = Spa Â and the closure of a square-zero ideal is square-zero, restricting to complete A and closed I changes nothing. The morphism Spa(A/I) → Spa A is a homeomorphism. The relative dimension of f at x is the rank of the (locally free, R0/smooth-differentials-locally-free) module of continuous differentials near x.

Hypotheses

  • f locally of finite presentation (over an analytic Y this is the same as locally of finite type)
  • lifting tested against square-zero thickenings of affinoid pre-adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism

Morphisms of Huber pairs of algebraically finite typedefinition

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (not necessarily complete). For finite subsets M₁,…,Mₙ ⊆ A with each MᵢA open, let A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M be the polynomial ring A[X] with the subspace topology of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994, §3; for Tate A and Mᵢ = {1} the Gauss-norm topology) and plus ring the integral closure of A⁺[m·Xᵢ : m ∈ Mᵢ, 1 ≤ i ≤ n]. A morphism of Huber pairs φ: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) is of algebraically finite type if it factors through a quotient mapping A[X₁,…,Xₙ]_M → B, i.e. a surjective, continuous, open ring homomorphism with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the plus ring. This is the polynomial analogue of Huber's topologically finite type and is equivalent to Huber 1996, Definition 1.2.5(ii) (A^▷ → B^▷ adic with rings of definition A₀ → B₀ of finite type, and B⁺ the integral closure of an open subring D with A⁺ → D of algebraically finite type), by Remark 1.2.6(ii)-(iii) (choose the weights so that the images of the m·Xᵢ generate a ring of definition over A₀); it is the notion used in Corollary 1.7.3(iii); the completion of such a φ is topologically of finite type, and Spa B = Spa B̂.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) Huber pair, completeness not required
  • Mᵢ finite with MᵢA open

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/algebraically-finite-type-ring-map

The blow-up scheme Proj(⊕ Jⁿ) of a finitely generated submodule (Huber 1994 (1.1)–(1.2))construction

Let φ : C → B be a ring homomorphism, F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B a finite subset and J ⊆ B the C-submodule generated by F. Let R(J) := ⊕_{n≥0} Jⁿ·Tⁿ ⊆ B[T] (J⁰ := φ(C); for n ≥ 1, Jⁿ is the additive subgroup generated by the products j₁⋯jₙ, j_i ∈ J), an ℕ-graded ring (Mathlib GradedAlgebra) generated over R(J)₀ = φ(C) by the degree-one elements f·T, f ∈ F. Put Y := Proj R(J) with g : Y → Spec C the composite of Mathlib's Proj.toSpecZero and Spec(C → φ(C)). R(J), Y, g, the covering in (a) and the chart rings in (b) need no hypothesis on F (Huber's (1.1) allows any C-submodule J). Assume now that F generates the unit ideal of B (F·B = B). The evaluation R(J) → B, T ↦ 1, maps the irrelevant ideal onto an ideal containing F, hence onto B, and so defines s : X := Spec B → Y (Mathlib Proj.fromOfGlobalSections) with g ∘ s = Spec φ; this is Huber's diagram (1.1) in the case I := J·B = B, where X = Proj(⊕ Iⁿ) = Spec B. Properties (Huber (1.2)(i),(ii)): (a) the opens D₊(f·T), f ∈ F, cover Y and s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f), so s is affine; (b) for a nonempty S ⊆ F with product t = ∏_{f∈S} f, the open U = D₊(t·T^{|S|}) is affine with O_Y(U) = C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S] ⊆ B_t (the φ(C)-subalgebra of the localisation B_t generated by these fractions) and O_X(s⁻¹U) = B_t; (c) g is projective, hence proper and separated, and Y is noetherian when C is. Lean name: AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup φ F.

Hypotheses

  • C, B commutative rings, φ : C → B a ring homomorphism.
  • F ⊆ B finite; J the C-submodule generated by F (no further hypothesis for R(J), Y, g, the covering {D₊(f·T)}, the chart rings and (c)).
  • F·B = B, for the morphism s and every statement involving it (s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f), s affine, g ∘ s = Spec φ, O_X(s⁻¹U) = B_t).

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up

The uniformization of a Tate Huber pairconstruction

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (Tau Ceti Pair) with A a Tate ring. Its *uniformization* is the Huber pair (A^u, A^{u+}) where A^u is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp = Huber.SpectralTop A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology; Tau Ceti IsHuberRing.completion, IsTateRing.completion), i.e. the separated completion of A for its spectral seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13), and A^{u+} is the closure of the image of A⁺ in A^u. It comes with the morphism of Huber pairs ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}), the composite of the continuous identity A → A_sp and the completion map. Properties: (a) (A^u, A^{u+}) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair, A^u is a Tate ring, and A^u is uniform (A^{u°} is bounded; the continuous extension of |·|_sp to A^u is a power-multiplicative norm defining its topology); (b) ι has dense image and kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0}; (c) for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded and every morphism of Huber pairs φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is exactly one morphism φ^u : (A^u, A^{u+}) → (B, B⁺) with φ^u ∘ ι = φ, so uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs into Tate Huber pairs; (d) Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond to rational subsets; (e) if A is complete, Hausdorff and uniform, ι is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: morphisms are Tau Ceti Pair.Hom (continuous, plus rings respected), which for Banach rings are the bounded morphisms (Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 2.11); the plus ring is the closure of the image of A⁺, not the image. Lean name: Huber.Pair.uniformization.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and A is a Tate ring.
  • For the universal property: (B, B⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with B° bounded.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization

The uniform completed tensor product of Tate Huber pairsconstruction

Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A a Tate ring, and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti Pair.Hom; f and g are adic and B, C are Tate by Wedhorn Proposition 6.25). The *uniform completed tensor product* is B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C := (B ⊗̂_A C)^u, the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), with inlᵘ := ι ∘ inl and inrᵘ := ι ∘ inr. Properties: (a) it is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pair and inlᵘ ∘ f = inrᵘ ∘ g; (b) it is a pushout of (f, g) in the category of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs: for every such (R, R⁺) and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g there is exactly one morphism χ : B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C → (R, R⁺) with χ ∘ inlᵘ = φ and χ ∘ inrᵘ = ψ; (c) the canonical morphism ι : B ⊗̂_A C → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C induces a homeomorphism of adic spectra identifying rational subsets; (d) ι is an isomorphism iff B ⊗̂_A C is uniform (for instance K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ = K⟨T, S⟩), and it is not an isomorphism in general: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5). No sheafiness of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C and no fibre-product property of its Spa is claimed. Lean name: Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor f g.

Hypotheses

  • (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, A a Tate ring.
  • f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product

Completed tensor products of Banach modules over complete Tate ringsconstruction

Let A be a complete Tate ring (Tau Ceti IsTateRing, complete and Hausdorff) with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm); for instance A = L a complete nonarchimedean field with its absolute value. A Banach A-module is a complete Hausdorff topological A-module V whose topology is defined by an additive subgroup V₀ stable under A₀ with V = ⋃ₙ ϖ⁻ⁿV₀, the ϖⁿV₀ forming a basis of neighbourhoods of 0; equivalently, an A-module complete for a norm |·| with |av| ≤ c·α_d(a)·|v| (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.2.7), a lattice being the A₀-submodule generated by {|·| ≤ 1} (which is {|·| ≤ 1} itself when c ≤ 1). For Banach A-modules V, W the completed tensor product V ⊗̂_A W is the Hausdorff completion of V ⊗_A W for the tensor topology, in which the images of ϖⁿ·(V₀ ⊗_{A₀} W₀), n ≥ 0, form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0. Equivalently it is the completion for the product seminorm |x| = inf max_i |v_i|·|w_i| over presentations x = Σ v_i ⊗ w_i (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.10, stated there for rings). It is a Banach A-module whose lattice is the closure of the image of V₀ ⊗ W₀; up to equivalence of norms it does not depend on the lattices. (a) Universal property: (v, w) ↦ v ⊗ w is a continuous A-bilinear map whose image spans a dense submodule. Every continuous A-bilinear map β: V × W → M into a complete Hausdorff topological A-module M whose topology has a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 consisting of A₀-submodules (for instance a Banach A-module with lattice M₀, for which continuity of β is equivalent to boundedness: β(V₀ × W₀) ⊆ ϖ⁻ᵏM₀ for some k) factors uniquely as β = β̂ ∘ ⊗ with β̂: V ⊗̂_A W → M continuous and A-linear. (b) Functoriality: continuous A-linear f: V → V' and g: W → W' induce f ⊗̂ g, compatibly with identities and composition, and A ⊗̂_A V ≅ V. (c) Compatibility: if V = B and W = C are complete Huber A-algebras (adic structure maps; B₀, C₀ rings of definition containing the images of A₀), then V ⊗̂_A W is B ⊗̂_A C of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product as a topological A-module, and its multiplication is the continuous extension of that of B ⊗_A C. (d) Exactness: − ⊗̂_A W carries a topologically split short exact sequence of Banach A-modules (continuous maps with a continuous retraction and a continuous section) to a topologically split short exact sequence. The field statements of Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.9 (injectivity of V ⊗_L W → V ⊗̂_L W, the cross-norm property, kernels and strictness of f ⊗̂ X) are not part of this node: they are AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness, which is proved from (f) and the existence of t-orthogonal bases (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis). (e) Finite projective modules: for a finite projective A-module P with its natural topology (a finite Banach module, Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12), P ⊗_A W → P ⊗̂_A W is an isomorphism. (f) Orthonormal bases: let A = L be a complete nonarchimedean field and let V have an orthonormal basis (e_i)_{i∈I}: every v ∈ V is uniquely Σ c_i e_i with c_i → 0 along the cofinite filter, and |v| = max |c_i|. Then for every Banach L-module E, E ⊗̂_L V ≅ c₀(I, E), the Banach module of I-indexed families in E tending to 0 with the supremum norm, via x ⊗ Σ c_i e_i ↦ (c_i x)_i, isometrically. If (e_i) is only t-orthogonal for some 0 < t ≤ 1 (t·max|c_i| ≤ |Σ c_i e_i| ≤ max|c_i|), the same map is a topological isomorphism with t·|·|_sup ≤ |·| ≤ |·|_sup. (g) Base change: for a continuous homomorphism A → A' of complete Tate rings, A' ⊗̂_A V is a Banach A'-module, and A'' ⊗̂_{A'} (A' ⊗̂_A V) ≅ A'' ⊗̂_A V for A → A' → A''. In particular M ⊗̂_A A⟨T/s⟩ is defined for a Banach A-module M and a rational localisation A → A⟨T/s⟩; it equals M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩ when M is finite projective (e) or finite over a strongly noetherian A (Huber 1994 Lemma 2.4(ii)). Conventions: the orthonormal description uses null families (c₀), not bounded families: E ⊗̂_L c₀(I, L) = c₀(I, E), whereas the mixed completed tensor product of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor with the profinite flat module ∏_I O gives bounded families. The existence of orthonormal or t-orthogonal bases, for instance for Banach spaces of countable type (Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert 2.7.2/3, cited by Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 7.8), is a hypothesis of (f); it is proved in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-countable-type-orthogonal-basis.

Hypotheses

  • A complete Hausdorff Tate ring with a norm datum (R0/tate-ring-norm); for (f), A = L a complete nonarchimedean field
  • V, W Banach A-modules; for (a), M a complete Hausdorff topological A-module with a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 consisting of A₀-submodules (e.g. a Banach A-module)
  • For (f): an orthonormal, or t-orthogonal, basis of V

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module

The Huber pair of a finite algebra over a noetherian affinoid ringconstruction

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Huber pair such that A is a complete noetherian Tate ring or has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance A strongly noetherian Tate, or an affinoid algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field). Let ψ: A → C be a finite A-algebra (C commutative and finitely generated as an A-module). Equip C with the natural A-module topology (the finest topology making C a topological A-module; Mathlib moduleTopology A C; Huber 1994, p. 524) and let C⁺ be the integral closure of ψ(A⁺) in C. Then: (i) C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring, Tate if A is, every A-submodule of C is closed, and ψ is continuous; (ii) C⁺ is a ring of integral elements, so Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra (C, C⁺) is a complete Huber pair; (iii) ψ is a finite morphism of Huber pairs (R0/finite-huber-pair-hom); (iv) universal property: for every complete Huber pair (D, D⁺) with a morphism χ: (A, A⁺) → (D, D⁺), morphisms of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (D, D⁺) under (A, A⁺) are exactly the A-algebra maps C → D; (v) if A is strongly noetherian Tate, so is C; (vi) Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a finite morphism of adic spaces, and for A strongly noetherian Tate every finite morphism X → Spa(A, A⁺) is isomorphic over Spa(A, A⁺) to one of this form, with C = O_X(X). Convention: the noetherian hypothesis is part of the construction; for a non-noetherian complete Tate ring A a finite A-algebra C = A/J with J not closed has a non-Hausdorff natural topology, so no complete Huber pair structure exists on C itself.

Hypotheses

  • A complete noetherian Tate ring, or A with a noetherian ring of definition
  • C finite A-algebra; natural A-module topology; C⁺ = integral closure of ψ(A⁺)

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-over-affinoid

Module of continuous differentials of a topologically finite type mapconstruction

Let φ: A → B be a continuous homomorphism of complete Huber rings (complete Hausdorff f-adic rings) which is topologically of finite type (tauceti TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType), with A of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring: a noetherian ring of definition, or strongly noetherian Tate — Huber's standing assumption (1.1.1)); then B and B ⊗̂_A B are of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type, R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability), their ideals are closed and finite modules with the natural topology are complete and Hausdorff. Let m: B ⊗̂_A B → B be the continuous extension of b ⊗ b' ↦ bb' to the completed tensor product (R0/completed-tensor-product) and I = ker m. The module of continuous differentials is Ωᶜ_{B/A} := I/I², a B-module via (B ⊗̂_A B)/I ≅ B, with the natural B-module topology, and d = d_{B/A}: B → Ωᶜ_{B/A}, d(b) = class of 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 (Huber 1996, (1.6.2)). Properties: (a) for every finite N ⊆ B with A[N] dense in B, I is generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 (n ∈ N); hence Ωᶜ_{B/A} is a finitely generated B-module generated by d(N). (b) d is a continuous A-derivation and is universal: for every complete Hausdorff topological B-module M and every continuous A-derivation D: B → M there is a unique continuous B-linear u: Ωᶜ_{B/A} → M with u ∘ d = D. (c) If A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_M → B is a quotient mapping with kernel 𝔞, then Ωᶜ_{B/A} ≅ (⊕ᵢ B dXᵢ)/(B-span of Σᵢ (∂P/∂Xᵢ) dXᵢ, P ∈ 𝔞), where ∂/∂Xᵢ are the termwise partial derivatives (which preserve A⟨X⟩_M); in particular Ωᶜ_{A⟨X⟩_M/A} is free with basis dX₁,…,dXₙ. (d) If B is a finite A-module, the canonical B-linear map Ω[B⁄A] → Ωᶜ_{B/A} from Mathlib's KaehlerDifferential (induced by d) is an isomorphism. Under this hypothesis Ωᶜ_{B/A} is complete and Hausdorff; without it (non-noetherian A) the ideal generated by the 1 ⊗ n − n ⊗ 1 need not be closed and none of (a)-(d) is asserted. The coherent sheaf Ω¹_{X/Y} on a locally noetherian analytic adic space is glued from these modules by the localisation compatibility (API localizationEquiv); it is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials.

Hypotheses

  • A → B continuous, topologically of finite type, between complete Huber rings
  • A of noetherian type (Huber's standing assumption); hence B, B ⊗̂_A B of noetherian type
  • M ranges over complete Hausdorff topological B-modules in the universal property

AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials

R1Analytification and algebraic correspondences

Fibre product with a schemeconstructionplanetHuber's fibre product X ×_Y S of a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space over a scheme

Let f: X → Y be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, S an adic space satisfying Huber's condition (every point has an open affinoid neighbourhood Spa(A, A⁺) with A having a noetherian ring of definition or A a strongly noetherian Tate ring; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space), and g: S_ → Y a morphism of locally ringed spaces, where S_ = (|S|, O_S) is the underlying locally ringed space of S (forgetting the topology of O_S and the valuations). Then there are an adic space R = X ×_Y S, a morphism of adic spaces p: R → S and a morphism of locally ringed spaces q: R_ → X with g ∘ p_ = f ∘ q, such that for every adic space U, every morphism of adic spaces u: U → S and every morphism of locally ringed spaces v: U_ → X with g ∘ u_ = f ∘ v there is a unique morphism of adic spaces w: U → R with p ∘ w = u and q ∘ w_ = v. The morphism p is locally of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and R satisfies Huber's condition. Over an affine open Spec B ⊆ Y, an affine open Spec C ⊆ f⁻¹(Spec B) with C = B[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I and an open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ g⁻¹(Spec B), the open subspace p⁻¹(Spa(A,A⁺)) ∩ q⁻¹(Spec C) of R is the increasing union ⋃_k Spa(A_k, A_k⁺) of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affine-chart-analytification. A Y-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ of Y-schemes locally of finite type induces h_S: X₁ ×_Y S → X₂ ×_Y S; this is functorial, and the triple (R, p, q) is unique up to unique isomorphism, so the construction is independent of the charts, presentations and sets E chosen.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y a morphism of schemes, locally of finite type
  • S satisfies Huber's condition (Huber 1994 3.8); Wedhorn 8.61 and Hübner 10.2 give the same construction for stable (stably sheafy) adic spaces S
  • g: S_ → Y is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; no topology on O_Y enters

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification

AnalytificationconstructionplanetThe adic analytification X ↦ X^ad = X ×_{Spec K} Spa(K, K°) of schemes locally of finite type over K

Fix a field K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, its valuation ring K° = {|x| ≤ 1}, a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (0 < |ϖ| < 1), and Spa K := Spa(K, K°), a one-point adic space. The identity of K defines a morphism of locally ringed spaces c_K: (Spa K)_ → Spec K. For a scheme X locally of finite type over K, its analytification is X^ad := X ×_{Spec K} Spa K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification), an adic space locally of finite type over Spa K, with the morphism of locally ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X lying over c_K; a K-morphism h: X₁ → X₂ gives h^ad := h_{Spa K}. This defines a functor (·)^ad: Sch^{lft}_K → Adic^{lft}_K from K-schemes locally of finite type to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, and q is a natural transformation (·)^ad_ → (·) of functors to locally ringed spaces over Spec K. For X = Spec K[T₁,…,Tₙ]/I, X^ad = ⋃_{k≥0} Spa(A_k, A_k°) with A_k = K⟨ϖ^k T₁,…,ϖ^k Tₙ⟩/I·K⟨ϖ^k T⟩ (functions on the closed polydisc of radius |ϖ|^{-k} modulo I), glued along the rational embeddings Spa(A_k, A_k°) = {|ϖ^k Tᵢ| ≤ 1 for all i} ⊆ Spa(A_h, A_h°) for k ≤ h; the plus ring of each chart is its power-bounded subring (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded). The result does not depend on ϖ or on the presentation, up to unique isomorphism over Spa K compatible with q.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially valued, rank one; the construction itself only uses that K is a complete Tate field that is strongly noetherian, which the anchor's Layer 0.5 proves for complete rank-one fields (BGR 5.2.6)
  • X locally of finite type over K, with no separatedness or quasi-compactness assumption

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor

Rigid–adic comparisonconstructionplanetHuber's functor r_K from rigid-analytic spaces to adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)

Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. There is a functor r_K: Rig_K → Adic^{lft}_K together with, for each rigid space X, a morphism of ringed sites ρ_X: (|r_K(X)|, O_{r_K(X)}) → (X, O_X) over Sp K = Spa K (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.3) such that r_K(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), ρ_X is locally coherent, and (r_K(X), ρ_X) is final: for every adic space Z locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) and every locally coherent morphism of ringed sites λ: (|Z|, O_Z) → (X, O_X) over Sp K there is a unique morphism f: Z → r_K(X) over Spa K with ρ_X ∘ f = λ. Moreover (Huber 1996 (1.1.11) and (1.4.1)): (a) r_K(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°) and r_K of a morphism of affinoids is induced by the K-algebra map; (b) r_K carries open immersions to open embeddings and r_K(U ∩ V) = r_K(U) ∩ r_K(V); (c) a family of admissible opens is an admissible covering iff the r_K(U_i) cover r_K(X); (d) the points of X correspond bijectively to the classical points of r_K(X) (points x with k(x) finite over K), with r_K(U) ∩ X = U for admissible U; if X is quasi-separated, U ↦ r_K(U) is a bijection from the quasi-compact admissible opens of X onto the quasi-compact opens of r_K(X), under which affinoid opens correspond to affinoid opens; (e) r_K commutes with fibre products; (f) a morphism f of rigid spaces is a closed immersion iff r_K(f) is a closed embedding (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings).

Hypotheses

  • K complete of rank one (Huber 1994 §4 hypothesis)
  • rigid-analytic varieties in the sense of BGR 9.3.1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space)

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor

Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a K-affinoid algebradefinition

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one, A a K-affinoid algebra and X = Max A. A subset U ⊆ X is an affinoid subdomain if there is a homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras i : A → A_U such that Max(i) : Max A_U → X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite) has image in U and is universal for this property: for every homomorphism φ : A → B into a K-affinoid algebra with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ U there is a unique K-algebra homomorphism φ_U : A_U → B with φ_U ∘ i = φ. The A-algebra A_U (the coordinate ring of U) is unique up to unique A-isomorphism; Max(i) is a bijection onto U inducing isomorphisms of residue fields; for affinoid subdomains V ⊆ U there is a unique A-algebra map ρ^U_V : A_U → A_V, with ρ^V_W ∘ ρ^U_V = ρ^U_W. Rational subdomains X(f₁,…,f_n/f₀) = {x : |f_j(x)| ≤ |f₀(x)| for all j}, for f₀,…,f_n ∈ A without common zero, are affinoid subdomains with coordinate ring A⟨f/f₀⟩ = A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩/(f₀T_j − f_j) (Weierstrass domains f₀ = 1, Laurent domains as intersections). Lean name: RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain A U, with coordinate ring RigidSpace.IsAffinoidSubdomain.coordRing.

Hypotheses

  • K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| of rank one
  • A is a K-affinoid algebra: a commutative K-algebra with a complete Hausdorff first-countable ring topology for which K → A is strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType (algebraMap K A): a continuous open surjection of K-algebras K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ = restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n K → A; Wedhorn Definition 5.57)

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain

Rigid-analytic spaces over K in the sense of Tate (BGR 9.3.1)definition

Let K be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field. For a K-affinoid algebra A (a quotient of some Tate algebra K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩, with its Banach topology), the affinoid space Sp(A) is the set Max A of maximal ideals with the Tate (strong) G-topology: a subset U ⊆ Max A is admissible open if it has a set-theoretic covering {U_i} by affinoid subdomains such that for every homomorphism of K-affinoid algebras φ : A → B with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ U finitely many U_i cover Max(φ)(Max B), and a family {V_j} of admissible opens is an admissible covering of its union V if for every φ : A → B with Max(φ)(Max B) ⊆ V the covering {Max(φ)⁻¹(V_j)} of Max B has a refinement by finitely many affinoid subdomains (Conrad AWS Definition 2.2.6; BGR 9.1.4); together with Tate's structure sheaf O_A, U ↦ A_U on affinoid subdomains. A rigid-analytic space over K is a pair (X, O_X) of a G-topologized set X and a sheaf of K-algebras O_X with local stalks, admitting an admissible covering by open subspaces isomorphic to affinoid spaces Sp(A_i). Morphisms are morphisms of locally G-ringed K-spaces. Rig_K denotes this category. A morphism f is a closed immersion if there is an admissible affinoid covering {U_i} of the target with each f⁻¹(U_i) affinoid and O(U_i) → O(f⁻¹U_i) surjective (Conrad AWS Example 3.1.5); f is separated if its diagonal is a closed immersion, quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact, and proper (Kiehl) if it is separated, quasi-compact and relatively compact over an admissible affinoid covering of the target (Conrad AWS Definition 3.2.3).

Hypotheses

  • K complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value
  • K-affinoid algebras are strongly noetherian Tate rings (anchor Layer 0.5), so Tate's acyclicity for finite rational coverings is the anchor's Layer 4; the extension to finite coverings by affinoid subdomains uses the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem, whose proof (BGR 7.3.5) is not in a public source read here

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space

Analytification of O_X-modules F ↦ F^ad = q_X^*F, its exactness, and analytified ideal sheavesconstruction

For a K-scheme X locally of finite type and an O_X-module F, put F^ad := q_X^*F = O_{X^ad} ⊗_{q_X⁻¹O_X} q_X⁻¹F, the pullback of sheaves of modules along the morphism of ringed spaces q_X: X^ad_ → X (mathlib:SheafOfModules.pullback for the continuous functor of opens V ↦ q_X⁻¹(V) and the ring map q_X^♯; O_{X^ad} regarded as a sheaf of rings). Then F ↦ F^ad is an exact functor O_X-Mod → O_{X^ad}-Mod with stalks (F^ad)_x ≅ O_{X^ad,x} ⊗_{O_{X,q(x)}} F_{q(x)}; it commutes with tensor products (the sheafified tensor product of sheaves of modules — Mathlib has the monoidal structure only on presheaves of modules, so this is built here) and with pullback along analytified morphisms ((h^*G)^ad ≅ (h^ad)^*G^ad), (O_X)^ad = O_{X^ad}, and for a quasi-coherent ideal I ⊆ O_X the map I^ad → O_{X^ad} is injective with image the ideal sheaf I·O_{X^ad} of the closed adic subspace V(I)^ad (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-immersions). The same holds relatively for the analytification X ×_{Spec A} S → X of a scheme X locally of finite type over Spec A, with S = Spa(A, A⁺) a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid (Zavyalov §6). It does not hold for X ×_Y S → X with an arbitrary scheme Y and morphism S → Y, whose projection need not be flat (Y = X = A¹_K and S = Spa K mapping to the origin: the projection is the inclusion of a point and q^* is not exact).

Hypotheses

  • X locally of finite type over K; F an arbitrary O_X-module (exactness uses flatness of q_X only)
  • coherence of F^ad for coherent F uses the coherent-sheaf notion of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf and is proved there

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules

Rigid analytification X ↦ X^an of schemes locally of finite type over Kconstruction

For a K-scheme X locally of finite type there is a rigid-analytic space X^an with a morphism of locally G-ringed K-spaces i_X: X^an → X that is final among rigid spaces over K with such a morphism: for every rigid space Y over K, composition with i_X is a bijection Hom_{Rig_K}(Y, X^an) → Hom_K(Y, X). X ↦ X^an is a functor; A^{n,an} is the union of the closed polydiscs of radius |c|^{-j} (0 < |c| < 1); for affine X = V(I) ⊆ A^n, X^an is the closed analytic subspace of A^{n,an} cut out by I; and i_X is a bijection onto the closed points of X; for a Zariski-open U ⊆ X the analytification of the open immersion U → X is an isomorphism of U^an onto the admissible open i_X⁻¹(U) of X^an; and for morphisms X → Z, Y → Z of K-schemes locally of finite type the canonical map (X ×_Z Y)^an → X^an ×_{Z^an} Y^an is an isomorphism.

Hypotheses

  • K complete of rank one; X locally of finite type over K

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification

Analytic groups: analytification of group schemes, finite locally free group schemes, abelian varieties and isogeniesconstruction

Let Sch^{lft}_K be the category of K-schemes locally of finite type (a full subcategory of Over(Spec K) closed under finite products, with its cartesian monoidal structure) and Adic^{lft}_K the category of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K = Spa(K, K°), which has finite products X ×_{Spa K} Y (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) and terminal object Spa K. Because (·)^ad preserves finite products (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-fibre-products), it is a monoidal functor and carries group objects to group objects: a group scheme (G, m, e, i) locally of finite type over K gives the analytic group G^ad with multiplication m^ad, unit e^ad: Spa K → G^ad and inverse i^ad, and a homomorphism φ gives the homomorphism φ^ad; commutative group schemes give commutative group objects. Relatively, for a group scheme G → Y locally of finite type and S → Y as in AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification, G ×_Y S is a group object over S. Properties: (a) for an affinoid Spa(D, D⁺) over Spa K, the group of its points in G^ad is G(D); (b) if G is finite locally free of rank d over Y then G^ad → Y^ad is finite, with O over each affinoid finite projective of rank d; (c) if A is an abelian variety over K then A^ad is a commutative analytic group that is proper, smooth of dimension dim A and connected over Spa K; (d) if φ: A → B is an isogeny (a finite surjective homomorphism) then φ^ad is a finite surjective homomorphism whose kernel A^ad ×_{B^ad, e^ad} Spa K is (ker φ)^ad, a finite analytic group.

Hypotheses

  • K complete of rank one; group schemes locally of finite type over K (resp. over Y)
  • the target category is adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa K, where finite products exist

AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-group-objects

R2Formal schemes, generic fibres, and Hasse domains

Admissible formal schemedefinitionplanetAdmissible formal O_K-schemes (formal schemes locally topologically of finite presentation without ϖ-torsion)

A formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation is a formal scheme X of finite ideal type in the sense of F0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme: locally Spf A with A an adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition) with a morphism to Spf O_K, that is covered by open formal subschemes isomorphic to Spf A with A a tfp O_K-algebra carrying the ϖ-adic topology; equivalently ϖO_X is an ideal of definition and each X_m = X ⊗_{O_K} O_K/ϖ^{m+1} is a scheme locally of finite presentation over O_K/ϖ^{m+1}. X is admissible if moreover O_X has no ϖ-torsion; by node tfp-locality this holds iff every (equivalently: some covering family of) formal affine open Spf A has A admissible, iff every local ring O_{X,x} is O_K-flat. Morphisms are morphisms of formal O_K-schemes; they are automatically adic. The special fibre is X_s = X ⊗_{O_K} k; the underlying topological spaces of X, X_0 and X_s coincide and are locally noetherian (noetherian when X is quasi-compact) although O_X need not be noetherian. The category of admissible formal O_K-schemes has fibre products: the formal fibre product X ×_Z Y divided by its ϖ-torsion ideal (which is zero if X or Y is flat over Z). A coherent open ideal on X is a coherent ideal sheaf 𝒜 ⊆ O_X which locally on X contains ϖ^m O_X for some m (a single m works when X is quasi-compact). When K is discretely valued, admissible formal O_K-schemes are exactly the locally noetherian formal schemes flat and adic locally of finite type over Spf O_K (F0's notions).

Hypotheses

  • K complete with nontrivial rank-one valuation; O_K possibly non-noetherian
  • Admissible is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's notion (tfp + ϖ-torsion-free), distinct from EGA's 'admissible ring'
  • Formal schemes are F0's formal schemes of finite ideal type; being locally tfp or admissible is a condition on them, not a new category of spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-formal-scheme

Generic fibreconstructionplanetHuber's analytic adic space d(X) of a formal scheme of type (S)

Proposition 1.9.1: for X of type (S) there are an adic space d(X) and a morphism of topologically ringed spaces λ = λ_X: d(X) → X such that (a) d(X) is analytic: for the ideal sheaf I ⊆ O_X of sections vanishing at every point, λ⁻¹(I)·O_{d(X)} = O_{d(X)}; (b) O_X → λ_* O_{d(X)} factors through λ_* O⁺_{d(X)} and λ: (d(X), O⁺_{d(X)}) → (X, O_X) is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; (c) (d(X), λ) is universal among adic spaces with a morphism to X satisfying (a) and (b). Hence d is a functor from type-(S) formal schemes with adic morphisms to analytic adic spaces, and λ is natural. Affine formulas: for X = Spf A with A noetherian, d(X) = t(X)_a with the restriction of π_X (node noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space); in case (b), with B the integral closure of (the image of) A in A(1/s), d(X) = Spa(A(1/s), B) and λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}. For X locally tfp over O_K (in particular admissible), d(Spf A) = Spa(A[1/ϖ], B); when K is discretely valued (so X is locally noetherian and t(X) is defined) d(X) is the open locus {|ϖ| ≠ 0} of t(X) over Spa(O_K, O_K) (Hübner §8), while for non-discrete K no adic space t(X) is available and only the affine formula is used; d(X) = d(X^{tf}) so ϖ-torsion is invisible. Open formal subschemes U ⊆ X give open subspaces d(U) = λ⁻¹(U), and for every affine U satisfying (S), d(U) is spectral (1.9.3).

Hypotheses

  • X of type (S); morphisms adic
  • Case (a) of the construction uses Huber 1994 §4 (node noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space); d(Spf A) in case (b) is an adic space because A(1/s) is strongly noetherian Tate (anchor Layer 4)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d

Admissible blow-upconstructionplanetAdmissible formal blow-ups and strict transforms

Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent open ideal (coherent, and locally ϖ^N O_X ⊆ 𝒜 for some N; a single N when X is quasi-compact). The admissible blow-up of 𝒜 is X' := lim_m Proj(⊕_{n≥0} 𝒜ⁿ ⊗_{O_X} O_X/ϖ^{m+1}) with its projection φ: X' → X. (a) Over a formal affine open Spf A with 𝒜 ↔ a = (f_0, …, f_r) ∋ ϖ^N, φ⁻¹(Spf A) is the ϖ-adic completion of the scheme-theoretic blow-up of a on Spec A, covered by the charts Spf A'_i with A'_i = A⟨ζ_j : j ≠ i⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)_{j≠i} modulo its ϖ-torsion (which equals its f_i-torsion), Spf A'_i being the locus where f_i generates 𝒜O_{X'}. (b) X' is admissible and 𝒜O_{X'} is invertible. (c) Universal property: every morphism ψ: Z → X of formal O_K-schemes (Z not necessarily admissible) with 𝒜O_Z invertible factors uniquely through φ. Further: φ is an isomorphism over X ∖ V(𝒜); formation commutes with flat base change and, in the admissible category, with arbitrary base change (strict transform); φ is proper and surjective on special fibres; blowing up 𝒜 and then ℬO_{X'} is blowing up 𝒜ℬ; for X quasi-compact a composite of admissible blow-ups is an admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 2.5), blow-ups of finitely many opens extend to X and are dominated by one admissible blow-up of X (2.6), and any two admissible blow-ups of X are dominated by a third, so admissible blow-ups of X form a cofiltered system. The strict transform of a coherent O_X-module ℳ is ℳ' = φ*ℳ/𝒩, where 𝒩 is the 𝒜O_{X'}-power torsion of φ*ℳ (sections killed locally by a power of 𝒜O_{X'}; the scheme-theoretic 'sections supported in φ⁻¹(V(𝒜))' of Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.1, V(𝒜) being read scheme-theoretically since the underlying space of X' is its special fibre); 𝒩 lies in the ϖ-power torsion, and if ℳ' has no ϖ-torsion, 𝒩 is the ϖ-power torsion of φ*ℳ, which is coherent (Lemma 1.4(c)).

Hypotheses

  • X admissible over O_K; X quasi-compact for composition (2.5) and extension (2.6)
  • 𝒜 coherent and open; a non-open centre changes the generic fibre
  • Composition 2.5 uses [RG, 5.1.4] and [EGA I_new 6.9.9]; extension 2.6 uses [EGA I_new 6.9.7]

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up

ε-ordinary locusconstructionplanetHasse domains X(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε} and their formal models

Let p be a prime, K a complete extension of Q_p (|p| = p⁻¹), 𝔛 an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ω an invertible O_𝔛-module, and Ha ∈ Γ(𝔛 ⊗_{O_K} O_K/p, ω^{⊗(p−1)}) a section (the Hasse invariant; for modular curves and Shimura varieties it is supplied by the moduli roadmaps). For ε ∈ ℚ with 0 ≤ ε < 1 the Hasse domain is X(ε) := 𝔛_η(|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε) ⊆ d(𝔛), the section domain (node section-valuation-domain) of any local lift H̃a of Ha to ω^{⊗(p−1)}, with the fractional convention of node fractional-valuation-bound; it is well defined because two lifts differ by p·(section) and |p| < |p|^ε for ε < 1. If O_K contains an element p^ε of p-adic valuation ε (an explicitly chosen element; for instance the completion of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}) contains such elements for every ε ∈ (1/(p−1))·ℤ[1/p]), the formal model 𝔛(ε) := 𝔛(|H̃a| ≥ |p^ε|) (node section-domain-formal-model) is independent of the local lift up to canonical isomorphism — equivalently it represents, on p-adically complete flat O_K-algebras S, pairs (g: Spf S → 𝔛, u ∈ Γ(Spf S, g*ω^{⊗(1−p)})) with u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε in S/p, modulo u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h) — and d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε). X(0) = {|Ha| = 1} is the tube of the ordinary locus 𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha). Formation of X(ε) and 𝔛(ε) commutes with pull-back along morphisms 𝔜 → 𝔛 (with the pulled-back ω and Ha) and with base change along complete extensions of K.

Hypotheses

  • K complete over Q_p; 𝔛 admissible over O_K; ω invertible; Ha a section of ω^{⊗(p−1)} modulo p
  • 0 ≤ ε < 1 (for ε = 1 the domain depends on the lift)
  • The formal model needs an element p^ε ∈ O_K; otherwise use the fractional-bound domain on the generic fibre or pass to an explicit extension

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-domain

Algebras topologically of finite type and of finite presentation over a complete rank-one valuation ring; admissible algebrasdefinition

Standing data: K is a field complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, not assumed discretely valued; O_K = K° = {|x| ≤ 1} is its valuation ring (so O_K is noetherian if and only if K is discretely valued); ϖ ∈ O_K is a pseudouniformiser, 0 < |ϖ| < 1; k = O_K/m_K is the residue field. The ϖ-adic topology on O_K is its valuation topology and does not depend on ϖ. For variables ξ = (ξ_1, …, ξ_n), O_K⟨ξ⟩ is the ring of restricted power series Σ c_ν ξ^ν with c_ν ∈ O_K and c_ν → 0, equivalently the ϖ-adic completion of O_K[ξ]. An O_K-algebra A is topologically of finite type (tft) if A ≅ O_K⟨ξ⟩/a for some n and some ideal a; it is topologically of finite presentation (tfp) if moreover a is finitely generated (this does not depend on the chosen presentation); it is admissible if it is tfp and has no ϖ-torsion, equivalently (O_K being a valuation ring) if it is tfp and flat over O_K. Such A carries the ϖ-adic topology; every O_K-algebra homomorphism between tft algebras is continuous. The word 'admissible' is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's and must not be confused with EGA's admissible topological rings. The same definitions are made verbatim over a noetherian ring R complete for the I-adic topology of an ideal I (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's case (II)), where tft and tfp agree.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, |·| nontrivial of rank one; discreteness is not assumed
