  • The topology is the ϖ-adic one, never the m_K-adic one (the two differ when m_K = m_K², e.g. K = C_p)
  • Presentations use finitely many variables

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/topologically-finitely-presented-algebra

Formal schemes of type (S): the class on which Huber's generic-fibre functor is defined, and its relation to admissible formal schemes and to Conrad's FS_Cdefinition

A formal scheme X = (X, O_X) is of type (S) if every point has an open affine neighbourhood U such that the topology of A := O_X(U) is adic and either (a) A is noetherian, or (b) there is s ∈ A such that sA is an ideal of definition and the Tate ring A(1/s) — the localisation A_s topologised by the images of s^m A — is strongly noetherian. For X of type (S) every formal affine open has an adic topology with a finitely generated ideal of definition. Morphisms of type-(S) formal schemes are adic (resp. locally of finite type) when locally the ring maps are adic (resp. topologically of finite type) in Huber's sense. Relations, all proved as part of this node's API: (i) every locally noetherian formal scheme (F0) is of type (S) via (a); (ii) every formal O_K-scheme locally of tf type (covered by Spf A with A tft over O_K with the ϖ-adic topology), in particular every locally tfp and every admissible one, is of type (S) via (b) with s = ϖ, since A[1/ϖ] is a quotient of K⟨ξ⟩ (K-affinoid after separated completion) and hence strongly noetherian; (iii) every object of Conrad's category FS_C (C an adic noetherian ring) is locally noetherian, hence of type (S) via (a); (iv) when K is not discretely valued, admissible formal O_K-schemes such as Spf O_K⟨T⟩ satisfy (b) but not (a) and are not objects of any FS_C, whereas Spf R_0[[T]] for a complete discrete valuation ring R_0 ⊆ O_K lies in FS_{R_0} and satisfies (a) but not (b); (v) for non-discrete K, Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ, T)-adic topology is not of type (S) at all. Formal completions of morphisms locally of finite type along finite-type ideals preserve type (S) and are adic (Huber 1996 (1.9.5)).

Hypotheses

  • Condition (S) is local on X and is stated for the rings of affine opens with adic topologies
  • The strongly noetherian hypothesis in (b) is on the Tate ring A(1/s), not on A
  • Conrad's FS_C requires C noetherian; type (S) does not

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S

Rig-points of admissible formal schemesdefinition

Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme. A rig-point of X is a morphism u: T → X of admissible formal O_K-schemes that is a closed immersion, with T = Spf B affine and B a local integral domain of dimension 1; its residue field is Frac(B). (Bosch–Lütkebohmert allow locally closed immersions; over a complete rank-one valuation ring locally closed rig-points are closed.) Properties: (3.2) B is finite over O_K and the integral closure of B in Frac(B) is the valuation ring O_{K'} of the finite extension K' = Frac(B) of K; (3.3) for an admissible blow-up X' → X the induced map on rig-points is bijective and preserves residue fields; (3.4) for X = Spf A the rig-points correspond bijectively to primes p ⊂ A with ϖ ∉ p and dim A/p = 1, and to closed points of Spec A[1/ϖ], i.e. to maximal ideals of the K-affinoid algebra A_K; (3.5) every closed point of X_s is the special point of some rig-point. Consequently rig-points of X correspond bijectively to the classical points of d(X) (residue field finite over K); the compatibility with the specialisation map λ (the special point of u is λ of the corresponding classical point) is proved in node specialisation-map, which depends on this node. Conrad's Lemma A.1.5: for Y flat and locally tfp over Spf O_K, every point y: Sp(K') → Y_rig is y_rig for a unique closed immersion Spf B → Y with B a finite flat O_K-domain, and every closed point of Y_s underlies such a map.

Hypotheses

  • X admissible over a complete rank-one O_K
  • Existence (3.5) in the rank-one case applies [BGR 7.1.5/4] to the integral closure of A in A ⊗ K (the packet gap entry describes it as the lifting of closed points of the reduction to points of Sp A); BGR is not in the library

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rig-point

Ideals of coefficients (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 2.1, Remark 2.2)definition

Let h: Z → T be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and 𝒥 ⊆ O_Z a coherent ideal, with closed formal subscheme V(𝒥) (locally Spf(B/b), b finitely generated). A coherent ideal 𝒞 ⊆ O_T is an ideal of coefficients of 𝒥 if (i) the projection Z ×_T V(𝒞) → Z factors through V(𝒥), and (ii) for every morphism T' → T of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation such that Z ×_T T' → Z factors through V(𝒥), the morphism T' → T factors through V(𝒞). Equivalently: 𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z, 𝒞 is the smallest coherent ideal of O_T with this property, and this remains true after every base change T' → T. An ideal of coefficients is unique when it exists; its formation commutes with base change (𝒞O_{T'} is the ideal of coefficients of 𝒥O_{Z×_T T'}) and with restriction to opens of T, so local ideals of coefficients glue. Set-theoretically, V(𝒞) ∩ T_0 is the set of t ∈ T_0 whose fibre Z ⊗ k(t) is contained in V(𝒥). If 𝒥 is open (ϖ^N O_Z ⊆ 𝒥) and h is faithfully flat, then 𝒞 is open (Remark 2.2, which Bosch–Lütkebohmert state without the flatness hypothesis). Affine formula: if Z = Spf B → T = Spf A and B has a topological basis (e_i)_{i∈I} over A (node topological-basis-lifting), and b = (f_1, …, f_r) with f_j = Σ_i a_{ij} e_i, then the ideal a = (a_{ij}) is contained in every ideal c ⊆ A with b ⊆ Bc, and is the ideal of coefficients of b whenever it is finitely generated. For f ∈ B, the content c(f) is the ideal of coefficients of fB. The same definitions apply on generic fibres, to ideals of B_K = B ⊗_{O_K} K and A_K (coherent ideals of O_{Z_rig}, O_{T_rig}), with rig-points in place of points.

Hypotheses

  • Z, T formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation; 𝒥 and 𝒞 coherent
  • Existence is not part of the definition (nodes ideal-of-coefficients-existence, rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence)
  • Not the ideal of the scheme-theoretic image and not determined by the zero locus: (a², ϖ) and (a, ϖ) have the same zero locus

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/ideal-of-coefficients

T-dévissages of a coherent module in one dimension (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.1)definition

Conventions: K is complete for a nontrivial rank-one valuation, O_K its valuation ring, ϖ a pseudouniformiser; formal schemes are formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation (node admissible-formal-scheme), X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}, X_0 has the underlying space of X, and for t ∈ T_0 the fibre X ⊗ k(t) is X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t). Let f: X → T be a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, ℳ a coherent O_X-module (node admissible-formal-scheme, coherent modules), x ∈ X_0, t = f(x) and n ∈ ℕ. A T-dévissage of ℳ in dimension n at x is a tuple D = (g: (Y, y) → (Z, z), ℳ, α: ℒ → 𝒩, 𝒫) consisting of (a) a pointed closed immersion (Y, y) → (X, x) of finite presentation whose ideal annihilates ℳ, so that ℳ is the direct image of a coherent O_Y-module, again written ℳ; (b) a pointed factorisation (Y, y) →g (Z, z) →h (T, t) of Y → T with g finite, y the only point of Y_0 above z, and h affine and smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension n; (c) a homomorphism α: ℒ = O_Z^ℓ → 𝒩 := g_*ℳ of coherent O_Z-modules such that α ⊗ k(ζ) is bijective, ζ the generic point of the fibre Z ⊗ k(t); 𝒫 := coker α. Then dim_z(𝒫 ⊗ k(t)) ≤ n − 1, and 𝒫 is a module over a closed formal subscheme Y' ⊆ Z of finite presentation with dim(Y' ⊗ k(t)) ≤ n − 1. The fibre dimension of ℳ at x is at most n (Definition 3.1 does not require equality). Dévissages pull back along pointed base changes (T', t') → (T, t).

Hypotheses

  • X, T quasi-compact and locally of tf presentation over O_K (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's standing assumption in §3)
  • h has geometrically irreducible fibres, so the fibre over t has a single generic point ζ
  • ℓ = 0 is allowed (then 𝒩 ⊗ k(ζ) = 0)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-devissage-step

T-dévissages in several dimensions and complete dévissages (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.2)definition

In the setting of node formal-devissage-step, a T-dévissage of ℳ at x in dimensions N = n¹ > n² > … > n^r = n ≥ 0 (between N and n) is a sequence (D¹, …, D^r) of T-dévissages D^i = (g^i: (Y^i, y^i) → (Z^i, z^i), ℳ^i, α^i: ℒ^i → 𝒩^i = g^i_*ℳ^i, 𝒫^i) such that D¹ is a T-dévissage of ℳ at x in dimension n¹ and, for i = 2, …, r, D^i is a T-dévissage of the coherent O_{Z^{i−1}}-module 𝒫^{i−1} at z^{i−1} in dimension n^i; thus ℳ¹ = ℳ|_{Y¹} and ℳ^i = 𝒫^{i−1}|_{Y^i}. Its length is r; it is complete if 𝒫^r = 0. Dévissages, complete or not, are stable under base change (T', t') → (T, t), and truncations (D¹, …, D^k) are dévissages in dimensions between N and n^k. The support of 𝒩^i has relative dimension ≤ n^i and that of 𝒫^i relative dimension < n^i, which is what makes dévissages the vehicle for induction on relative dimension.

Hypotheses

  • Dimensions strictly decreasing
  • Completeness is the condition 𝒫^r = 0

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-devissage

Flat locus and flatness in dimension ≥ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II §3, after Corollary 3.8)definition

Let f: X → T be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. The flat locus of ℳ over T is F(ℳ/T) = {x ∈ X_0 : ℳ_x is a flat O_{T,f(x)}-module} ⊆ X_0 (points of X_0 are the points of X). For n ∈ ℕ and x ∈ X_0 with t = f(x), ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n at x if dim_x((X_0 ∖ F(ℳ/T)) ∩ (X ⊗ k(t))) < n — the dimension at x of the non-flat locus inside the fibre, −∞ when x is not in its closure; ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n if this holds at every x ∈ X_0, and T-flat in dimension ≥ n over an open U_0 ⊆ T_0 if it holds at every x over U_0. A morphism f is flat in dimension ≥ n if O_X is. Flatness in dimension ≥ n implies flatness in dimension ≥ n + 1, and if dim(X/T) ≤ n then every ℳ is T-flat in dimension ≥ n + 1. (Raynaud–Gruson 5.2.1 give the scheme-theoretic notion through a retrocompact open of flatness with small complement.)

Hypotheses

  • Dimensions are measured in the fibres X ⊗ k(t), not in X_0
  • Flatness is stalkwise over the base

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/flat-in-dimension

Rig-flatness, relative rig-dimension and rig-flatness in dimension ≥ n (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §5; II Definition 3.9 and §4)definition

Let f: X → T be a morphism of quasi-compact formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation with T admissible, and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. (i) Rig-flatness: for formal affine opens Spf C ⊆ X and Spf A ⊆ T with f(Spf C) ⊆ Spf A, ℳ ↔ the finite C-module M, and a rig-point x of Spf C (a maximal ideal of C_K = C ⊗_{O_K} K, node rig-point), ℳ is rig-flat over T at x if the localisation M_x is a flat A-module (equivalently (M_K)_x is flat over (A_K)_y, y the image maximal ideal); this is independent of the charts and invariant under admissible blow-ups of X and of T (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Proposition 5.3). (ii) Relative rig-dimension (II Definition 3.9): for a rig-point x of X over the rig-point t of T, dim_x(X/T) is the Krull dimension of the local ring at x of the affinoid algebra C_K ⊗_{A_K} K(t), K(t) = A_K/t — the dimension at x of the rigid fibre X_rig ×_{T_rig} t; for a closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X, dim(Y/T)_rig is the supremum of dim_y(Y/T) over the rig-points y of Y (−∞ if there are none). (iii) ℳ is rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n if there is a closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X of finite presentation with dim(Y/T)_rig ≤ n − 1 such that ℳ is rig-flat at every rig-point of X not factoring through Y; above a rig-point t of T if this holds for the rig-points of X and Y over t. Rig-flat in dimension ≥ 0 means rig-flat at every rig-point ('f_rig flat' for ℳ = O_X); if dim(X/T)_rig ≤ n − 1 then ℳ is rig-flat in dimension ≥ n.

Hypotheses

  • T admissible; X locally of tf presentation, possibly with ϖ-torsion
  • Dimensions are those of rigid fibres over rig-points of T
  • Bosch–Lütkebohmert's Proposition 3.11 (the non-rig-flat locus is Zariski closed) is not needed: (iii) quantifies over closed subschemes Y

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rig-flat-in-dimension

Smooth and étale morphisms of formal schemes locally of tf presentation; continuous differentialsdefinition

Let f: X → Y be a morphism of formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation (for P7: O_K = W(κ), κ perfect). f is smooth at x ∈ X of relative dimension d if there are an open neighbourhood U of x and a Y-immersion j: U → D^n_Y = Spf O_Y⟨ζ_1, …, ζ_n⟩ such that, locally at j(x), the ideal of j(U) is generated by n − d sections g_{d+1}, …, g_n whose differentials are linearly independent in Ω¹_{D^n_Y/Y} ⊗ κ(j(x)); f is smooth if smooth at all points, and étale if smooth of relative dimension 0 (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 1.1). Equivalently (II Lemma 1.2): f is flat at x and f_0: X_0 → Y_0 is smooth at x of relative dimension d; equivalently every reduction f_m: X_m → Y_m modulo ϖ^{m+1} is smooth at x of relative dimension d (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth for schemes). Equivalently f is formally smooth and locally topologically of finite presentation, and then locally f factors as an étale morphism to D^d_Y. The module of continuous differentials Ω¹_{X/Y} := lim_m Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m} is coherent; for f smooth of relative dimension d it is locally free of rank d, with basis dT_1, …, dT_d on an étale chart X → D^d_Y. A formal scheme smooth over Spf O_K is admissible.

Hypotheses

  • X, Y locally of tf presentation over O_K (K complete of rank one) or noetherian (Bosch–Lütkebohmert's case II)
  • Smoothness is a condition on all levels X_m, not on the generic fibre: d(f) smooth does not imply f smooth

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-formal-scheme

Fractional valuation bounds |f| ≤ |g|^q and |f| ≥ |g|^q for q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}definition

Let A be a commutative ring, f, g ∈ A and q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}. For v ∈ Spv A write q = a/b with a ∈ ℕ, b ∈ ℕ_{>0}, and define |f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q to mean v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a) (the valuative relation f^b ≤_v g^a), and |f(v)| ≥ |g(v)|^q to mean v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a); strict versions likewise. This does not depend on the representative (a, b) of q, because x ↦ x^n is strictly increasing on a totally ordered value monoid. Put fracPowLE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)} and fracPowGE f g q := {v : v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a)}. No element 'g^q' of A (or of the base field) is used: when K = Q_p, |p|^{1/2} is not the absolute value of any element of K, yet {|f| ≤ |p|^{1/2}} is defined. Second convention, compatible with the first: if B is an A⁺-algebra containing c and a unit u of B⁺ with c^b = g^a u (e.g. c = ϖ^{a/b} ∈ L = K(ϖ^{1/b}), or c = p^ε ∈ Z_p^cycl of p-adic valuation ε), then for v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) one has |f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q ⟺ v(f) ≤ v(c). When g is a unit (e.g. g = ϖ in a Tate ring), fracPowLE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺) is the rational subset R({f^b, g^a}/g^a) and fracPowGE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺) is R({g^a, f^b}/f^b).

Hypotheses

  • A arbitrary commutative ring for the definition; A Huber, g a unit, for the rational-subset descriptions
  • q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}; the representative (a, b) is arbitrary with b > 0
  • The threshold |g|^q is realised by an element only after an explicit extension (second convention)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/fractional-valuation-bound

Coherent modules and coherent rings (the ring case of EGA 0 §5.3, as recalled in Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1)definitionadded in review

Let A be a commutative ring. A finitely generated A-module M is coherent if every finitely generated submodule of M is finitely presented; A is a coherent ring if it is coherent as an A-module (every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented). If two of the modules in a short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 are coherent, so is the third; hence finite direct sums, kernels, cokernels and images of maps between coherent modules, and sums and intersections of coherent submodules of a coherent module, are coherent. Over a coherent ring a module is coherent iff it is finitely presented, and M ⊗_A N and Hom_A(M, N) are coherent for coherent M, N. If A is coherent and a ⊆ A is a finitely generated ideal, A/a is a coherent ring and an A/a-module is coherent over A/a iff it is coherent over A.

Hypotheses

  • No noetherian hypothesis: the point of the notion is the non-noetherian rings O_K⟨ξ⟩/a
  • Coherent means finitely generated with all finitely generated submodules finitely presented, not merely finitely presented

Added during review; not yet independently checked

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/coherent-modules

Huber's functor t from locally noetherian formal schemes to adic spacesconstruction

For a locally noetherian formal scheme X (F0) there are an adic space t(X) and a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces π_X: (t(X), O⁺_{t(X)}) → (X, O_X) such that every morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces (Z, O⁺_Z) → (X, O_X) from an adic space Z factors uniquely through a morphism of adic spaces Z → t(X). On affines t(Spf A) = Spa(A, A), and π_X(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}, the centre of x. The universal property makes t a functor; t is fully faithful; a morphism f of locally noetherian formal schemes is adic (EGA I 10.12) resp. locally of finite type (EGA I 10.13) if and only if t(f) is adic resp. locally of finite type (Huber 1994 Proposition 4.2(i)). The trivial valuations form a subspace t(X)_t ⊆ t(X) and π_X restricts to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (t(X)_t, O⁺|) ≅ (X, O_X); in particular π_X has a section ι_X by trivial valuations. The smallest saturated subcategory of adic spaces containing the image of t consists of the adic spaces locally of the form Spa(A, A⁺) with A finitely generated over a noetherian ring of definition A_0 and A⁺ the integral closure of A_0 in A (4.2(ii)).

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian (F0); for non-noetherian formal models use node generic-fibre-functor-d instead
  • Spa(A, A) must be an adic space: the structure presheaf of Spa(A, A) for a noetherian adic ring A is a sheaf (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space

The specialisation map λ_X = sp: d(X) → Xconstruction

For X of type (S) the specialisation map is the continuous map λ_X: d(X) → X underlying Proposition 1.9.1. For X = Spf A and x ∈ d(X), λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}, an open prime of A; equivalently λ(x) is the centre of x, the image of the closed point of Spec κ(x)⁺ under the map Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A induced by A → κ(x)⁺ (|A(x)| ≤ 1). Properties: (i) λ is continuous: for s ∈ A, λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {|s| = 1} = {|s| ≥ 1} is open and λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1} is closed; (ii) λ is natural: λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X; (iii) for X admissible over O_K, λ maps each classical point (residue field finite over K) to a closed point of X_s, and every closed point of X_s is the image of a classical point (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 3.4, 3.5), λ of the classical point attached to a rig-point being its special point; the restriction sp: X_rig → X to classical points is Berthelot's specialisation map of rigid geometry, which is anticontinuous: preimages of closed subsets are admissible opens (the tubes of node tube); (iv) λ is compatible with admissible blow-ups φ: X' → X, i.e. φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ) with d(φ) an isomorphism (node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups); (v) for X quasi-compact admissible, the maps λ_{X'} over all admissible blow-ups X' → X induce a homeomorphism d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'| and an isomorphism (d(X), O⁺) ≅ lim (X', O_{X'}) (Zariski–Riemann description; Hübner Theorem 8.9, proof cited from Bhatt's notes Proposition 8.1.3, and Conrad, Several approaches §4.1).

Hypotheses

  • X of type (S) for (i),(ii); admissible over O_K for (iii)–(v)
  • Care: in the adic space, λ⁻¹ of a closed set is closed, not open; the rigid 'anticontinuity' concerns classical points and corresponds to the interior (node tube)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/specialisation-map

Tubes ]T[ of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigidconstruction

Let X be an admissible formal O_K-scheme with specialisation λ: d(X) → X (node specialisation-map). For T ⊆ X locally closed (X and X_s have the same space): (i) if T = U is open, ]U[ := λ⁻¹(U) = d(X|_U), an open subspace; (ii) if T = Z is closed and X = Spf A with Z = V(f_1, …, f_r) ⊆ Spec A/ϖ (f_i ∈ A), then ]Z[ := ⋃_{m≥1} {x ∈ d(X) : |f_i(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ| for all i}; this is independent of the chosen f_i and of ϖ, equals the interior of the closed set λ⁻¹(Z), and glues over affine covers; (iii) for T = U ∩ Z, ]T[ := λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[. Each ]T[ is open in d(X). Rigid comparison: the classical points of ]T[ are exactly the classical points x with sp(x) ∈ T, i.e. Berthelot's tube sp⁻¹(T), which is an admissible open of X_rig, and r(sp⁻¹(T)) = ]T[ under AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor. For closed Z and rational q > 0, the closed tube of radius |ϖ|^q is [Z]_q := {x : |f_i(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^q for all i}, in the convention of node fractional-valuation-bound; it is quasi-compact and ]Z[ = ⋃_{q>0} [Z]_q. The set λ⁻¹(Z) itself is closed, and in general strictly larger than ]Z[ by non-classical boundary points; Huber's pseudo-adic spaces d(X, L) use λ⁻¹(L), not the interior.

Hypotheses

  • X admissible over O_K (the definitions make sense for X of type (S) with ϖ replaced by s)
  • T locally closed in X_s
  • Radii |ϖ|^q with q ∈ ℚ_{>0} use node fractional-valuation-bound, never an element ϖ^q of K

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube

Fitting ideals of coherent modules on formal schemes (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 3.13)construction

Let X be a formal O_K-scheme locally of tf presentation and ℳ a coherent O_X-module. For r ∈ ℕ the r-th Fitting ideal F_r(ℳ) ⊆ O_X is the coherent ideal given on a formal affine open U = Spf A by the ring-level Fitting ideal F_r(M) ⊆ A of the finitely presented A-module M = Γ(U, ℳ): for a presentation A^m →φ A^n → M → 0, F_r(M) is generated by the (n − r) × (n − r) minors of φ (F_r(M) = A if n − r ≤ 0), independently of the presentation and compatibly with base change, F_r(M ⊗_A A') = F_r(M)A' (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.4.1; the ring-level Fitting ideal of finitely presented modules is owned by the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 0). These glue to a coherent ideal F_r(ℳ), compatible with restriction and with pull-back along morphisms of formal schemes; F_0(ℳ) ⊆ F_1(ℳ) ⊆ …; F_r(ℳ)_x = O_{X,x} iff ℳ_x is generated by r elements; if ℳ is locally free of rank r then F_{r−1}(ℳ) = 0 and F_r(ℳ) = O_X.

Hypotheses

  • ℳ coherent, so its sections over formal affine opens are finitely presented modules over coherent rings (node tfp-algebra-coherent)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-fitting-ideal

Conrad's Berthelot-type functor (·)^rig on FS_C for arbitrary complete kconstruction

Fix an adic noetherian ring C with a continuous map C → R to the valuation ring R of a complete nonarchimedean field k (no discreteness assumption on k; examples: C = R if k is discretely valued; C = R_0 a complete discrete valuation ring with R_0 → R local; C = Z discrete). FS_C is the category of locally noetherian formal schemes X over Spf C whose underlying reduced scheme is locally of finite type over C_red; affine opens have algebras that are quotients of C[[q_1, …, q_n]]{{T_1, …, T_m}} with the (I, q)-adic topology. For X in FS_C and a rigid space Z over k, Hom^cont_C(Z, X) is the set of morphisms of locally ringed G-topologised spaces whose ring maps are C-algebra maps landing in locally power-bounded sections and carrying locally topologically nilpotent sections to locally topologically nilpotent sections. Theorem 3.1.5: Hom^cont_C(·, X) is represented by a quasi-separated rigid space X^rig; (·)^rig takes open/closed immersions to open/closed immersions and open covers to admissible covers, commutes with fibre products (a), with analytic extension of k (b) and with change of C (c), preserves separatedness (d), and sends topologically finite type maps to quasi-compact maps (e). Spf(C[[q]])^rig is the open unit disc Δ = {|t| < 1}. Through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor this gives an adic space r(X^rig) over Spa(k, R).

Hypotheses

  • C adic noetherian with continuous C → R; k arbitrary complete nonarchimedean
  • Objects of FS_C are locally noetherian: the functor does not apply to non-noetherian formal O_K-models when k is not discretely valued (those are handled by nodes generic-fibre-functor-d and raynaud-generic-fibre)
  • Theorem 3.1.6 (preservation of finiteness, smoothness, properness, flatness, fibre dimension) is the separate node berthelot-rig-functor-preserves-properties

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base

The domain {|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q} cut out by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal modelconstruction

Let 𝔛 be an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ℒ an invertible O_𝔛-module, s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ) and q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}. Choose an open cover 𝔛 = ⋃ U_j by formal affines U_j = Spf A_j with generators ℒ|_{U_j} = O e_j, and write s|_{U_j} = f_j e_j. Define 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) := ⋃_j (fracPowGE f_j ϖ q ∩ d(U_j)) ⊆ d(𝔛), and likewise 𝔛_η(|s| ≤ |ϖ|^q) with fracPowLE. These sets do not depend on the cover or the generators: on U_j ∩ U_k one has e_k = u e_j with u ∈ O(U_j ∩ U_k)^×, so f_j = u f_k, and |u(x)| = 1 on d(U_j ∩ U_k) because u, u⁻¹ ∈ O ⊆ O⁺. They are open (finite unions of rational subsets when 𝔛 is quasi-compact) and functorial under pull-back. Independence of lifts: if s' ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ) with s − s' ∈ ϖ^c ℒ for some c ∈ ℚ with c > q (ϖ^c ℒ meaning sections whose local coordinates satisfy |·| ≤ |ϖ|^c), then 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) = 𝔛_η(|s'| ≥ |ϖ|^q); hence a section s̄ of ℒ ⊗ O_K/ϖ^m (m > q) determines a well-defined domain 𝔛_η(|s̄| ≥ |ϖ|^q) through arbitrary local lifts. The domain depends on the integral structure ℒ, not only on the invertible sheaf ℒ_η on d(𝔛).

Hypotheses

  • 𝔛 admissible (the construction works verbatim for 𝔛 of type (S) with ϖ replaced by s)
  • ℒ invertible on the formal model; s a global section (or local lifts of a section modulo ϖ^m with m > q)
  • q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}, interpreted by node fractional-valuation-bound

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/section-valuation-domain

Formal model of a section domain: the open chart of the admissible blow-up of (s, c)construction

Let 𝔛 be an admissible formal O_K-scheme, ℒ invertible, s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ), and c ∈ O_K ∖ {0} (the threshold, e.g. c = ϖ^a, or c = p^ε when K contains such an element; for a fractional q = a/b without such an element use (s^{⊗b}, ϖ^a) in ℒ^{⊗b}). Let 𝒜 ⊆ O_𝔛 be the coherent open ideal locally generated by (f_j, c) where s = f_j e_j (independent of generators), and let 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ⊆ Bl_𝒜 𝔛 be the open formal subscheme where s generates 𝒜O. Locally, over U = Spf A with ℒ|_U = Ae and s = fe, 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ×_𝔛 U = Spf(A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) modulo ϖ-torsion), with u ∈ Γ(ℒ⁻¹) the section with u·s = c. Universal property: for a ϖ-torsion-free formal scheme Z over Spf O_K with g: Z → 𝔛, lifts of g to 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) correspond bijectively to sections u ∈ Γ(Z, g*ℒ⁻¹) with u·g*s = c (such u is unique if it exists). Generic fibre: d(𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|)) → d(𝔛) is an open immersion with image {x : |s(x)| ≥ |c(x)|} = sectionDomainGE s q when |c| = |ϖ|^q. Change of lift: if s' = s + c' t with c' ∈ c·m_K (so |c'| < |c|) and t ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ), the models for s and s' are canonically isomorphic over 𝔛 via u' = u(1 + (c'/c) u t)⁻¹, compatibly with the equality of generic-fibre domains; if c'' = wc with w ∈ O_K^×, the models for c and c'' are isomorphic via u'' = wu. Flatness: if f̄ is a non-zero-divisor on A/ϖ and c ∈ m_K (or c a unit), A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) is already ϖ-torsion-free.

Hypotheses

  • 𝔛 admissible; ℒ invertible; c ∈ O_K nonzero, so 𝒜 ⊇ c O_𝔛 is open
  • The model is an open formal subscheme of an admissible blow-up, not the blow-up itself: its generic fibre is the domain {|s| ≥ |c|}, not d(𝔛)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/section-domain-formal-model

Conrad's Hasse-invariant loci S^{>h}, S^{≥h} of a generalized elliptic curve are admissible opensconstruction

For a generalized elliptic curve E → S over a rigid space S over k (k complete over Q_p, |p| = p⁻¹), the Hasse invariant of a fibre E_s is h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p) ∈ [1/p, 1] (Definition B.3.3: a lifts the coefficient of X^p in [p]*(X) mod p on the formal group of a semistable model). The loci S^{>h} (h ∈ [1/p, 1) ∩ √|k^×|) and S^{≥h} (h ∈ (1/p, 1] ∩ √|k^×|) of points with h(E_s) > h (resp. ≥ h) are admissible opens; their formation commutes with base change on S and, for quasi-separated or pseudo-separated S (Conrad 4.1.1(2)), with analytic extension of k; S^{≥h} → S is quasi-compact; and {S^{≥h}}_{h ∈ (h_0,1)} is an admissible cover of S^{>h_0}. Local description: on a formal affine Spf A of the formal completion M̂ of the proper moduli scheme M over which e*Ω̂¹ is trivial, with Γ_A ≅ Spf A[[X]] the formal group and a_{Γ_A} the coefficient of X^p in [p]*(X), S^{>h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| > h} and S^{≥h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}, independent of the coordinate X. Thresholds h ∈ √|k^×| are read with the convention of node fractional-valuation-bound. Through R1's comparison r these are opens of the adic space, and for h = |p|^ε with 0 ≤ ε < 1 (so h ∈ (1/p, 1]) S^{≥h} is the Hasse domain X(ε) of node hasse-domain for ω the Hodge bundle and Ha the Hasse invariant (a ≡ Ha in the trivialisation of ω by the dual of dX).

Hypotheses

  • k complete nonarchimedean of residue characteristic p, analytic over Q_p
  • E → S a generalized elliptic curve over a rigid space; the reduction to the universal case uses the analytified moduli (Conrad Theorem 3.2.3) and fpqc descent of admissible opens ([C3, 4.2.4, 4.2.7]), not read
  • M̂^rig ≅ M^an_k and Ê^rig ≅ E^an_k use properness (node good-reduction-locus)

AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-loci-admissible-opens

R3Coherent sheaves and finite traces

Coherent sheafdefinitionplanetCoherent sheaves on locally noetherian adic spaces

Let X be a locally noetherian adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) with structure sheaf 𝒪_X (anchor Layer 5). A sheaf F of 𝒪_X-modules on the topological space X is coherent if there is an open covering of X by affinoid open subspaces U_i ≅ Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) with A_i complete of noetherian type (noetherian ring of definition, or strongly noetherian Tate) and finitely generated A_i-modules M_i with F|_{U_i} ≅ M̃_i (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf). Coh(X) is the full subcategory of 𝒪_X-modules on coherent objects. On strongly noetherian Tate affinoid opens U the condition then holds with M = F(U) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid); on affinoid opens with a noetherian ring of definition the definition is used only through such coverings.

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian adic space
  • 𝒪_X a sheaf (X an adic space, anchor Layer 5)

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf

Trace mapconstructionplanetThe trace of a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces

Let f : Y → X be a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-morphism). The trace Tr_f : f_*𝒪_Y → 𝒪_X is the composite of the multiplication map f_*𝒪_Y → ℋom_{𝒪_X}(f_*𝒪_Y, f_*𝒪_Y) with the trace ℋom(E, E) → 𝒪_X of the vector bundle E = f_*𝒪_Y, defined on every open U over which E is free as the matrix trace (independent of the basis) and glued. On a sheafy Tate affinoid U = Spa(A, A⁺) it is Tr_{B/A} for B = 𝒪_Y(f⁻¹U) (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace). Tr_f is 𝒪_X-linear, Tr_f ∘ f^♯ is multiplication by the degree, and Tr_f is not a sum over geometric points of fibres unless f is étale.

Hypotheses

  • f finite locally free

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/analytic-trace-finite-locally-free

Glueing squares of complete Tate ringsdefinition

A glueing square is a commutative square of complete Hausdorff Tate rings with continuous homomorphisms R → R₁, R → R₂, R₁ → R₁₂, R₂ → R₁₂ such that (a) the sequence 0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ → 0, (r₁, r₂) ↦ r₁ − r₂, is exact and strict (R carries the subspace topology of R₁ × R₂ and R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ is open onto R₁₂); (b) R₂ → R₁₂ has dense image; (c) every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a prime ideal of R₁ × R₂. A finite (resp. finite projective) glueing datum on it is a triple of finite (resp. finite projective) modules M₁, M₂, M₁₂ over R₁, R₂, R₁₂ with isomorphisms ψ_i : M_i ⊗_{R_i} R₁₂ ≅ M₁₂; its module of sections is M = ker(ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂). Convention: condition (c) replaces Kedlaya–Liu's surjectivity of Gel'fand spectra M(R₁ ⊕ R₂) → M(R), which they use only through (c); every topological ring here is metrised by the norm |x| = inf{cⁿ : ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ R₀} of a pseudouniformiser ϖ and ring of definition R₀ (KL Remark 2.4.4).

Hypotheses

  • all four rings complete Hausdorff Tate rings; maps continuous
  • (a) strict exactness, (b) density, (c) maximal ideals lift

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square

Quasi-Stein adic spacesdefinition

Let X an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value. X is quasi-Stein if there is a sequence U₁ ⊆ U₂ ⊆ ⋯ of affinoid open subspaces with X = ⋃ₙ Uₙ such that each restriction 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) → 𝒪_X(Uₙ) has dense image. It is Stein if moreover, for every n, Uₙ = {x ∈ U_{n+1} : |f₁(x)| ≤ 1, …, |f_r(x)| ≤ 1} is the Weierstrass domain of U_{n+1} defined by some f₁, …, f_r ∈ 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) and there is aₙ ∈ K with 0 < |aₙ| < 1 such that f₁/aₙ, …, f_r/aₙ topologically generate the affinoid K-algebra 𝒪_X(U_{n+1}) (Kiehl's condition after Definition 2.3). The data of the exhausting sequence is not part of the predicate; theorems quantify over any such sequence.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-space

Vector bundles (locally free sheaves of finite rank) on adic spacesdefinition

Let X be an adic space (anchor Layer 5; 𝒪_X is a sheaf). A vector bundle on X is a sheaf of 𝒪_X-modules E such that X has an open covering {U_i} with E|_{U_i} ≅ 𝒪_{U_i}^{n_i} for some n_i ∈ ℕ; equivalently E satisfies Mathlib's SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree with local bases of finite type. The rank is the locally constant function x ↦ n_i on U_i. Vector bundles form the full subcategory VectorBundle(X) of 𝒪_X-modules. No noetherian hypothesis is imposed; on locally noetherian X every vector bundle is coherent, but not conversely.

Hypotheses

  • X an adic space (structure presheaf a sheaf)

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf

Completely continuous maps of Banach modules over an affinoid algebradefinition

Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°, and fix a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A containing the image of K°. A Banach A-module is a complete topological A-module M whose topology is defined by an open A₀-submodule M₀ (so the ϖⁿM₀ form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0), with the norm |m| = inf{|a| : a ∈ K, m ∈ aM₀}. A continuous A-linear map f : M → N of Banach A-modules is completely continuous if it is the limit, in the operator norm, of continuous A-linear maps f_i : M → N with finitely generated image. It is strictly completely continuous if there are such f_i and a ∈ K° ∖ {0} such that for every i, a·f_i(M₀) lies in some finitely generated A₀-submodule of N₀, which may depend on i (Kiehl's 'streng vollständig stetig': 'in einem — von i abhängigen — endlichen B₀-Untermodul von N₀'); the scalar a, and hence the bound a·f_i(M₀) ⊆ N₀, is uniform in i.

Hypotheses

  • K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
  • M, N Banach A-modules
  • f continuous A-linear

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/completely-continuous-map

Relatively compact affinoid subdomains over an affinoid base (Kiehl)definition

Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°. Let V = Spa(B, B°) be an affinoid adic space over Spa(A, A°) with B topologically of finite type over A, and U ⊆ V an affinoid open subspace. U is relatively compact in V over A, written U ⋐_A V, if there are a closed immersion V ↪ Dⁿ_A = Spa(A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩) over A and ε ∈ √|K^×| with ε < 1 such that U ⊆ {|X_i| ≤ ε for all i}. (Kiehl's 'U liegt im Innern von V bezüglich A'.)

Hypotheses

  • K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value; adic spaces are locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°); A denotes an affinoid K-algebra (a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩, strongly noetherian Tate) with A⁺ = A°
  • V affinoid tft over A
  • U affinoid open in V

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/relatively-compact-affinoid

Finite locally free morphisms of adic spacesdefinition

A morphism of adic spaces f : Y → X is finite locally free if it is finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) and f_*𝒪_Y is a vector bundle on X (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf). Its degree is the rank of f_*𝒪_Y, a locally constant function on X. Over an open affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with A a complete Tate ring such that f⁻¹(Spa A) is affinoid — such affinoids cover X by the definition of finiteness, and every open affinoid with A strongly noetherian qualifies (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism, Zavyalov Theorem B.2.18) — f⁻¹(Spa A) = Spa(B, B⁺) with B a finite projective A-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing) and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺, and for every rational V ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺), f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V)) with the uncompleted tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-algebra-tensor-complete (iii)). It is not asserted that f⁻¹ of every sheafy Tate affinoid is affinoid (Zavyalov Remark B.2.19; Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.2.18).

Hypotheses

  • f a morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-morphism

The sheaf M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X associated with a finite module on a noetherian affinoidconstruction

Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A complete and Hausdorff, and A is of one of Huber's two noetherian types: (I) A has a noetherian ring of definition, or (II) A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian: every A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ is noetherian), let X = Spa(A, A⁺) and let M be a finitely generated A-module. The associated presheaf M̃ (Huber's M ⊗ 𝒪_A) is the presheaf of topological 𝒪_X-modules on X defined on the rational basis by M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) for U = R(T/s), where 𝒪_X(U) = A⟨T/s⟩ is the complete rational localisation of anchor Layer 3.1 and the ordinary (uncompleted) tensor product carries its natural 𝒪_X(U)-module topology (the quotient topology along any surjection 𝒪_X(U)ⁿ ↠ M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)); the restriction for rational V ⊆ U is id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U}. On an arbitrary open W ⊆ X, M̃(W) = lim M̃(V) over the rational V ⊆ W, with the inverse-limit topology. An A-linear map φ : M → N induces φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ, functorially. Convention: the tensor product is not completed; for finite M over these rings M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) is already complete and equals the completed tensor product (Huber Lemmas 2.3(iii), 2.4(ii)), and the construction is only made for finitely generated M.

Hypotheses

  • A complete and Hausdorff; A has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring
  • A⁺ ⊆ A a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0.2)
  • M a finitely generated A-module

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf

The abelian tensor category of coherent sheaves and pullbackconstruction

Let X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space whose points all have affinoid neighbourhoods Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (for instance X locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°), K a complete nonarchimedean field). Coh(X) is an abelian full subcategory of 𝒪_X-modules closed under kernels, cokernels, images, extensions, ⊗_{𝒪_X} and the internal Hom sheaf ℋom_{𝒪_X}(F, G); the inclusion is exact. For a morphism f : Y → X of such spaces, the pullback f*F = 𝒪_Y ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪_X} f⁻¹F defines a right exact monoidal functor f* : Coh(X) → Coh(Y) with (id)* ≅ id and (g ∘ f)* ≅ f* ∘ g*; affinoid-locally, for Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) induced by a continuous A → B, f*M̃ ≅ (M ⊗_A B)~. Base change of coherent sheaves along a fibre product square (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) is pullback along the projection.

Hypotheses

  • X, Y locally noetherian analytic with strongly noetherian Tate affinoid charts
  • f a morphism of adic spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf-operations

The coherent sheaf of continuous differentials Ω¹_{X/Y} and its exterior powersconstruction

Let f: X → Y be a morphism locally of finite type (anchor Layer 5.2) between locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space). There is a coherent O_X-module Ω¹_{X/Y} (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf) with an f⁻¹O_Y-linear derivation d = d_{X/Y}: O_X → Ω¹_{X/Y}, characterised as follows. For every pair of affinoid opens U = Spa(B, B⁺) ⊆ X and V = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V and A → B topologically of finite type (such U cover X), Ω¹_{X/Y}|_U ≅ (Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf), with d = d_{B/A} on sections over U (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/continuous-differentials). The identifications on a rational U' = Spa(B⟨T/s⟩) ⊆ U are the localisation isomorphisms Ωᶜ_{B⟨T/s⟩/A} ≅ B⟨T/s⟩ ⊗_B Ωᶜ_{B/A}. Shrinking V to a rational V' ⊇ f(U), A' = A⟨T'/s'⟩, does not change Ωᶜ_{B/A} = Ωᶜ_{B/A'}. Properties: (a) universal property: for every coherent O_X-module F, Hom_{O_X}(Ω¹_{X/Y}, F) is the set of f⁻¹O_Y-linear derivations D: O_X → F that are continuous on sections over affinoid opens, via u ↦ u ∘ d; (b) exact sequences: for X → Y → Z (both locally of finite type) the sequence f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0 is exact, and for a closed embedding i: X → P over Y with coherent ideal 𝓘 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-ideal-closed-subspace), 𝓘/𝓘² → i*Ω¹_{P/Y} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0 is exact; (c) f is unramified iff Ω¹_{X/Y} = 0; if f is smooth of relative dimension n at x, Ω¹_{X/Y} is a vector bundle of rank n near x (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/locally-free-sheaf), and for X → Y → Z with f smooth the sequence of (b) is left exact and locally split; if f is étale, f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} ≅ Ω¹_{X/Z}, in particular u*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y} for every étale u: U → X, which makes U ↦ Ω¹_{U/Y}(U) a sheaf on the small étale site of X; (d) base change: for a cartesian square X' = X ×_Y Y' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence) with projection p: X' → X, p*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{X'/Y'} compatibly with d; (e) analytification: for a morphism h of schemes locally of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field K, Ω¹_{X^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω¹_{X/Y})^ad compatibly with d (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-kahler-differentials); (f) exterior powers: Ωⁱ_{X/Y} := ⋀ⁱ_{O_X} Ω¹_{X/Y}, the sheaf associated with U ↦ ⋀ⁱ_{O(U)} Ω¹_{X/Y}(U), is coherent, with sections (⋀ⁱ_B Ωᶜ_{B/A})~ over U as above; for f smooth of relative dimension n it is a vector bundle of rank C(n, i); d extends uniquely to f⁻¹O_Y-linear maps d: Ωⁱ_{X/Y} → Ωⁱ⁺¹_{X/Y} with d ∘ d = 0 and d(ω ∧ η) = dω ∧ η + (−1)ⁱ ω ∧ dη, the relative de Rham complex Ω•_{X/Y}. Conventions: this is the coherent sheaf of the continuous differentials of R0 (Huber 1996 (1.6.2)); Mathlib's algebraic KaehlerDifferential of the rings O_X(U) is not the object (it is not finitely generated). The Kähler differentials of rigid and dagger spaces (Grosse-Klönne) and the log differentials of Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu with trivial log structures are the same sheaf. The sheaf on the étale site in (c) and the pro-étale sheaves built from it are AdicEtaleGeometry A2's and PadicHodgeTheory's.

Hypotheses

  • f: X → Y locally of finite type; X, Y locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (every point has an affinoid neighbourhood with a strongly noetherian complete Tate ring)
  • For (b): the second morphism locally of finite type; for (c): f unramified, smooth or étale as in R0; for (d): the hypotheses of R0/fibre-products-existence, case (a)

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheaf-of-continuous-differentials

The GAGA comparison maps on cohomology and higher direct imagesconstruction

Let K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X and F an 𝒪_X-module with analytification F^an (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-of-modules). The comparison map c_F : Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an) is the composite of Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X, ι_*ι*F) (the unit F → ι_*ι*F) with the edge map Hⁱ(X, ι_*F^an) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an); it is A-linear and δ-functorial in F. For f : X → Y over Spec A, the relative comparison map (Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an) is the adjoint of the sheafified map V ↦ [Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) → Hⁱ((f^an)⁻¹V^an, F^an)], δ-functorial in F and compatible with composition in f. These maps are isomorphisms for proper f and coherent F (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga) and not in general.

Hypotheses

  • K a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value and A an affinoid K-algebra (A = K allowed); X is a scheme locally of finite type over Spec A, X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°) its relative analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification; for A = K AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-functor) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces ι_X : X^an → X

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/gaga-comparison-map

Trace of endomorphisms of finite projective modulesconstruction

Let R be a commutative ring and M a finitely generated projective R-module. The trace tr_M : End_R(M) → R is the R-linear map tr_M = contractLeft ∘ (dualTensorHomEquiv R M M)⁻¹, where dualTensorHomEquiv : M^∨ ⊗_R M ≅ End_R(M) (Mathlib, for M finite projective) and contractLeft(φ ⊗ m) = φ(m). Convention: this is the trace used throughout R3; Mathlib's LinearMap.trace R M agrees with it when M is free but is defined to be 0 when M has no finite basis, so it is not the trace of a finite projective non-free module.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative
  • M finite projective over R

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/projective-module-trace

The trace of a finite locally free algebraconstruction

Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra which is finitely generated and projective as an R-module (a finite locally free R-algebra). The trace Tr_{B/R} : B → R is b ↦ tr_B(m_b), the projective-module trace (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/projective-module-trace) of multiplication by b. It is R-linear, Tr_{B/R}(1) is the locally constant degree function (its image in R_𝔭 is rank_𝔭 B), and the trace form (x, y) ↦ Tr_{B/R}(xy) is symmetric. It is not defined as a sum over geometric points: for B = k[x]/(x²), Tr(1) = 2 although Spec B has one geometric point.

Hypotheses

  • R commutative
  • B finite projective as an R-module

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace

The trace of a finite locally free morphism of schemesconstruction

Let π : X → Y be a finite locally free morphism of schemes (Mathlib: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite, Flat and LocallyOfFinitePresentation). The trace Tr_π : π_*𝒪_X → 𝒪_Y is the 𝒪_Y-linear map which on every affine open V = Spec A ⊆ Y with π⁻¹(V) = Spec B is Tr_{B/A} (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace); these glue because the affine formula is compatible with localisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change). Tr_π ∘ π^♯ is multiplication by the locally constant degree of π.

Hypotheses

  • π finite locally free

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/scheme-trace-finite-locally-free

Pull–identify–trace operators along correspondencesconstruction

A correspondence from Y to X is an adic space C with morphisms q : C → Y and p : C → X, p finite locally free. Given vector bundles (or, on locally noetherian analytic spaces, coherent sheaves) E_Y on Y and E_X on X and an 𝒪_C-linear identification φ : q*E_Y → p*E_X, the pull–identify–trace operator T = T(C, φ) : Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) → Hⁱ(X, E_X) is the composite Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) →(q*) Hⁱ(C, q*E_Y) →(φ) Hⁱ(C, p*E_X) = Hⁱ(X, p_*p*E_X) = Hⁱ(X, p_*𝒪_C ⊗ E_X) →(Tr_p ⊗ id) Hⁱ(X, E_X), using that p is finite (p_* exact on coherent / vector bundles) and the projection formula. No normalising factor is included; consumers multiply by their own constants (e.g. 1/q_a in BHW).

Hypotheses

  • p finite locally free
  • q arbitrary
  • φ an 𝒪_C-linear map q*E_Y → p*E_X

AdicSpacesPartII:R3/pull-identify-trace

R4Étale and pro-étale sites

Normal crossings divisordefinitionplanetSmooth pairs: a smooth adic space with a strict normal crossings divisor

Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field and B^n_K := Spa(K⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, K°⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩) the closed unit polydisc (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc). A smooth pair over K is a pair (X, D) where X is an adic space smooth over Spa(K, K°) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism) and D ⊆ X is a closed adic subspace with ideal sheaf I_D ⊆ O_X (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings) such that every x ∈ X has a strict normal crossings chart: an open neighbourhood V of x, integers 0 ≤ r ≤ n and an étale morphism h: V -> B^n_K with I_D|_V = h^*(T_1 ⋯ T_r)·O_V (so D ∩ V = h^{-1}(V(T_1 ⋯ T_r)); r = 0 means D ∩ V = ∅). The boundary complement is the open subspace U := X ∖ D with its open immersion j: U -> X. Conventions: 'strict' means that charts exist on an open cover of X over K itself; the normal crossings divisors of Diao-Lan-Liu-Zhu (charts étale-locally, equivalently analytic-locally after a finite separable extension of K) form the weaker class and are not smooth pairs in this sense unless charts exist over K. D is reduced and an effective Cartier divisor. No condition is imposed on irreducible components, and r may vary with x.

Hypotheses

  • X smooth over Spa(K, K°): locally of finite type (hence locally noetherian and analytic) and smooth in R0's sense.
  • Charts are analytic-local on X and defined over K; h is étale in R0's sense.

AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair

Restriction of the étale and pro-étale sites of a smooth pair to its boundary complementconstruction

Let (X, D) be a smooth pair over K (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair) with boundary complement j: U = X ∖ D -> X. Construct: (a) U as an object of X_ét and the equivalence of sites U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-slice-site), under which the morphism of sites j_ét: U_ét -> X_ét of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality is the slice morphism; (b) the functors on sheaves of sets and of abelian groups j^{-1}F = F|_U with (j^{-1}F)(V) = F(V) for V ∈ U_ét, j_*G with (j_*G)(W) = G(W ×_X U), and j_! (extension by zero for abelian sheaves), the sheafification of the presheaf W ↦ G(W) if W -> X factors through U and W ↦ 0 otherwise; with adjunctions j_! ⊣ j^{-1} ⊣ j_* and canonical isomorphisms j^{-1} j_* ≅ id ≅ j^{-1} j_! (j is a monomorphism); (c) the same on the pro-étale sites, U_proét ≃ X_proét/U (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/proetale-slice-open-subspace), with j_proét compatible with ν: ν_X ∘ j_proét corresponds to j_ét ∘ ν_U. The inclusion j is in general not quasi-compact (for (B^1, V(T)) the complement is not quasi-compact), so no base-change or continuity statement requiring a qcqs morphism (such as Scholze Corollary 3.17(ii) for j) is part of this construction; exactness properties and derived functors of j_!, j_* belong to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.

Hypotheses

  • (X, D) a smooth pair; only the ordinary (non-logarithmic) sites are restricted here.
  • Sheaves of sets and abelian groups; j_! only for sheaves with a zero object (abelian groups, modules).

AdicSpacesPartII:R4/boundary-complement-restriction

R5Families and sousperfectoid spaces

Sousperfectoid ringdefinitionplanetSousperfectoid Tate rings and perfectoid frames

Fix a prime p. Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing) in which p is topologically nilpotent (equivalently, a Tate ring with a continuous ring map Z_p -> R: a complete Tate Z_p-algebra). A perfectoid frame for R is a triple (R̃, ι, σ) consisting of a perfectoid Tate ring R̃ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: complete, uniform, with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ such that ϖ^p divides p in R̃° and Frobenius R̃°/ϖ -> R̃°/ϖ^p is bijective), a continuous ring homomorphism ι: R -> R̃, and a continuous R-linear map σ: R̃ -> R (R̃ an R-module through ι) with σ ∘ ι = id_R. R is sousperfectoid if it admits a perfectoid frame; a Huber pair (R, R⁺) is sousperfectoid if R is. Conventions: ι is then injective and a homeomorphism onto the closed subring ι(R) = ker(id - ι∘σ); σ need not be multiplicative and need not map any ring of integral elements into R⁺; no perfectoid base field is fixed, and R̃ is not required to contain one; characteristic p is allowed (then R̃ is a perfect complete Tate ring).

Hypotheses

  • R complete and Hausdorff (anchor convention 3), Tate, p topologically nilpotent in R.
  • The splitting is in topological R-modules: σ is continuous and R-linear.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring

Sousperfectoid spacedefinitionplanetSousperfectoid adic spaces

An adic space X (anchor Layer 5: an object of Huber's category 𝒱 covered by affinoid adic spaces) is sousperfectoid if it admits an open cover by affinoid adic spaces Spa(R, R⁺) with R sousperfectoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring); such Spa(R, R⁺) are adic spaces by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-sheafy. Equivalently, the open affinoid subspaces Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X with R sousperfectoid form a basis of the topology of X. A sousperfectoid space is analytic (its charts are Tate). A morphism of sousperfectoid spaces is a morphism of adic spaces.

Hypotheses

  • No base is fixed; X lives over Spa Z_p because p is topologically nilpotent on every chart.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space

Completed tensor product with a profinite moduleconstructionplanetThe mixed completed tensor product V ⊗̂ M (CHJ §6.1)

Let E be a finite extension of Q_p with O = O_E, ϖ a uniformizer, and M a profinite flat O-module. For an O-module X define X ⊗̂ M := lim_i (X ⊗_O M/I_i), the limit over any cofinal system (I_i) of open O-submodules of M (CHJ Definition 6.3; independent of the system). For an E-vector space V with an O-lattice V° ⊆ V (V°[1/ϖ] = V) define V ⊗̂ M := (V° ⊗̂ M)[1/ϖ] (CHJ Definition 6.6). When V is an E-Banach space, V° is always taken open and bounded, and V ⊗̂ M is then canonically independent of V°. Suppose V is a Banach E-algebra and M carries an O-algebra structure for which 0 has a basis of open ideals. (CHJ call this a "small O-algebra" without defining it. Examples: a small Z_p-algebra when E = Q_p, or an O-algebra that is reduced, ϖ-torsion-free and finite over O[[X_1, ..., X_d]].) Then choosing V° an open bounded subring and the I_i ideals makes V ⊗̂ M a ring. It is a Banach E-algebra with unit ball V° ⊗̂ M, and with a pseudobasis (e_i) of M it is, as a Banach space, the space of bounded I-indexed families in V.

Hypotheses

  • M profinite flat; V Banach over E with open bounded lattice V° (for non-Banach V the lattice is part of the data and affects the result).

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor

Profinite flat modules over the ring of integers of a p-adic fielddefinition

Let E be a finite extension of Q_p, O = O_E with uniformizer ϖ. A topological O-module M is linear-topological if 0 has a basis of neighbourhoods consisting of O-submodules (mathlib IsLinearTopology O M), and M is a profinite flat O-module if it is flat over O (equivalently ϖ-torsion-free), linear-topological, compact and Hausdorff (CHJ Definition 6.1; CHJ's "compact" includes Hausdorff). Then the topology of M is profinite, every open submodule has finite index, and M is ϖ-adically complete and separated.

Hypotheses

  • O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field (E/Q_p finite).

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/profinite-flat-module

Small Z_p-algebrasdefinition

A small Z_p-algebra (CHJ §1.4) is a ring R that is reduced, p-torsion-free and finite as an algebra over Z_p[[X_1, ..., X_d]] for some d ≥ 0. It carries its canonical adic profinite topology (the a-adic topology for an ideal of definition a, e.g. the Jacobson radical, independent of choices), for which it is a profinite flat Z_p-module (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/profinite-flat-module) and a noetherian semilocal ring, complete for its p-adic topology.

Hypotheses

  • d unspecified; all constructions are independent of the choice of d and of the ideal of definition.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/small-coefficient-algebra

Coherent R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.18)definition

Let K be a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p, X affinoid rigid over K, R small. For a rational U ⊆ X and a finite rational cover 𝔘 of U, a sheaf F of R|_U-modules is 𝔘-coherent if for every U_i ∈ 𝔘 there is a finitely generated R(U_i)-module M_i with F|_{U_i} ≅ Loc(M_i). F is coherent if it is 𝔘-coherent for some finite rational cover 𝔘. F is locally projective if the M_i can be chosen projective.

Hypotheses

  • K discretely valued (so that Loc is exact and fully faithful).

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-coherent-module

The product X ×_L Y of a perfectoid space and a smooth rigid space (BHW Corollary 3.4)construction

Let L be a perfectoid field, L' a perfectoid field extension of L (complete, with L -> L' continuous), X a perfectoid space over L and Y a rigid space over L' (an adic space locally of topologically finite type over Spa(L', O_L')) that is smooth over L' (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism). Then the fibre product X ×_L Y := X ×_{Spa(L, O_L)} Y exists in the category of adic spaces and is a sousperfectoid adic space. Construction: X ×_L Y = X' ×_{L'} Y with X' = X ×_L Spa(L', O_L') perfectoid; for affinoid perfectoid X' = Spa(S, S⁺) and an open V ⊆ Y with an étale map h: V -> B^n_{L'} (Huber 1.6.10), X' ×_{L'} V = (X' ×_{L'} B^n_{L'}) ×_{B^n_{L'}} V with X' ×_{L'} B^n = Spa(S⟨T_1, ..., T_n⟩, S⁺⟨T⟩); these pieces glue. It is not asserted, and is false in general, that X ×_L Y is perfectoid.

Hypotheses

  • L, L' perfectoid fields (BHW: L a perfectoid extension of Q_p^cyc); the printed hypothesis 'a perfectoid extension of L'/L' means 'a perfectoid extension L' of L' (sourceIssues).
  • Y smooth over L' (so locally étale over polydiscs); X arbitrary perfectoid over L.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product

The coefficient sheaf R = O_X ⊗̂ R on an affinoid rigid space (CHJ §6.3)construction

Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field extension of Q_p, X = Spa(A, A°) an affinoid rigid space over K and R a small Z_p-algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/small-coefficient-algebra). On the site of rational subsets of X with finite rational covers, define R(U) := O_X(U) ⊗̂ R. This is the mixed completed tensor over Z_p of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/mixed-completed-tensor, computed with an open bounded subring of the Banach Q_p-algebra O_X(U); by lattice independence the result does not depend on that choice. Restriction maps are induced by those of O_X, which are bounded. Each R(U) is a Banach K-algebra and the restriction maps are continuous K-algebra maps, so R is a presheaf of Banach K-algebras on the rational site. That R is a sheaf, with vanishing higher Čech cohomology, is the separate theorem AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-tate-acyclicity; it then extends to all quasi-compact opens by finite covers. When X is reduced the unit ball of R(U) can be taken to be O_X°(U) ⊗̂ R (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/rational-integral-compatibility); for non-reduced X it cannot (packet sourceIssue E28).

Hypotheses

  • K a complete nonarchimedean extension of Q_p (characteristic 0 alone is not enough); X affinoid for this node (qcqs X by gluing on finite covers).
  • No discreteness of K is needed for the construction; it is needed for noetherianity, flatness, Loc and Kiehl.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/completed-coefficient-sheaf

The localisation functor Loc for R-modules (CHJ Definition 6.14, Proposition 6.16)construction

Let X be affinoid rigid over a complete nonarchimedean extension K of Q_p, R small, U ⊆ X rational and M a finitely generated R(U)-module. Loc(M) is the presheaf of R|_U-modules V ↦ R(V) ⊗_{R(U)} M on rational V ⊆ U. If K is discretely valued: Loc is a fully faithful exact functor from finitely generated R(U)-modules to R-modules on U, Loc(M) is a sheaf, and Ȟ^i(𝔘, Loc(M)) = 0 = H^i(U, Loc(M)) for i ≥ 1 and every finite rational cover 𝔘. If K is not discretely valued, Loc(M) is still a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology when M is finitely generated projective.

Hypotheses

  • Finitely generated modules; discreteness of K for general M.

AdicSpacesPartII:R5/coefficient-sheaf-loc

F0Formal geometry integrated with R0–R3

Formal schemedefinitionplanetFormal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes

A formal scheme (of finite ideal type) is a locally ringed space X such that every point has an open neighbourhood U with (U, O_X|_U) isomorphic, as a locally ringed space, to Spf A for some adic ring A of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum); such U are the affine formal opens. X is locally noetherian if every point has an affine formal open neighbourhood Spf A with A noetherian, and noetherian if moreover its underlying space is quasi-compact (EGA I, 10.4.2). Morphisms of formal schemes are morphisms of locally ringed spaces; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence they are automatically continuous on rings of sections, so this category agrees with EGA's category of formal preschemes of this type (EGA I, 10.4.5). Pinned conventions: (1) 'scheme' means Mathlib's Scheme (EGA's préschéma; no separatedness); (2) the topology on Γ(U, O_X) for an affine formal open U is recovered, not stored: it is the J-adic topology for any finitely generated ideal J ⊆ Γ(U, O_X) whose radical is the ideal of sections vanishing at every point of U; (3) every scheme is a formal scheme (take A discrete) and Scheme → FormalScheme is fully faithful (EGA I, 10.4.8).

Hypotheses

  • affine pieces Spf A with A adic of finite ideal type; for 'locally noetherian' the A are noetherian

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme

Formal spectrumconstructionplanetThe formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring

Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) with ideal of definition I. The formal spectrum Spf A is the locally ringed space defined as follows. Its underlying space is the closed subspace of Spec A consisting of the open prime ideals, which is V(I) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus I and is homeomorphic to Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) for every n via the quotient maps (EGA I, 10.1.1–10.1.2). For each n let O_n be the structure sheaf of Spec(A ⧸ I^{n+1}) transported to V(I); the structure sheaf is O_{Spf A} := lim_n O_n, the limit in sheaves of commutative rings along the reduction maps. Then: Γ(Spf A, O) ≅ A (EGA I, 10.1.3); for f ∈ A and D(f) := D(f) ∩ V(I), Γ(D(f), O) ≅ A_{f} (the completed localisation, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization) and (D(f), O|_{D(f)}) ≅ Spf A_{f} (EGA I, 10.1.4); the stalk at an open prime p is colim_{f ∉ p} A_{f}, a local ring with residue field Frac(A ⧸ p), noetherian when A is noetherian (EGA I, 10.1.6). A continuous homomorphism φ : B → A induces a morphism of locally ringed spaces Spf φ : Spf A → Spf B, q ↦ φ⁻¹(q) (EGA I, 10.2.1). Convention: Spf A is a locally ringed space (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace); the topology of the rings of sections is not part of the data (see AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme), and for quasi-compact open U the ring Γ(U, O) carries the limit topology of the discrete rings Γ(U, O_n), recorded as an API item.

Hypotheses

  • A adic of finite ideal type; noetherianity only for the noetherian statements (noetherian stalks)
  • φ continuous for functoriality

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum

Formal completionconstructionplanetThe formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme and X′ ⊆ X a closed subset. Let 𝓘 ⊆ O_X be a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′ (for example the ideal of the reduced induced closed subscheme). The formal completion X̂ = X̂_{/X′} is the locally noetherian formal scheme ofThickenings(V(𝓘^{n+1}))_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings): its underlying space is X′ and O_X̂ = lim_n (O_X/𝓘^{n+1})|_{X′}. It does not depend on 𝓘: all such ideals form a filtered set Φ, and on noetherian opens the powers of any one member are cofinal in Φ (EGA I, 10.8.2); 𝓘O_X̂ is an ideal of definition. For X = Spec A (A noetherian) and X′ = V(I): X̂ ≅ Spf Â where Â = AdicCompletion I A with the I-adic topology (EGA I, 10.8.5). Further: X̂_red is the reduced closed subscheme with space X′; X̂ is noetherian iff X′ is quasi-compact (EGA I, 10.8.6); there is a canonical morphism of locally ringed spaces i_X : X̂ → X (the inclusion of X′ with O_X → i_*O_X̂ the limit of the quotient maps) (EGA I, 10.8.7), which is flat (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact); for U ⊆ X open, Û_{/U∩X′} is the open formal subscheme of X̂ on U ∩ X′; for X′ = X, X̂ = X.

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian scheme (Mathlib IsLocallyNoetherian)
  • X′ closed subset; 𝓘 quasi-coherent of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion

Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definitiondefinition

Let A be a commutative topological ring. An ideal J of A is an ideal of definition when J is open and every neighbourhood of 0 contains J^n for some n ≥ 1 (EGA 0, 7.1.2). The ring A is an adic ring of finite ideal type, written IsAdicRing A, when there is a finitely generated ideal I of A such that the topology of A is the I-adic topology (Mathlib IsAdic I: the powers I^n are open and form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0) and A is I-adically separated and complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete I A). An adic noetherian ring is an adic ring of finite ideal type whose underlying ring is noetherian; then every ideal of definition is finitely generated. Conventions: completeness always includes separatedness; the topology is part of the data, so k⟦t⟧ with the discrete topology and k⟦t⟧ with the t-adic topology are different adic rings; morphisms of adic rings are continuous ring homomorphisms. For I as above, an ideal J is an ideal of definition if and only if IsAdic J holds, if and only if J is open and J^n ⊆ I for some n (EGA 0, 7.1.4(i)); so every statement below may use any ideal of definition.

Hypotheses

  • A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring
  • the witnessing ideal I is finitely generated (automatic when A is noetherian)
  • IsAdicComplete I A: separated and complete for the I-adic filtration

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring

Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_ndefinition

Let X be a formal scheme. An ideal-sheaf datum on X is, as in Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData, an ideal 𝒥(U) ⊆ Γ(U, O_X) for each affine formal open U, with 𝒥(D(f)) = 𝒥(U)·A_{f} for basic opens (it is the sheaf 𝒥(U)^Δ on U). It is an ideal of definition when 𝒥(U) is an ideal of definition of the adic ring Γ(U, O_X) for every affine formal open U; it suffices to check this on an affine formal open cover (EGA I, 10.3.3, 10.3.5, 10.5.1). For an ideal of definition 𝒥: (X, O_X/𝒥) is a scheme X_𝒥 (affine if X is, locally noetherian if X is), with a canonical morphism X_𝒥 → X which is a homeomorphism on spaces (EGA I, 10.5.2); O_X = lim_n O_X/𝒥^{n+1} (EGA I, 10.5.3). Notation: X_n := (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), n ≥ 0. If X is locally noetherian: the powers 𝒥^{n+1} are ideals of definition and form a fundamental system; there is a largest ideal of definition 𝒯, the unique one with X_𝒯 reduced, 𝒯(U) = √(𝒥(U)) = sections vanishing at every point, and X_red := X_𝒯 (EGA I, 10.5.1, 10.5.4).

Hypotheses

  • X a formal scheme; the largest ideal of definition and the power statements need X locally noetherian

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition

Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemesdefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is adic if there is an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y such that f*(𝒦)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X; then f*(𝒦′)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X for every ideal of definition 𝒦′ of Y (EGA I, 10.12.1). An adic formal scheme over S is a locally noetherian formal S-scheme with adic structure morphism; every S-morphism between adic S-formal schemes is adic. For affine X = Spf A, Y = Spf B, f = Spf φ is adic iff I_B·A is an ideal of definition of A (IsAdic (I_B.map φ)). Notation: for ideals of definition 𝒦 of Y and 𝒥 of X with f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, f_n : X_n → Y_n denotes the reduction modulo 𝒥^{n+1}, 𝒦^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems). Characterisation: f is adic iff for some such pair (𝒦, 𝒥) every square X_m → X_n over Y_m → Y_n (m ≤ n) is cartesian, i.e. X_m = X_n ×_{Y_n} Y_m; in that case 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X (EGA I, 10.12.3 and the proof of 10.12.3.1). (With 𝒥 replaced by f*(𝒦)O_X for a non-adic f the quotients (X, O_X/f*(𝒦^{n+1})O_X) are not schemes — e.g. F_p⟦T⟧ on the one-point space of Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ — so the ideal must be an ideal of definition.)

Hypotheses

  • X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes

Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemesdefinition

Let Y be a locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition 𝒦 and f : X → Y a morphism of formal schemes. f is of finite type if X is locally noetherian, f is adic, and the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) with 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X is a morphism of schemes of finite type (Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact) (EGA I, 10.13.1 (a), 10.13.3). Equivalent conditions: (b) X is locally noetherian and the colimit of an adic system (X_n) over (Y_n) with X_0 → Y_0 of finite type; (c) every point of Y has a noetherian affine formal neighbourhood V = Spf B such that f⁻¹(V) is a finite union of noetherian affine formal opens Spf A_i with each A_i ≅ B{T_1,…,T_r}/𝔞 topologically (EGA I, 10.13.1). The condition does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n is of finite type. Affine criterion: Spf A → Spf B (noetherian) is of finite type iff A is topologically a quotient of some B{T} (EGA I, 10.13.4). The local variant f locally of finite type (Huber’s notion used in R2) drops quasi-compactness of f_0.

Hypotheses

  • Y locally noetherian; 'finite type' of schemes includes quasi-compactness (EGA I, 6.3.1)

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type

Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemesdefinition

A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is proper if f is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type) and, for an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y and 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X, the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) is a proper morphism of schemes (Mathlib IsProper) (EGA III, 3.4.1). This does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n : X_n → Y_n is proper. A closed subset Z of X is proper over Y if, viewed in X_0, it is proper over Y_0 (the reduced closed subscheme on Z is proper over Y_0). For a proper morphism g : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes, a closed subset Y′ ⊆ Y and X′ = g⁻¹(Y′), the completion ĝ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} is proper (EGA III, 3.4.1).

Hypotheses

  • X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism

Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal schemedefinition

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme. An O_X-module is a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of rings O_X (Mathlib SheafOfModules over TauCeti.SheafOfModules.ringCatSheaf of the structure sheaf). It is coherent if it is locally finitely presented (Mathlib SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation). Coh(X) denotes the full subcategory of coherent O_X-modules. The topology Γ(U, F) = lim Γ(U, F ⊗ O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) is not part of the data. The following facts are theorems proved downstream, not part of the definition (their proofs use AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence and AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system, which themselves depend on this definition): O_X is a coherent sheaf of rings, so the definition agrees with EGA's coherence (EGA I, 10.10.3, 10.11.1); Coh(X) is abelian and closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions, ⊗ and internal Hom; every ideal of definition is coherent; morphisms of coherent modules are automatically continuous (EGA I, 10.11.6); f* preserves coherence — all in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module-properties.

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian formal scheme

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module

The completed localisation A_{f} of an adic ringconstruction

Let A be an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I and let f ∈ A. The completed localisation is A_{f} := AdicCompletion (I·A_f) A_f, where A_f = Localization.Away f, with the I·A_{f}-adic topology; equivalently A_{f} = lim_n (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f (EGA 0, 7.6.1–7.6.2, 7.6.15). It does not depend on the choice of I. The canonical map A → A_{f} is continuous and sends f to a unit; it has the universal property: every continuous ring homomorphism u : A → B into a complete separated linearly topologised ring B with u(f) a unit factors uniquely through a continuous homomorphism A_{f} → B (EGA 0, 7.6.6). A_{f} is an adic ring of finite ideal type with ideal of definition I·A_{f}, and A_{f} ⧸ I^{n+1}A_{f} ≅ (A ⧸ I^{n+1})_f; if A is noetherian then A_{f} is noetherian and flat over A (EGA 0, 7.6.11, 7.6.13). For g a multiple of f in A (g ∈ √(fA) mod I suffices) there is a unique continuous A-algebra map A_{f} → A_{g}.

Hypotheses

  • A adic of finite ideal type (IsAdicRing A), with ideal of definition I
  • f ∈ A arbitrary; A_{f} = 0 exactly when f is nilpotent modulo I

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization

Completed tensor product of adic rings of finite ideal typeconstruction

Let φ : A → B and ψ : A → C be continuous homomorphisms of adic rings of finite ideal type, with ideals of definition I_B ⊆ B and I_C ⊆ C. Let J ⊆ B ⊗_A C be the ideal generated by I_B ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ I_C (finitely generated). The completed tensor product is B ⊗̂_A C := AdicCompletion J (B ⊗_A C) with its J-adic topology. It is an adic ring of finite ideal type (ideal of definition J·(B ⊗̂_A C)), independent of the choice of I_B, I_C, and B ⊗̂_A C ⧸ J^{n+1} ≅ (B ⧸ I_B^{n+1}) ⊗_{A} (C ⧸ I_C^{n+1}) modulo J^{n+1}. Universal property (EGA 0, 7.7.6, used in EGA I, 10.7.2): the canonical continuous maps B → B ⊗̂_A C ← C induce a bijection between continuous A-algebra maps B ⊗̂_A C → D and pairs of continuous A-algebra maps (B → D, C → D), for every adic ring D of finite ideal type (more generally every complete separated linearly topologised A-algebra D). Warning: B ⊗̂_A C need not be noetherian when B and C are (EGA I, 10.7.4); it is noetherian when B is topologically of finite type over A and C is noetherian (EGA I, 10.13.5).

Hypotheses

  • A, B, C adic rings of finite ideal type; φ, ψ continuous (not necessarily adic)
  • noetherianity of the result only under the finite-type hypothesis of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic

Gluing formal schemes along open subschemesconstruction

A glue datum of formal schemes is a glue datum of locally ringed spaces (Mathlib LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData: pieces U_i, open immersions V_ij → U_i, isomorphisms t_ij : V_ij ≅ V_ji with the cocycle condition) in which every U_i is a formal scheme. The glued locally ringed space X is a formal scheme; each ι_i : U_i → X is an open immersion with image covering X; X is locally noetherian if every U_i is, and noetherian if moreover the index set is finite and every U_i is noetherian. Universal property: morphisms X → Y of formal schemes correspond to families of morphisms f_i : U_i → Y agreeing on the V_ij (EGA 0, 4.1.7; EGA I, 10.4.2 is local, and EGA I, 10.7.3 constructs products by gluing affine pieces as in the scheme case). Gluing commutes with FormalScheme.ofScheme (Mathlib Scheme.GlueData).

Hypotheses

  • pieces are formal schemes (finite ideal type); cocycle condition of Mathlib GlueData

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing

The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickeningsconstruction

An adic thickening system is a sequence of schemes X_0 → X_1 → X_2 → ⋯ with closed immersions u_n : X_n → X_{n+1} that are homeomorphisms on underlying spaces, such that, writing O_n for the structure sheaves on the common space T and 𝒥_n = ker(O_n → O_0): (a) 𝒥_n is locally nilpotent; (b) ker(O_n → O_m) = 𝒥_n^{m+1} for m ≤ n; (c) 𝒥_1 = 𝒥_1/𝒥_1² is an O_0-module of finite type. Then the locally ringed space X := (T, lim_n O_n) is a formal scheme; the maps lim O_k → O_n are surjective; 𝒥 := ker(lim O_k → O_0) is an ideal of definition with ker(lim O_k → O_n) = 𝒥^{n+1} and 𝒥/𝒥² ≅ 𝒥_1; the canonical morphisms ι_n : X_n → X form a cocone; X is locally noetherian (resp. noetherian) when X_0 is (EGA I, 10.6.3–10.6.4). On affine opens: if X_0 = Spec A_0 then every X_n = Spec A_n and X = Spf(lim A_n), with lim A_n adic of ideal of definition ker(lim A_n → A_0) (EGA 0, 7.2.7). EGA 10.6.3 without (b)–(c) produces formal preschemes that need not be of finite ideal type; those are outside this carrier.

Hypotheses

  • closed immersions X_n → X_{n+1} that are homeomorphisms, with locally nilpotent kernels
  • adic conditions (b) and (c) (EGA I, 10.6.4)

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings

Closed formal subschemes and closed immersionsconstruction

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module). Its support Y = Supp(O_X/𝒜) is closed and (Y, (O_X/𝒜)|_Y) is a locally noetherian formal scheme, noetherian if X is (EGA I, 10.14.1): the closed formal subscheme X.subscheme 𝒜, with canonical morphism j : X.subscheme 𝒜 → X. The assignment 𝒜 ↦ X.subscheme 𝒜 is a bijection from coherent ideals onto closed formal subschemes. A closed immersion is a morphism isomorphic over X to some j (EGA I, 10.14.2). On X = Spf A (A adic noetherian) every coherent ideal is 𝔞^Δ for an ideal 𝔞 of A and Spf A.subscheme 𝔞^Δ ≅ Spf(A/𝔞), with j = Spf of the quotient map. Closed immersions are adic and of finite type (EGA I, 10.14.3); for a locally noetherian scheme X with closed subset X′ and a closed subscheme Z of X, the completion Ẑ_{/Z∩X′} is the closed formal subscheme of X̂ defined by the completed ideal (EGA I, 10.14.7, used in EGA III, 5.1.8).

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian formal scheme; 𝒜 coherent ideal of O_X

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme

Extension of a morphism to formal completionsconstruction

Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian schemes and X′ ⊆ X, Y′ ⊆ Y closed with f(X′) ⊆ Y′. There is a unique morphism of formal schemes f̂ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} with i_Y ∘ f̂ = f ∘ i_X; it is the colimit of the morphisms V(𝓘^{n+1}) → V(𝓚^{n+1}) induced by f for ideals with f*(𝓚)O_X ⊆ 𝓘, and does not depend on the ideals (EGA I, 10.9.1–10.9.2). On underlying spaces f̂ is the restriction of f to X′. Functoriality: (g ∘ f)^ = ĝ ∘ f̂ and id^ = id (EGA I, 10.9.3). Affine case: for f = Spec φ, φ : B → A, f̂ = Spf φ̂ with φ̂ : B̂ → Â the continuous extension (EGA I, 10.9.1). Base change: if X′ = f⁻¹(Y′) then X̂ ≅ X ×_Y Ŷ as formal schemes, where X is viewed as a formal scheme (EGA I, 10.9.9), and f̂ is adic; completion commutes with fibre products (EGA I, 10.9.7).

Hypotheses
