  • X, Y locally noetherian; f(X′) ⊆ Y′
  • base change statement needs X′ = f⁻¹(Y′); product statement needs X ×_S Y locally noetherian

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism

Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subsetconstruction

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme, X′ ⊆ X closed with completion X̂ = X̂_{/X′}, and F a coherent O_X-module. The completion of F along X′ is F̂ = F_{/X′} := lim_n (F ⊗_{O_X} O_X/𝓘^{n+1})|_{X′} for any 𝓘 of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′; it is independent of 𝓘, a coherent O_X̂-module, and its sections over X̂ are the formal sections of F along X′ (EGA I, 10.8.4). For quasi-compact open U, Γ(U ∩ X′, F̂) = lim_n Γ(U, F/𝓘^{n+1}F). A morphism u : F → G induces û : F̂ → Ĝ, (v ∘ u)^ = v̂ ∘ û, so completion is an additive functor Coh(X) → Coh(X̂). For X = Spec A, F = M~ with M finite: Γ(X̂, F̂) = M̂ = AdicCompletion I M ≅ M ⊗_A Â (EGA I, 10.8.4, 10.10.1; EGA 0, 7.3.3). There is a canonical functorial isomorphism i_X*(F) ≅ F̂, and completion is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact). Completion is compatible with ⊗ and Hom: (F ⊗ G)^ ≅ F̂ ⊗ Ĝ, Hom(F, G)^ ≅ Hom(F̂, Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.8.10), and with pullback: for f : X → Y and coherent G on Y, (f*G)^ ≅ f̂*(Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.9.5).

Hypotheses

  • X locally noetherian; F coherent (Mathlib-level: a finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-module)

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf

The coherent module M^Δ on Spf A attached to a finite A-moduleconstruction

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, X = Spec A and 𝔛 = Spf A, identified with the completion X̂_{/V(I)} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, specIso). For a finite A-module M, M^Δ := (M~)^ is the completion along V(I) of the coherent sheaf M~ on X (EGA I, 10.10.1). Its sections are Γ(D(f) ∩ 𝔛, M^Δ) = M ⊗_A A_{f} = lim_n (M/I^{n+1}M)_f; an A-linear map u : M → N gives u^Δ : M^Δ → N^Δ, so M ↦ M^Δ is an additive functor from finite A-modules to coherent O_𝔛-modules. For A discrete, M^Δ = M~ (Mathlib tilde).

Hypotheses

  • A adic noetherian; M finite

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module

Internal Hom of sheaves of modules; compatibility of ⊗ and ℋom with pullback and with M ↦ M~constructionadded in review

Let (X, O_X) be a ringed space (a scheme, or a locally noetherian formal scheme with its sheaf of rings TauCeti.SheafOfModules.ringCatSheaf) and F, G sheaves of O_X-modules. (a) The internal Hom ℋom_{O_X}(F, G) is the sheaf of O_X-modules U ↦ Hom_{O_U}(F|_U, G|_U) (EGA 0, 4.1.5); Γ(X, ℋom(F, G)) = Hom_{O_X}(F, G), ℋom is left exact in each variable and ℋom(O_X, G) = G. (b) For every morphism of ringed spaces f : Y → X, f*(F ⊗ G) ≅ f*F ⊗ f*G canonically (EGA 0, 4.3.3.1; ⊗ is Tau Ceti SheafOfModules.tensorProduct, f* is Mathlib SheafOfModules.pullback). (c) If F is of finite presentation and f is flat, the canonical map f*ℋom(F, G) → ℋom(f*F, f*G) is an isomorphism (EGA 0, 6.7.6). (d) On Spec A, (M ⊗_A N)~ ≅ M~ ⊗ N~, and Hom_A(M, N)~ ≅ ℋom(M~, N~) when M is finitely presented (EGA I, 1.3.12); hence on a locally noetherian scheme ⊗ and ℋom of coherent modules are coherent. (The formal-scheme analogue is recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module and deduced from the affine case.)

Hypotheses

  • F of finite presentation for the flat-pullback isomorphism; coherence statements on locally noetherian (formal) schemes

Added during review; not yet independently checked

AdicSpacesPartII:F0/internal-hom-sheaf-of-modules

F1Dagger geometry and overconvergent de Rham complexes

Dagger algebradefinitionplanetDagger algebras over a complete nonarchimedean field

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). A K-dagger algebra is a commutative K-algebra A for which there exist n ∈ ℕ and a surjective K-algebra homomorphism W_n → A (equivalently A ≅ W_n/I for an ideal I). A morphism of dagger algebras is a K-algebra homomorphism (no continuity is imposed; it is automatic, F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity). Sp(A) denotes the set of maximal ideals of A. Attached data, each independent of the presentation up to canonical isomorphism: the residue norm class of a presentation (F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity), the completion A → Â (written A' by Grosse-Klönne), Â = T_n/IT_n, a K-affinoid algebra (F1/dagger-completion-comparison), the supremum seminorm |a|_sup = max_{m ∈ Sp(A)} |a mod m|, and the integral subring A^int = {a ∈ A : |a|_sup ≤ 1} = A ∩ (Â)°, which is the ring of power-bounded elements of A.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra

Dagger spacedefinitionplanetDagger spaces (rigid spaces with overconvergent structure sheaf)

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Rigid spaces are, throughout, the quasi-separated Tate rigid-analytic spaces over K of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space (G-topological spaces locally isomorphic to Sp(B) for K-affinoid algebras B), compared with adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, under which admissible opens and admissible coverings correspond to opens and open coverings. A K-dagger space is a pair (X, O†_X) where X is a rigid space over K and O†_X ⊆ O_X is a subsheaf of K-algebras for the G-topology of X such that X has an admissible covering by affinoids U = Sp(Â_U) together with dagger algebras A_U with completion Â_U (a dagger structure on U) for which O†_X(V) = A_U⟨f/g⟩† for every rational subdomain V = R(f/g) ⊆ U with f, g ∈ A_U. A morphism (X, O†_X) → (Y, O†_Y) is a morphism of rigid spaces φ : X → Y over K with φ^♯(O†_Y) ⊆ φ_*O†_X. The affinoid dagger space of a dagger algebra A is Sp(A) := (Sp(Â), O†_A) with O†_A(R(f/g)) = A⟨f/g⟩†. This is Grosse-Klönne's definition 2.12 (locally G-ringed spaces with saturated G-topology admitting an admissible covering by affinoid dagger spaces, F1/dagger-g-topology) written, as in Vezzani 2.22, as a rigid space with a subsheaf; through AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor it is equivalently a quasi-separated adic space locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) with a subsheaf O† ⊆ O that is locally of the form R(f/g) ↦ A⟨f/g⟩† on rational subsets of Spa(Â, Â°). Dagger spaces are assumed quasi-separated.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
  • X quasi-separated

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-space

Strict neighbourhooddefinitionplanetStrict neighbourhoods of affinoids and the cofinal fringe system

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Rigid spaces are, throughout, the quasi-separated Tate rigid-analytic spaces over K of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space (G-topological spaces locally isomorphic to Sp(B) for K-affinoid algebras B), compared with adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, under which admissible opens and admissible coverings correspond to opens and open coverings. Let W be a rigid space and U ⊆ W an admissible open for which the complement W − U is admissible open (e.g. U an affinoid subdomain or a finite union of such). An admissible open V ⊆ W is a strict neighbourhood of U in W if {W − U, V} is an admissible covering of W; equivalently, in the adic space of W (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor), V contains the closure Ū of U (Vezzani's U ⋐_W V). For a fringe presentation, the affinoid Sp(T_n/IT_n) is written Sp(C) ⊂† Sp(D) inside D = T_n(ρ_0)/I (Grosse-Klönne 2.21), and for dagger spaces Sp(A) ⊂† Sp(B) means Sp(Â) ⊂† Sp(B̂). Cofinality: given ρ_0 ∈ Γ*, ρ_0 > 1, I ⊆ T_n(ρ_0) and an open immersion Sp(T_n(ρ_0)/I) → W, the affinoids V_ρ = Sp(T_n(ρ)/IT_n(ρ)), 1 < ρ ≤ ρ_0, form a cofinal system of strict neighbourhoods of V_1 = Sp(T_n/IT_n) in W. (Strict neighbourhoods of tubes in frames are PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3's notion, not this one.)

Hypotheses

  • W a rigid space over K
  • U ⊆ W quasi-compact open

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/strict-neighbourhood

Weak completionconstructionplanetThe Monsky–Washnitzer weak completion S† of a finitely generated O_K-algebra

Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). Let S be a finitely generated O_K-algebra and Ŝ = lim_m S/π^mS its π-adic completion. Choose generators x_1, …, x_n of S. The weak completion S† ⊆ Ŝ is the set of z ∈ Ŝ that can be written z = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(x_1, …, x_n) (convergent in Ŝ) with P_j ∈ O_K[X_1..X_n] of total degree ≤ c(j+1) for some real c; equivalently, S† is the image of O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† → Ŝ, X_i ↦ x_i. S† is an O_K-subalgebra of Ŝ containing the image of S, and it does not depend on the choice of generators. The dagger algebra attached to S is A† := S† ⊗_{O_K} K (F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre).

Hypotheses

  • O_K a complete discrete valuation ring
  • S a finitely generated O_K-algebra

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion

Dagger–rigid comparisonconstructionplanetThe comparison functor from dagger spaces to rigid spaces

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). The functor (·)' : (X, O†_X) ↦ X from K-dagger spaces to the quasi-separated rigid-analytic spaces of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space, with the natural inclusion ν : O†_X ⊆ O_{X'} of structure sheaves, is faithful and satisfies: (1) Sp(A)' = Sp(Â) for every dagger algebra A (whose adic space is Spa(Â, Â°)); (2) X is connected (resp. normal, reduced, regular) iff X' is; (3) X and X' have the same opens and coverings (the same underlying G-topological space) and ν is an isomorphism on local rings at classical points; (4) a morphism ρ : X → Y is a closed immersion (resp. open immersion, locally closed immersion, isomorphism, quasi-compact, separated) iff ρ' is; (5) if ρ is finite, so is ρ'; (6) if Y is a quasialgebraic rigid space (admissibly covered by opens of analytifications of affine finite type K-schemes; e.g. Y smooth), there are an admissible affinoid covering Y = ⋃ V_i and affinoid dagger spaces U_i with U_i' ≅ V_i, and U_i is unique up to (non-canonical) isomorphism. On coherent modules, F ↦ F' (with F' = O_{X'} ⊗ (F(X) ⊗_A Â) on X = Sp(A), glued) is a faithful exact functor coh(O†_X) → coh(O_{X'}) with a natural injection of underlying abelian sheaves F → F'.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued
  • dagger and rigid spaces quasi-separated
  • in (6): Y quasialgebraic

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-to-rigid-functor

Overconvergent de Rham complexconstructionplanetThe overconvergent de Rham complex of a smooth dagger space, with coefficients in a module with integrable connection

Let X be a smooth K-dagger space (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). The de Rham complex Ω^•_X = (Ω^0_X → Ω^1_X → Ω^2_X → …) is the complex of coherent locally free O†_X-modules Ω^i_X = ⋀^i Ω^1_X with the K-linear exterior derivative d (F1/dagger-differentials). More generally, for a coherent O†_X-module E with an integrable connection ∇ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1_X (K-linear, ∇(fe) = f∇e + e ⊗ df, ∇_1 ∘ ∇ = 0), DR(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_X with differentials ∇_i. The de Rham cohomology is the hypercohomology H^i_dR(X, E) := H^i(X, DR(E)) on the site of X, and H^i_dR(X) := H^i_dR(X, O†_X). For X = Sp(A) affinoid, H^i_dR(X, E) = H^i(Γ(X, E) ⊗_A Ω^•_A). For X' the associated rigid space, (Ω^i_X)' = Ω^i_{X'} and DR(E)' = DR(E'); but in general H^i_dR(X) ≠ H^i_dR(X') (see the tests).

Hypotheses

  • X smooth
  • E coherent with integrable connection

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-complex

Dagger algebras of Monsky–Washnitzer typedefinition

Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, residue field k = O_K/π and fraction field K (any characteristic; K carries the π-adic absolute value). A K-dagger algebra A is of Monsky–Washnitzer type (MW-type) if A is a regular ring and the ring A^int/πA^int is a smooth k-algebra (A^int = elements of supremum norm ≤ 1, F1/dagger-algebra). Its reduction (special fibre) is A^int/πA^int. The regularity clause is part of the definition: it does not follow from smoothness of A^int/πA^int.

Hypotheses

  • O_K a complete DVR
  • A a K-dagger algebra

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra

Affinoid subdomains of the maximal spectrum of a dagger algebradefinition

Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and X = Sp(A) its set of maximal ideals. A subset U ⊆ X is an affinoid subdomain if there are a dagger algebra B = O_X(U) and a morphism π : A → B with Sp(π)(Sp B) ⊆ U such that for every dagger algebra D the map Hom_K(B, D) → {f ∈ Hom_K(A, D) : Sp(f)(Sp D) ⊆ U}, g ↦ g ∘ π, is bijective. Then B is unique up to unique isomorphism and Sp(π) : Sp(B) → U is a bijection. Rational subdomains R(f/g) with O_X(R(f/g)) = A⟨f/g⟩† (F1/dagger-rational-localisation) and Weierstrass domains (g = 1) are affinoid subdomains; the notion is transitive and stable under base change A → D.

Hypotheses

  • A a K-dagger algebra

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-affinoid-subdomain

Coherent modules on dagger spacesdefinition

Let X be a K-dagger space. For an affinoid X = Sp(A) and an A-module M, M ⊗ O_X denotes the sheaf extending U ↦ M ⊗_A O†_X(U) on affinoid subdomains (a sheaf by F1/dagger-tate-acyclicity). An O†_X-module F is coherent if there are an admissible (open) affinoid covering X = ⋃ U_i, U_i = Sp(A_i), finite A_i-modules M_i and isomorphisms F|_{U_i} ≅ M_i ⊗ O_{U_i}. Coherent ideals, closed immersions of dagger spaces (defined by coherent ideals), separated and finite morphisms are defined as for rigid spaces.

Hypotheses

  • X a K-dagger space

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-coherent-module

Relative compactness, partially proper and proper morphisms, and Stein spaces for dagger spacesdefinition

Let f : X = Sp(A) → Y = Sp(B) be a morphism of affinoid K-dagger spaces and U ⊆ X an affinoid subdomain. Write U ⊂⊂_Y X if there are a surjection τ : B⟨X_1..X_r⟩† → A and ε ∈ Γ*, ε < 1, with U ⊆ Sp(A⟨ε^{-1}τ(X_1), …, ε^{-1}τ(X_r)⟩†). A morphism f : X → Y of dagger spaces is partially proper if it is separated and there are admissible affinoid coverings Y = ⋃ Y_i and f^{-1}(Y_i) = ⋃ X_{ij} such that each X_{ij} satisfies X_{ij} ⊂⊂_{Y_i} X̃_{ij} for some admissible open affinoid X̃_{ij} ⊆ f^{-1}(Y_i); f is proper if it is quasi-compact and partially proper. A dagger space X is a Stein space if it has an admissible affinoid covering X = ⋃_{i∈ℕ} U_i with U_i ⊂† U_{i+1} for all i (a Stein covering). The same definitions apply to rigid spaces, where they agree with Huber's partial properness (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism).

Hypotheses

  • f a morphism of K-dagger spaces

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-partially-proper

Smooth dagger spacesdefinition

A K-dagger space X (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) is smooth if its associated rigid space X' (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytic-space) is smooth over K, i.e. its adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor) is smooth over Spa(K, O_K) in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/smooth-morphism. Equivalently: for every affinoid Sp(A) ⊆ X, A is regular and Ω^1_A is projective of rank equal to the local dimension; equivalently X is locally étale over a dagger polydisc. X has pure dimension n if dim O_{X,x} = n at every point; then ω_X := Ω^n_X.

Hypotheses

  • X a K-dagger space

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-smooth-space

Strict normal crossings divisors on smooth dagger spaces (smooth dagger pairs)definition

Let X be a smooth K-dagger space (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and D ⊆ X a closed dagger subspace (F1/dagger-coherent-module). D is a strict normal crossings divisor if its associated rigid pair (X', D') corresponds, under AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, to a smooth pair in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair (X' smooth over K with the strict normal crossings divisor D'); only this dagger-specific transfer is defined here. Equivalently: every point has an affinoid neighbourhood Sp(A) with elements x_1, …, x_n ∈ A such that dx_1, …, dx_n is a basis of Ω^1_A and D ∩ Sp(A) = V(x_1⋯x_r) for some r ≤ n (as a closed subspace); equivalently, at every point x ∈ D the local ring O_{X,x} is regular with a regular system of parameters x_1..x_d such that D is cut out by x_1⋯x_r. The pair (X, D) is then a smooth dagger pair; D is reduced and an effective Cartier divisor, and locally on an admissible affinoid covering D = V(x_1) ∪ … ∪ V(x_r) with smooth pieces V(x_i) whose partial intersections are smooth of the expected codimension. As in AdicSpacesPartII:R4/smooth-pair no condition is imposed on the global irreducible components: they need not be smooth (e.g. for residue characteristic ≠ 2 the analytified nodal cubic V(y^2 − x^2(1 + x)) ⊆ Sp(K⟨x, y⟩†) is a strict normal crossings divisor in this sense — at the origin it is V((y − x√(1+x))(y + x√(1+x))) with √(1+x) analytic on |x| < 1 — yet it is irreducible and singular).

Hypotheses

  • X smooth
  • D ⊆ X a closed dagger subspace

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-snc-divisor

The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† of overconvergent power seriesconstruction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). For n ∈ ℕ define W_n = K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>1} T_n(ρ) ⊆ K[[X_1, …, X_n]], the set of power series Σ_ν a_ν X^ν for which there is a real ρ > 1 with |a_ν| ρ^{|ν|} → 0 (equivalently: there are ρ > 1 and C ≥ 0 with |a_ν| ≤ C ρ^{-|ν|} for all ν; equivalently there is ρ ∈ Γ*, ρ > 1, such that the series converges at every point x of K_a^n (K_a an algebraic closure) with max_i |x_i| ≤ ρ; convergence only at the K-rational points of such a polydisc does not suffice when K is discretely valued and ρ < |π|^{-1}, since those points already lie in the unit polydisc). Because ρ ↦ T_n(ρ) is antitone, the union is directed and W_n is a K-subalgebra of K[[X]]; the union may be taken over ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ∞) (Γ* = √|K^×|) but NOT only over ρ ∈ |K^×|. W_n ⊆ T_n = T_n(1), and W_n carries the Gauss norm |f| = max_ν |a_ν| restricted from T_n. Convention: the variables are X_1, …, X_n, |ν| = ν_1+…+ν_n, and ‘overconvergent’ always means ‘restricted at some radius strictly bigger than 1’.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued (rank one)
  • n ∈ ℕ

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/overconvergent-tate-algebra

Fringe (radius-indexed) presentations of a dagger algebraconstruction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. A fringe presentation of A consists of n ∈ ℕ, a radius ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1, elements f_1, …, f_r ∈ T_n(ρ_0), and a K-algebra isomorphism W_n/(f_1, …, f_r)W_n ≅ A. For ρ ∈ Γ* ∩ (1, ρ_0] put A_ρ := T_n(ρ)/(f)T_n(ρ), a K-affinoid algebra (F1/radius-tate-algebra-affinoid), with transition maps A_{ρ'} → A_ρ for ρ ≤ ρ' induced by T_n(ρ') ⊆ T_n(ρ), and put A_1 := T_n/(f)T_n. Then A = colim_{ρ → 1+} A_ρ as K-algebras, and A_1 = Â is the completion. The fringe algebra of the presentation at radius ρ is the image B_ρ ⊆ A of A_ρ (equivalently of T_n(ρ)); A_ρ → A need not be injective. Geometrically, X_ρ = Sp(A_ρ) is a decreasing family of affinoids with ⋂_ρ X_ρ = Sp(Â) and Sp(Â) ⊆ X_ρ the Weierstrass domain {|X_1|, …, |X_n| ≤ 1}; this situation is written Sp(Â) ⊂† X_ρ.

Hypotheses

  • A a K-dagger algebra
  • ρ_0 ∈ Γ* with ρ_0 > 1 and f_i ∈ T_n(ρ_0)

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation

The fringe (direct limit) topology on dagger algebras and their finite modulesconstruction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and A a K-dagger algebra. The fringe topology on A is the finest locally K-convex topology for which every map A_ρ → A of a fringe presentation is continuous, A_ρ carrying its Banach topology; equivalently the direct limit of the intrinsic Banach topologies of the fringe algebras of A. It does not depend on the fringe presentation, is Hausdorff, is finer than the norm (affinoid) topology of F1/dagger-norm-and-continuity, and every K-algebra homomorphism of dagger algebras is continuous for it. A finite A-module M carries the fringe topology obtained as the quotient topology from A^r ↠ M (equivalently by base extension from a module over a fringe algebra), independent of choices; A-linear maps of finite modules are continuous. If K is spherically complete (in particular discretely valued), A with its fringe topology is a complete reflexive Hausdorff locally convex K-space.

Hypotheses

  • A a K-dagger algebra
  • for completeness and reflexivity: K spherically complete

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology

The dagger (overconvergent completed) tensor product A_1 ⊗†_B A_2construction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and let α_1 : B → A_1, α_2 : B → A_2 be morphisms of K-dagger algebras with surjections f_1 : W_{n_1} → A_1, f_2 : W_{n_2} → A_2. Define A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 as the image of W_{n_1+n_2} = K⟨X, Y⟩† under the continuous map T_{n_1+n_2} → Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2 into the completed tensor product of the K-affinoid algebras Â_1, Â_2 over B̂ that sends X_i ↦ f̂_1(X_i) ⊗ 1 and Y_j ↦ 1 ⊗ f̂_2(Y_j). It is a K-dagger algebra with maps ι_i : A_i → A_1 ⊗†_B A_2, independent of the surjections up to unique isomorphism, and it is the pushout of α_1, α_2 in the category of dagger algebras: for morphisms u_i : A_i → C with u_1α_1 = u_2α_2 there is a unique u : A_1 ⊗†_B A_2 → C with u ι_i = u_i. Its completion is Â_1 ⊗̂_{B̂} Â_2. Equivalently (Kedlaya) A_1 ⊗†_K A_2 is the direct limit of the completed tensor products B_1 ⊗̂_K B_2 of fringe algebras B_i of A_i. Notation: for λ ∈ Γ*, K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := ⋃_{ρ>λ} K⟨ρ^{-1}Z⟩ and A⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩† := A ⊗†_K K⟨λ^{-1}Z⟩†, A⟨Z⟩† := A⟨1^{-1}Z⟩†.

Hypotheses

  • α_i : B → A_i morphisms of K-dagger algebras

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product

Rational localisation A⟨f/g⟩† of a dagger algebra and its universal propertyconstruction

Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)) and g, f_1, …, f_m ∈ A without common zero on Sp(A) (equivalently generating the unit ideal). Define A⟨f/g⟩† := A⟨X_1, …, X_m⟩†/(gX_i − f_i)_{i≤m} (A⟨X⟩† from F1/dagger-tensor-product). The map A → A⟨f/g⟩† is universal among morphisms of dagger algebras φ : A → C such that Sp(φ) lands in R(f/g) := {x ∈ Sp(A) : |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| for all i}: φ(g) is then a unit and φ factors uniquely through A⟨f/g⟩†. Special cases: Weierstrass localisations A⟨f⟩† (g = 1) and Laurent localisations A⟨f^{-1}⟩† = A⟨X⟩†/(fX − 1). Sp(A⟨f/g⟩†) = R(f/g), the completion of A⟨f/g⟩† is the affinoid rational localisation Â⟨f/g⟩, and A⟨f/g⟩† depends only on the subset R(f/g), not on (f, g).

Hypotheses

  • A a K-dagger algebra
  • g, f_1..f_m ∈ A generate the unit ideal

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation

The integral Monsky–Washnitzer algebra O_K⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩† = W_n ∩ O_K[[X]]construction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1}. Define O_K⟨X_1..X_n⟩† := W_n ∩ O_K[[X_1..X_n]], the overconvergent power series with coefficients in O_K; it is W_n^int (F1/dagger-algebra). If O_K is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π, a series f ∈ O_K[[X]] lies in O_K⟨X⟩† iff there is c > 0 with f = Σ_{j≥0} π^j P_j(X), P_j ∈ O_K[X], deg P_j ≤ c(j+1) (the Monsky–Washnitzer degree growth condition), and then O_K⟨X⟩† is noetherian, O_K⟨X⟩†/π^m = O_K[X]/π^m for all m, its π-adic completion is O_K⟨X⟩ = T_n ∩ O_K[[X]], and O_K⟨X⟩† ⊗_{O_K} K = W_n.

Hypotheses

  • K complete, nontrivially and nonarchimedeanly valued; for the degree-growth description, noetherianity and the π-adic statements: O_K a discrete valuation ring

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra

Dagger analytification of schemes of finite typeconstruction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K) and X a K-scheme of finite type. Its dagger analytification X^† is the partially proper K-dagger space with (X^†)' = X^an, the rigid analytification (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-analytification), which exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism by F1/partially-proper-dagger-rigid-equivalence because X^an is partially proper. X ↦ X^† is a functor, compatible with open and closed immersions and fibre products; for X affine with presentation K[X_1..X_n]/(f), X^† = ⋃_{ρ ∈ Γ*} Sp(K⟨ρ^{-1}X⟩†/(f)). For X proper, coherent cohomology satisfies GAGA: H^i(X, F) ≅ H^i(X^†, F^†) for coherent F.

Hypotheses

  • X of finite type over K

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-analytification

The module of (universally finite) differentials Ω^1_A of a dagger algebra and the exterior derivativeconstruction

Let A be a K-dagger algebra (K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K)). The module of differentials of A is a finite A-module Ω^1_A = Ω^1_{A/K} with a K-derivation d : A → Ω^1_A that is universal among K-derivations of A into finite A-modules: every K-derivation D : A → M, M finite, is u ∘ d for a unique A-linear u. Explicitly, for a presentation A = W_n/(f_1, …, f_r): Ω^1_A = (⊕_i A dX_i) / (Σ_j (∂f_k/∂X_j) dX_j)_k with d g = Σ_i (∂g/∂X_i) dX_i. Equivalently Ω^1_A = J/J^2 for J the kernel of the multiplication A ⊗†_K A → A (Kedlaya's module of continuous differentials). Put Ω^i_A = ⋀^i_A Ω^1_A with d extended by d(a db_1 ∧ … ∧ db_i) = da ∧ db_1 ∧ … ∧ db_i. These sheafify to coherent O†_X-modules Ω^i_X on every dagger space X, with (Ω^i_X)' = Ω^i_{X'}. For a finitely generated algebra S over a complete DVR O_K the same construction gives Ω^1_{S†/O_K} (van der Put's D^1), with Ω^1_{S†/O_K} ⊗ K = Ω^1_{S†⊗K}.

Hypotheses

  • A a K-dagger algebra

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials

De Rham cohomology with supports in the complement of an admissible openconstruction

Let X be a smooth K-dagger (or rigid) space and j : U → X the inclusion of an admissible open with complement Y = X − U (a closed subset, not given a space structure). For a sheaf F on X let Γ_Y(F) = ker(F → j_*j^{-1}F) and RΓ_Y its right derived functor; for a complex such as Ω^•_X define H^i_Y(X, Ω^•_X) := H^i(X, RΓ_Y Ω^•_X) (and likewise H^i_Y(X, F) for coherent F). There is a distinguished triangle RΓ_Y(X, Ω^•) → RΓ(X, Ω^•) → RΓ(U, Ω^•) →, a Mayer–Vietoris triangle RΓ_{Y∩Y'} → RΓ_Y ⊕ RΓ_{Y'} → RΓ_{Y∪Y'} → when U ∪ U' is an admissible covering of an admissible open, and for Z ⊆ Y closed a triangle RΓ_Z → RΓ_Y → Rj'_*RΓ_{Y−Z}j'^{-1} → with j' : X − Z → X.

Hypotheses

  • X smooth (dagger or rigid)
  • U ⊆ X admissible open, Y = X − U

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports

Compactly supported coherent and de Rham cohomology of affinoid and Stein dagger spacesconstruction

Let K be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |.| of rank one (in Lean: NontriviallyNormedField K, IsUltrametricDist K, CompleteSpace K). Let X = Sp(A) be an affinoid K-dagger space with a fringe presentation A = W_m/IW_m, I ⊆ T_m(ρ_0), fringe stages X_ρ = Sp(T_m(ρ)/IT_m(ρ)), so X' ⊂† X_ρ. For a coherent O†_X-module F choose (after shrinking ρ_0) a coherent O_{X_{ρ_0}}-module F_{ρ_0} with F(X) = colim_ρ F_{ρ_0}(X_ρ) (F1/fringe-module-descent) and put H^i_c(X, F) := H^i_{X}(X_{ρ_0}, F_{ρ_0}), the cohomology of F_{ρ_0} with supports in the complement of the admissible open X_{ρ_0} − X' (F1/de-rham-cohomology-with-supports). For X smooth, H^i_{dR,c}(X) := H^i_{X}(X_ρ, Ω^•_{X_ρ}). Both are independent of ρ and of the fringe presentation. For a smooth Stein dagger space X with Stein covering (U_j)_{j∈ℕ}, H^i_c(X, F) := colim_j H^i_{U_j}(U_{j+1}, F) and H^i_{dR,c}(X) := colim_j H^i_{U_j}(U_{j+1}, Ω^•), along the extension-by-zero maps. H^i_c(X, F) carries the finest locally convex topology making the boundary maps H^{i−1}(X_{ρ_0} − X', F_{ρ_0}) → H^i_c(X, F) continuous, and a topological A-module structure.

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/compact-support-de-rham

The logarithmic de Rham complex Ω^•_X(log D) along a strict normal crossings divisorconstruction

The sheaf Ω^1_X(log D) ⊆ j_*Ω^1_{X−D} is the O†_X-submodule generated locally, in coordinates with D = V(x_1⋯x_r), by dx_1/x_1, …, dx_r/x_r, dx_{r+1}, …, dx_n; it is locally free of rank n and independent of the coordinates. For a smooth component D_1 of D (a smooth closed dagger subspace which is a union of irreducible components of D) with D = D_1 + D' — so that D'|_{D_1} is a strict normal crossings divisor on D_1 — there is a residue map Res_{D_1} and an exact sequence of complexes 0 → Ω^•_X(log D') → Ω^•_X(log D) → ι_*Ω^•_{D_1}(log D'|_{D_1})[−1] → 0. Its hypercohomology is H^i_dR(X, log D) := H^i(X, Ω^•_X(log D)), and (Ω^•_X(log D))' = Ω^•_{X'}(log D').

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/log-de-rham-complex

The boundary-vanishing (compact-support) logarithmic de Rham complex Ω^•_X(log D)(−D)construction

Let (X, D) be a smooth K-dagger space with a strict normal crossings divisor and I_D ⊆ O†_X its (invertible) ideal. The compact-support logarithmic de Rham complex is the subcomplex Ω^•_X(log D)(−D) := I_D · Ω^•_X(log D) of Ω^•_X(log D); in coordinates with D = V(x_1⋯x_r) it is x_1⋯x_r·Ω^•_X(log D) ⊆ Ω^•_X. Its hypercohomology H^i_{c}(X, D) := H^i(X, Ω^•_X(log D)(−D)) is the de Rham cohomology of the pair with vanishing along the boundary. There are natural maps Ω^•_X(log D)(−D) ⊆ Ω^•_X ⊆ Ω^•_X(log D), inducing H^i_c(X, D) → H^i_dR(X) → H^i_dR(X, log D), and on X − D the complex restricts to Ω^•_{X−D}. With coefficients: for a locally free E with integrable connection having logarithmic poles along D, DR_c(E) := I_D·E ⊗ Ω^•_X(log D).

AdicSpacesPartII:F1/compact-support-log-complex

General algebraic K-theory

Algebraic K-theory · 9 definitions · 10 constructions · 11 planets

K.1The Q-construction and its smallness

The K-groups of an exact categorydefinitionplanet

For a small exact category the K-theory space is the realisation of the nerve of Q(A) and the K-groups are its homotopy groups shifted by one: the n-th K-group is the (n+1)-st homotopy group of that space at the zero object, for every non-negative n. The groups are abelian, including in degree zero, where the definition agrees with the Grothendieck group by the previous node. The space and the groups are functors from exact categories and exact functors to spaces and to abelian groups, and isomorphic exact functors induce the same maps. For a ring the K-groups are those of the exact category of finitely generated projective modules; for a noetherian ring the G-groups are those of the finitely generated modules; for a quasi-projective scheme the K-groups are those of the vector bundles.

Hypotheses

  • A is small, or has a set of isomorphism classes and is replaced by a small model as in the earlier node.
  • The basepoint is a zero object, and the choice does not matter.
  • The indexing is the one fixed here: the n-th K-group is the (n+1)-st homotopy group, so that degree zero is the fundamental group.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.1/K-groups-of-exact-categories

The Q-constructionconstructionplanetExact categories and Quillen's category Q(A)

For an exact category A the category Q(A) has the objects of A; a morphism from A to B is an equivalence class of diagrams in which A is received by an admissible epimorphism out of a subobject of B and that subobject is an admissible monomorphism into B, two such diagrams being equivalent when an isomorphism between them is the identity on A and on B. Composition is by pullback of the two middle objects. Equivalently a morphism from A to B is an admissible subobject of B together with an admissible epimorphism from it onto A. Two kinds of morphism are distinguished, the admissible monomorphisms and the oppositely oriented admissible epimorphisms; both are closed under composition, every morphism factors as one of the second kind followed by one of the first, uniquely up to isomorphism, the morphisms from the zero object to B correspond to the admissible subobjects of B, and the isomorphisms of Q(A) correspond to the isomorphisms of A.

Hypotheses

  • A is an exact category in the sense of Quillen: an additive category with a class of conflations satisfying the usual axioms, which is what the pinned TauCeti.ExactStructure records.
  • The equivalence classes of the defining diagrams must form a set; this is guaranteed for a small exact category, and the next node says how a small model is chosen.
  • Composition uses the pullback of an admissible epimorphism along an arbitrary map, which exists and is again an admissible epimorphism by the base-change axiom; this is where the exactness axioms are used.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.1/exact-categories-and-Q-construction

K.2Ring K-theory and the plus construction

The K-theory of a ring as a functor, and what the comparisons are natural inconstruction

Putting the previous nodes together: the assignment of the K-theory space to a ring is a functor on unital rings and ring homomorphisms, through the base-change functor on finitely generated projectives; it carries finite products of rings to products and commutes with filtered colimits; and the plus comparison is natural for ring maps and for block sum. This node is the aggregate the stage text asks for, and it is also where the limits of the naturality claim are fixed: the space-level product description depends on a choice of component representatives, and the translations between components are not natural, so no naturality is asserted for them.

Hypotheses

  • The rings are unital and the maps are unital.
  • Naturality is asserted for ring maps and for the block-sum operation, and for nothing else.
  • The product description is at the level of spaces after a choice; the infinite-loop structure is not claimed to split.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2/functorial-K-theory-of-a-ring

K.2:plusRing K-theory and the plus construction

Scalar extension of finitely generated projectives, without a flatness hypothesisconstruction

For a unital ring homomorphism from A to B the functor sending a module to its extension of scalars carries finitely generated projective A-modules to finitely generated projective B-modules and split exact sequences to split exact sequences, with no flatness hypothesis: projectivity and finite generation are both preserved by base change, and a split exact sequence is carried to a split exact sequence by any additive functor whatever. The resulting exact functor between the categories of finitely generated projectives is what makes the K-theory of a ring a functor. Tau Ceti already has the category of finitely generated projectives with its exact structure, proved to be the split one, and the statement that every additive functor is exact for split structures; Mathlib has the two base-change statements. What is missing, and what this node builds, is the functor itself along an arbitrary unital ring map and the functoriality of K that follows.

Hypotheses

  • The ring map is unital and the rings need not be commutative; the extension of scalars is the tensor product over the source, taken on the correct side.
  • No flatness is assumed. Flatness would be needed to preserve arbitrary exact sequences, and is not needed here because the exact structure on finitely generated projectives is the split one.
  • The pinned Mathlib base-change statements for projectivity and for finite generation are stated for an algebra over a commutative ring; for an arbitrary unital ring map the corresponding statements are part of this node.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:plus/scalar-extension-and-functoriality

The extension category and the fibration over Q(A)construction

For an exact category A the EXTENSION CATEGORY has as objects the admissible exact sequences of A, with morphisms the equivalence classes of the displayed three-row diagrams. The functor to Q(A) sending a sequence to its quotient term is fibred, its fibre over the zero object is the groupoid of isomorphisms of A, and each fibre is symmetric monoidal with a faithful monoidal functor from that groupoid. Localising the fibre at that action and comparing gives a fibration from the localised groupoid through the localised fibre to a contractible category, and the localised extension category is itself contractible; these are the inputs to the plus-equals-Q theorem of the next node.

Hypotheses

  • A is a small exact category; for the contractibility statements A is split exact, that is every admissible exact sequence splits.
  • The groupoid of isomorphisms acts on each fibre by direct sum on the sub and total terms, leaving the quotient term fixed.
  • Split exactness is what makes the relevant category connected; without it the source records that it is not.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:plus/extension-category-and-the-fibration

K.4:constructionWaldhausen’s S-construction and delooping

Waldhausen categorydefinitionplanetCategories with cofibrations, Waldhausen categories and their extra axioms

A CATEGORY WITH COFIBRATIONS is a category with a subcategory of cofibrations such that every isomorphism is a cofibration, there is a distinguished zero object whose map to every object is a cofibration, and pushouts along cofibrations exist with cofibrations stable under cobase change. A WALDHAUSEN CATEGORY adds a subcategory of weak equivalences containing the isomorphisms, closed under composition and satisfying the gluing axiom, that the pushout of a map of cofibration squares whose components are weak equivalences is a weak equivalence. Three further axioms are used only by later theorems and are stated separately: SATURATION, that in a composable pair whose composite is a weak equivalence one factor is a weak equivalence exactly when the other is; the EXTENSION axiom, that a map of cofibration sequences whose sub and quotient maps are weak equivalences has total map a weak equivalence; and the CYLINDER axiom for a cylinder functor. An exact category is a Waldhausen category with the admissible monomorphisms as cofibrations and the isomorphisms as weak equivalences.

Hypotheses

  • The categories are small, so that the weak-equivalence classes form a set and the Grothendieck group is defined.
  • An exact functor preserves the zero object, cofibrations, weak equivalences and the pushouts along cofibrations.
  • Saturation, extension and the cylinder axiom are NOT part of the definition; each theorem of K.4 names the ones it uses.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/waldhausen-categories

Waldhausen's S-constructionconstructionplanetWaldhausen's S-construction and the induced cofibrations

For a category with cofibrations, the n-th term of the S-construction is the category whose objects are sequences of n cofibrations together with a compatible choice of all subquotients, with morphisms the natural transformations of such diagrams; the zeroth term is trivial, the first is the category itself, and the second is the extension category, whose three face maps are the quotient, total and sub functors. The faces delete a row and a column and the degeneracies duplicate, and they are exact, so the terms form a simplicial category with cofibrations; taking the subcategories of weak equivalences gives a simplicial category whose realisation is the object of the next node. The cofibrations of the n-th term are NOT the objectwise ones: a map is a cofibration when for every triple of indices the induced map of cofibration sequences is a cofibration of the second term, which is a condition on the canonical maps out of the pushouts. The stage text's warning is exactly this, and this node states it as a hypothesis rather than a remark.

Hypotheses

  • The ambient category is a small category with cofibrations; for the weak-equivalence subcategories it is a Waldhausen category.
  • The choices of subquotients are part of the data of an object and must be compatible with the displayed staircase diagram.
  • The cofibrations of the n-th term are defined by the latching condition stated above; objectwise cofibrations do not in general satisfy the pushout conditions required.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/S-construction

The K-theory space of a Waldhausen categorydefinition

The K-theory space of a small Waldhausen category is the loop space of the realisation of the weak-equivalence S-construction, and its K-groups are the homotopy groups of that loop space, so the n-th K-group is the (n+1)-st homotopy group of the realisation. The fundamental group of the realisation is the Grothendieck group of the category, which fixes the indexing; the realisation is an H-space under coproduct, and the whole is in fact an infinite loop space obtained by iterating the construction.

Hypotheses

  • The category is small and Waldhausen; no extra axiom is needed for the definition.
  • The basepoint is the trivial object of the zeroth term, whose realisation is a point.
  • The infinite-loop structure comes from iterating the construction, and the identification of consecutive terms is the delooping theorem of K.4.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction/K-theory-space-of-a-waldhausen-category

K.5Relative and nonunital theories

Relative K-theorydefinitionplanetRelative K-theory as a homotopy fibre

For a ring homomorphism the RELATIVE K-THEORY space is the homotopy fibre of the induced map of K-theory spaces, and the relative groups are its homotopy groups; they fit into a long exact sequence with the absolute groups, ending in the zeroth relative group mapping to the zeroth group of the source. All the relative groups, the zeroth one included, are abelian, because the functorial H-space structure on the K-theory space makes the fibre one. A pair consisting of a ring and a two-sided ideal is treated through the quotient map, and then the zeroth relative group is the zeroth K-group of the ideal and the first is the classical relative group. For an exact functor of Waldhausen categories the relative theory is the double loop space of the relative S-construction of K.4, and its sequence ends one step further, with the cokernel of the map of Grothendieck groups appearing as a first negative group.

Hypotheses

  • The rings are unital and the map is unital; for a pair the ideal is two-sided.
  • The homotopy fibre is taken at the basepoint of the target, and the H-space structure used for the group laws is the functorial one.
  • The Waldhausen version needs the relative S-construction and its fibration, which is K.4's theorem.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.5/relative-K-theory

Nonunital rings, the unitisation and the comparison with the unital theoryconstruction

A ring without unit is treated through a specified unitisation, the canonical augmented ring obtained by adjoining the integers, and its K-theory is defined as the relative theory of the augmentation. The unitisation is pinned in Mathlib with its universal property, and nothing K-theoretic is built on it there. The comparison with the usual theory is the statement that for a nonunital ring contained as a two-sided ideal in a unital ring there is a map from the theory defined this way to the relative theory of the pair, and the question of when it is an isomorphism is exactly excision, which is the next node's subject.

Hypotheses

  • The nonunital ring is an associative ring without unit; the unitisation is the canonical one over the integers, which is the pinned construction.
  • The augmentation is the ring map to the integers and the relative theory is that of the augmentation.
  • The comparison map exists for any unital ring containing the nonunital one as a two-sided ideal, and no claim is made about its being an isomorphism here.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.5/nonunital-rings-and-unitisation

K.6Nonconnective extension

Flasque ringdefinitionplanetFlasque rings, infinite sum rings and the Eilenberg swindle

A ring is FLASQUE, in Karoubi's sense, when there is a bimodule M, finitely generated projective as a right module, together with a bimodule isomorphism from the direct sum of the ring with M onto M. For a flasque ring the zeroth K-group vanishes, because for every finitely generated projective P the natural isomorphism from the direct sum of P with its tensor product against M onto that tensor product makes the class of P equal to zero; this is the Eilenberg swindle. When the underlying right module structure on M is the ring itself the ring is called an INFINITE SUM RING, and the cone rings are examples, hence flasque. The notion has nothing to do with the flasque sheaves that both pinned libraries call by that name, and a formalisation must not reuse the name.

Hypotheses

  • R is a ring, not necessarily commutative; M is an R-bimodule, finitely generated projective as a right module.
  • The isomorphism is of bimodules and is part of the data, not merely an abstract isomorphism of underlying modules.
  • The pinned libraries' IsFlasque is the sheaf-theoretic notion; the audit records this and the name must be kept apart.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/flasque-rings-and-the-swindle

Bass's negative K-groupsdefinitionplanet

For n positive define the n-th negative K-group of a ring inductively as the cokernel of the difference map from the direct sum of the (n-1)-st negative group of the two polynomial rings into that of the Laurent ring; the case n = 1 starts from the zeroth K-group. Each is a functor from rings to abelian groups. The first negative group is what the Fundamental Theorem for the zeroth K-group produces: that theorem gives a split exact sequence exhibiting the zeroth K-group of the Laurent ring as the direct sum of the zeroth group, the first negative group and two copies of the N-term, which is the obstruction to homotopy invariance.

Hypotheses

  • R is a ring; the groups are defined for every ring, with no regularity or noetherian hypothesis.
  • The definition is by iterated contraction, so it depends on the previous node's machine and on nothing else.
  • The N-terms are the cokernels of the maps from the K-group of the ring to that of the polynomial ring, and vanish exactly when the K-group in that degree is homotopy invariant.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/negative-k-groups

Frobenius pairdefinitionplanetFrobenius categories, Frobenius pairs and their derived categories

A Frobenius category is an exact category with enough projective and enough injective objects in which the projectives and the injectives coincide; its stable category, obtained by killing the maps that factor through a projective-injective, is triangulated. A FROBENIUS PAIR is a fully faithful inclusion of one small Frobenius category in another carrying projective-injectives into projective-injectives, and its DERIVED CATEGORY is the Verdier quotient of the two stable categories. This is the category of models on which the whole nonconnective construction of this layer runs: the bounded complexes over an exact category, with degreewise split conflations and the homotopy-acyclic complexes as the subcategory, form a Frobenius pair whose derived category is the bounded derived category, and that is how an exact category enters the machine.

Hypotheses

  • The categories are small; the inclusion is fully faithful and exact and preserves projective-injective objects.
  • The stable category is triangulated, with the shift given by the cokernel of an inflation into an injective object.
  • For the example, the conflations of the complex category are the degreewise split ones, and the subcategory is the complexes homotopy equivalent to acyclic complexes; acyclic has the exact-category meaning, that each differential factors through a conflation.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/frobenius-pairs

The Bass K-theory spectrumconstructionplanetThe nonconnective Bass K-theory spectrum

For a functor E from rings to spectra, let LE be the homotopy cofiber of the map from the homotopy pushout of the two polynomial spectra over the spectrum of the ring into the spectrum of the Laurent ring, and let the desuspended functor be its loop space; there is a cofibration sequence natural in both arguments. Applying this to connective K-theory and using the Fundamental Theorem, the homotopy groups of the desuspension recover the K-groups one degree down in positive degrees, and the zeroth and first negative groups in degrees zero and minus one. Multiplication by the class of the variable gives a natural map from the K-theory spectrum to its desuspension, which the Fundamental Theorem shows is the inclusion of the minus-one-connective cover; iterating gives maps of the k-fold desuspensions, each the inclusion of a deeper connective cover, and the nonconnective Bass spectrum is the homotopy colimit of that diagram. Its homotopy groups are the K-groups in non-negative degrees and Bass's negative groups below.

Hypotheses

  • E is a functor from rings to spectra; for the main statements E is one of the functorial models of connective K-theory the source lists.
  • The homotopy pushout and the homotopy cofiber are taken in spectra; neither pinned library has spectra, which the audit records.
  • The comparison map is multiplication by the class of the variable in the first K-group of the Laurent polynomial ring over the integers.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/nonconnective-spectrum

The countable flasque envelopeconstructionplanetThe countable flasque envelope and the suspension of a Frobenius pair

The COUNTABLE ENVELOPE of a small exact category has as objects the sequences of inflations, with morphism groups the limit over the source index of the colimit over the target index; it is exact, has exact countable coproducts, and is FLASQUE: the functor sending a sequence to the countable sum of its shifts satisfies the direct sum of the identity with it being naturally isomorphic to it, which is the Eilenberg swindle in functorial form. Applied to a Frobenius pair this gives an endofunctor F of Frobenius pairs whose derived category has countable coproducts and is c-compactly generated by the original, so that the idempotent completion of the original derived category is the c-compact part of the enlarged one. The SUSPENSION S of a pair is the enlarged Frobenius category together with the objects that vanish in the quotient of the enlarged derived category by the original, so that the derived category of the suspension is exactly that quotient. The natural transformations from the identity through F to S then satisfy the axioms of the model set-up, and this is the flasque enlargement and suspension the stage text asks for.

Hypotheses

  • The exact category and the Frobenius pairs are small; the envelope is taken with the source's morphism formula, not with a naive colimit.
  • Flasque is used in Karoubi's sense of the earlier node, a functor T with the identity plus T naturally isomorphic to T, and has nothing to do with the sheaf-theoretic predicate the pinned libraries call by that name.
  • c-compact means that the represented functor commutes with countable coproducts; the generation statement is by countable homotopy colimits.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/frobenius-pairs-flasque-envelope-and-suspension

The axioms a theory of negative K-theory must satisfydefinition

A theory of negative K-theory for possibly non-unital rings is a sequence of functors in degrees at most zero together with natural boundary maps from the K-group of a quotient to the next group down of the ideal, satisfying four axioms: in degree zero the functor is the Grothendieck group; for every two-sided ideal the five-term sequence through the ideal, the ring and the quotient is exact; every flasque ring has vanishing groups in all degrees at most zero; and the inclusion of a ring in its infinite matrix ring induces isomorphisms in all those degrees. Bass's groups form such a theory. The axioms are what a second construction must be checked against, and they are the interface through which this layer's nonconnective spectrum is compared with the Bass groups.

Hypotheses

  • The rings are allowed to be non-unital, which is what makes the ideal axiom usable.
  • The matrix ring in the fourth axiom is the union of the finite matrix rings.
  • The axioms do not determine the theory by themselves; the source records that Bass's groups satisfy them, which is what the axioms are for.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/axioms-for-negative-k-theory

The set-up: negative K-groups of a triangulated category with modelsdefinition

For a small triangulated category the zeroth invariant is the zeroth K-group of its idempotent completion. A SET-UP consists of a category of models with a functor to small triangulated categories, together with endofunctors F and S and natural transformations from the identity through F to S, such that both preserve exact sequences, the zeroth invariant of an enlargement vanishes, and the sequence from a model through its enlargement to its suspension is exact; a sequence of small triangulated categories is EXACT when the composite is zero, the first functor is fully faithful and the induced functor from the Verdier quotient to the third is cofinal. The negative groups of a model are then the zeroth invariant of its iterated suspension. Taking the models to be Frobenius pairs and the functors of the previous node gives the negative K-groups of an exact category, of a ring, of a scheme and of a differential graded algebra.

Hypotheses

  • The categories are small; cofinal means fully faithful with every object a direct summand of one in the image.
  • The idempotent completion carries a canonical triangulated structure, which is what makes the zeroth invariant well defined.
  • The axiomatic form is deliberate: the source records that it allows models other than Frobenius pairs, which it does not develop.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/schlichting-set-up

Contracted functors and the contraction LFconstruction

For a functor F from rings to abelian groups define LF(R) to be the cokernel of the difference map from the direct sum of F of the polynomial ring in t and of the polynomial ring in t inverse into F of the Laurent polynomial ring. Call F ACYCLIC when the four-term sequence, from F of the ring through those two, to the Laurent ring and onto LF, is exact for every ring; call it CONTRACTED when it is acyclic and the defining surjection onto LF admits a splitting natural in both the ring and the variable. Iterating gives the functors NLF and L-squared F. This is the machine that produces the negative K-groups, and the naturality of the splitting is the part that does the work.

Hypotheses

  • F is a functor from rings to abelian groups; the polynomial and Laurent rings are over the given ring.
  • The splitting of a contracted functor is natural in the variable as well as in the ring; naturality in the ring alone is not enough for the iteration.
  • The notation F with subscript minus one is the source's alternative name for LF and is recorded so that the literature can be read.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.6/contracted-functors

K.7Morita invariance and products in K-theory

External products in K-theoryconstructionplanetExternal products from biexact functors

A functor of two variables that is exact in each variable separately induces a bilinear pairing of the zeroth K-groups, sending the pair of classes to the class of the value, and more generally a pairing of the K-theory spectra. For rings and the tensor product over a commutative base this gives the external product from the K-groups of two algebras to those of the tensor product algebra, and for a single commutative ring the internal product that makes the total K-group a graded ring. The construction is by a biexact functor of the relevant categories and carries associativity, unit and symmetry homotopies from the corresponding coherence of the tensor product; those homotopies are the data that must be carried, not consequences to be rediscovered.

Hypotheses

  • A and B are exact categories and the functor is biexact, meaning exact in each variable when the other is fixed.
  • For the ring case the tensor product is over a fixed commutative base and the modules are finitely generated projective over the respective algebras.
  • The unit is the class of the base ring as a module over itself, and the symmetry is the swap of the two factors.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.7/products-from-biexact-functors

Global Galois deformation rings

Galois representations and modularity · 15 definitions · 8 constructions · 9 planets

R04.1Deformation functors

Lifting functordefinitionplanetThe lifting (framed deformation) functor

Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). The lifting functor Lift_ρ̄ : Art_𝒪 → Set sends A to the set of continuous homomorphisms ρ : G → GL_n(A) (A discrete) with ρ mod m_A = ρ̄; a morphism f : A → B acts by ρ ↦ GL_n(f)∘ρ. On C_𝒪 it is extended by continuity: Lift_ρ̄(A) is the set of continuous lifts for the m_A-adic topology, and equals lim_k Lift_ρ̄(A/m_A^k).

Hypotheses

  • Pro-representability is not part of the definition (RS-08): Lift_ρ̄ is a plain functor; its representability is universal-lifting-ring.
  • Continuity: for A Artinian, GL_n(A) is finite and discrete, so ρ is continuous iff it factors through an open normal subgroup.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/lifting-functor

Deformation functordefinitionplanetDeformations up to strict equivalence

Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). The deformation functor Def_ρ̄ : Art_𝒪 → Set is A ↦ Lift_ρ̄(A)/Γ̂_n(A), lifts up to conjugation by Γ̂_n(A) = ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)) (strict equivalence). It is defined for every ρ̄; its representability needs End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽 (universal-deformation-ring).

Hypotheses

  • Strict equivalence, not GL_n(A)-conjugacy: the two agree when ρ̄ is Schur (strict-vs-full-conjugacy) but not in general.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/strict-deformation-functor

Determinant deformationsdefinitionplanetDeformations of a residual determinant

Let D̄ := det ∘ ρ̄ : 𝔽[G] → 𝔽, a continuous determinant of dimension n in Chenevier's sense (a multiplicative polynomial law homogeneous of degree n; the foundations are imported from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0). Def_{D̄}(A) is the set of continuous determinants D : A[G] → A of dimension n with D ⊗_A 𝔽 = D̄, for A ∈ Art_𝒪 (and by continuity for A ∈ C_𝒪). It is a separate functor: it is not assumed equivalent to Def_ρ̄ (determinant-comparison).

Hypotheses

  • Continuity of a determinant: its characteristic-polynomial coefficients g ↦ Λ_i(g) are continuous (Chenevier §2.30).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/determinant-deformation-functor

Deformations as modules with a residual identificationdefinition

Setting: G is a profinite group, 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p (or W(𝔽)) with residue field 𝔽 finite of characteristic p, n ≥ 1, and ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) is continuous. Art_𝒪 is the category of Artinian local 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 and C_𝒪 that of complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with residue field 𝔽 (both imported from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1). Γ̂_n(A) := ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(𝔽)). Fix V̄ = 𝔽^n with G acting by ρ̄ and its standard basis β. A deformation of V̄ to A ∈ Art_𝒪 is a pair (V_A, ι) with V_A a finite free A-module with a continuous A-linear G-action and ι : V_A ⊗_A 𝔽 ≅ V̄ a G-equivariant isomorphism; a framed deformation adds an A-basis β_A of V_A lifting β through ι. Isomorphisms are G-equivariant A-linear isomorphisms compatible with ι (and with the bases). Def^mod_ρ̄(A) and Def^{mod,□}_ρ̄(A) are the sets of isomorphism classes.

Hypotheses

  • Bases lifting β exist for every (V_A, ι) because V_A is free and V_A → V_A ⊗ 𝔽 is surjective (Nakayama).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/module-deformation-functor

Lifts and deformations with fixed determinantdefinition

Let χ : G → 𝒪^× be continuous with χ mod λ = det ρ̄. Lift_{ρ̄,χ}(A) := {ρ ∈ Lift_ρ̄(A) : det ρ = χ_A}, χ_A the composite G → 𝒪^× → A^×; it is stable under Γ̂_n(A), and Def_{ρ̄,χ} := Lift_{ρ̄,χ}/Γ̂_n. These are subfunctors of Lift_ρ̄ and Def_ρ̄.

Hypotheses

  • The determinant is not fixed in the variable-determinant problems of G8; this is the separate fixed-determinant variant.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/fixed-determinant-functors

Change of coefficient ring and residue fieldconstruction

Let 𝒪 → 𝒪′ be a local homomorphism of such coefficient rings, finite, with residue extension 𝔽 ⊆ 𝔽′, and ρ̄′ := ρ̄ ⊗_𝔽 𝔽′. Restriction along 𝒪 → 𝒪′ identifies Lift^{𝒪′}_{ρ̄′}(A′) with the set of lifts of ρ̄ to A′ in the sense of local 𝒪-algebras whose residue map 𝔽 → 𝔽′ is the given inclusion, naturally in A′ ∈ Art_{𝒪′}; the same holds for Def, for fixed determinant, and for Schur ρ̄ (End_{𝔽′[G]}(ρ̄′) = End_{𝔽[G]}(ρ̄) ⊗ 𝔽′ = 𝔽′).

Hypotheses

  • The categories Art_{𝒪′} and the residue-field-extension API come from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.1/change-of-coefficients

R04.2Representability and universal representations

Mazur's finiteness condition Φ_pdefinition

A profinite group G satisfies Φ_p if for every open subgroup Δ ≤ G the group Hom_cont(Δ, 𝔽_p) is finite; equivalently, the maximal pro-p quotient of every open subgroup is topologically finitely generated.

Hypotheses

  • The condition quantifies over all open subgroups; finiteness of Hom(G, 𝔽_p) alone is weaker (sourceIssues E1).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/phi-p-condition

The universal continuous lift over the inverse-limit ringconstruction

ρ^□ : G → GL_n(R^□_ρ̄) = lim_k GL_n(R^□_ρ̄/m^k) is the continuous homomorphism obtained from the compatible universal lifts over the Artinian quotients R^□_ρ̄/m^k; it is continuous for the m-adic topology and, for A ∈ C_𝒪, every continuous lift to GL_n(A) is GL_n(f)∘ρ^□ for a unique f ∈ Hom_{C_𝒪}(R^□_ρ̄, A). The same construction gives ρ^univ over R_ρ̄ (Schur) and the fixed-determinant versions.

Hypotheses

  • R^□_ρ̄ is complete and separated for its maximal-ideal topology (R03.1: objects of C_𝒪 are inverse limits of Artinian quotients).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.2/universal-continuous-lift

R04.3Local conditions and global presentations

Local deformation problemsdefinition

For a profinite group G_v satisfying Φ_p and ρ̄_v : G_v → GL_n(𝔽), a deformation problem D is a collection of lifts (R, ρ) (R ∈ C_𝒪) containing (𝔽, ρ̄_v), closed under pushforward along morphisms of C_𝒪, detected along injections, closed under the fibre products (R₁ ×_{R₁/I₁ ≅ R₂/I₂} R₂), closed under inverse limits along separated filtrations, and stable under conjugation by Γ̂_n(R).

Hypotheses

  • These are the axioms of Clozel–Harris–Taylor as stated by Gee; the local lifting rings they cut out are those of LocalGaloisDeformationRings (R08.x) in applications.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-deformation-problem

Global deformation data and T-framed deformationsdefinition

Let F be a number field, S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞ where ρ̄ ramifies, G = G_{F,S}, ρ̄ : G → GL_n(𝔽) absolutely irreducible, χ a lift of det ρ̄, D_v a deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} for each v ∈ S, and T ⊆ S. A T-framed deformation of type 𝒮 = (S, {D_v}, χ) to A is a class of tuples (ρ, {α_v}_{v∈T}) with ρ a lift of determinant χ, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∈ D_v for v ∈ S, α_v ∈ Γ̂_n(A), modulo (ρ, {α_v}) ∼ (βρβ^{-1}, {βα_v}) for β ∈ Γ̂_n(A).

Hypotheses

  • Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ (Schur suffices for representability; RS-08 keeps the absolutely irreducible statement).
  • The framed local lift α_v^{-1}ρ|_{G_{F_v}}α_v is well defined (R04.1/restriction-of-deformations).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/global-deformation-type

The map from local rings to the global framed ringconstruction

Define R^loc_{S,T} := ⊗̂_{v∈T} R^□_{ρ̄|G_v,χ}/I(D_v), the completed tensor product over 𝒪 of the local framed rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1) cut out by the local problems. Restricting the universal T-framed deformation, v ↦ α_v^{-1}ρ^□T|_{G_{F_v}}α_v, gives the tautological 𝒪-algebra map R^loc_{S,T} → R^□T_𝒮.

Hypotheses

  • The framed local lift is well defined on equivalence classes (R04.1/restriction-of-deformations); the local rings are those of R08.1 (requested).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.3/local-to-global-map

R04.4Restriction, twisting and change of problem

Determinant fixed on SdefinitionplanetRings with determinant fixed only on S, and the determinant map

(KW II §4.1.1, n = 2.) R^□_{S∪V} represents tuples (V_A, (β_{v,A})_{v∈S}) with V_A a deformation of ρ̄ as a G_{F,S∪V}-representation such that det V_A|D_v = ψχ_p for v ∈ S, and β_{v,A} lifts of the chosen basis; R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} is the same with det V_A = ψχ_p globally. Both are R^{□,loc,ψ}_S-algebras, and R̄ denotes base change to the local-condition quotient R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S. The determinant map d : Sp R^□_{S∪V} → G*_V, ρ ↦ det ρ · (ψχ_p)^{−1}, satisfies d(χ ⊗ ρ) = χ² d(ρ), and Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V} = d^{−1}(1) is a closed subfunctor.

Hypotheses

  • These are Newton–Thorne's R′_Q and R′^□_Q for p = 2 with V = Q a set of Taylor–Wiles places (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B item 7).
  • The unframed variants are the trace subrings; the framed rings are power series in 4|S| − 1 variables over them (KW II Proposition 4.1, R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S

Twisting by charactersconstructionplanetThe action of twisting characters

Let W = S ∪ V with S ∩ V = ∅, S containing the places above p and ∞ (KW II §4.1). Let G_V = Gal(F^S_V/F), the Galois group of the maximal abelian p-extension of F unramified outside V and split at S; it is a finite abelian p-group. The diagonalizable group G*_V (G*_V(A) = residually trivial Hom(G_V, A^×)) acts on Sp R^□_{S∪V} (determinant fixed only on S) by χ·(ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)) = (χ ⊗ ρ, (ρ_v), (g_v)); each χ ∈ G*_V(𝒪) gives an automorphism a_χ with a_χ ∘ ρ^univ = χ ⊗ ρ^univ, commuting with the ∏_{v∈S}(GL_2)_1 action on frames. For p = 2 the subgroup G*_{V,2} of characters of G_V/2G_V preserves the determinant and acts on Sp R^{□,ψ}_{S∪V}. The actions descend to the quotients with local conditions at S and to the unframed (trace) subrings.

Hypotheses

  • Finiteness of G_V is class field theory: G_V is the p-part of a ray class group of modulus supported on V (tame, as V has no place above p) modulo the classes of places in S; requested from Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory.
  • For n = 2 as in KW II; for general n the determinant changes by χ^n.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/twisting-action

Diagonalizable groups on complete local algebrasdefinition

For a finitely generated abelian group a whose torsion has p-power order, the diagonalizable group (a)* on complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras is the completion of the diagonalizable group scheme D(a) at the identity of its special fibre: (a)*(A) = Hom(a, 1 + 𝔪_A), with affine algebra the completion of 𝒪[a] at (π, augmentation ideal). T = (ℤ^t)* = Ĝ_m^t is the split formal torus and T_{p^m} = ((ℤ/p^m)^t)* = μ_{p^m}^t. Truncation: the closed immersion T_{p^m} ↪ T is an isomorphism after truncation at level m + 1 (A ↦ A/𝔪^{m+1}), because (1 + X)^{p^m} − 1 ∈ (p, X)^{m+1}.

Hypotheses

  • KW II use these for the twisting groups G*_V (V a set of auxiliary places) and for the torus T of 2-adic patching.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4/diagonalizable-groups

Restriction to a finite extension as a ring mapconstruction

Let F′/F be a finite extension and S′ the places of F′ above S. Restricting lifts along G_{F′,S′} → G_{F,S} gives a local 𝒪-algebra map res : R^□_{ρ̄|G_{F′,S′}} → R^□_{ρ̄} of framed rings and, with fixed determinant, R^□_{ρ̄|,χ|G_{F′}} → R^□_{ρ̄,χ}. If ρ̄|G_{F′,S′} is absolutely irreducible it gives res : R^univ_{ρ̄|G_{F′,S′}} → R^univ_{ρ̄} on unframed rings. If for each v′ | v the local problem D_{v′} contains the restrictions to G_{F′_{v′}} of the lifts in D_v, res descends to the rings with local conditions, R̄_{F′} → R̄_F (KW II's γ).

Hypotheses

  • Absolute irreducibility of ρ̄|G_{F′,S′} is what makes the unframed ring of the restriction exist (R04.2/universal-deformation-ring); the framed map needs no hypothesis.
  • The compatibility of local problems is checked in each application; KW II choose F′ so that it holds (proof of Theorem 10.1).

R04.5Taylor–Wiles auxiliary primes

Taylor–Wiles datadefinition

Let F be a number field, S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞ and those where ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(𝔽) ramifies, and N ≥ 1. A Taylor–Wiles datum of level N is a finite set Q of finite places disjoint from S such that, for v ∈ Q, N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^N and ρ̄(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues, together with a choice of eigenvalue α_v (equivalently an eigenline; β_v is the other). Put Δ_v = the maximal p-quotient of k(v)^× and Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} Δ_v (KW II write Δ′). The deformation problem S_Q allows arbitrary ramification at v ∈ Q (L_v = H¹(G_v, ad⁰)), so the dual Selmer condition there is L_v^⊥ = 0. For p = 2, KW II also require each v ∈ Q to split in the Kummer extension F̃_n/F (dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes).

Hypotheses

  • N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^N is equivalent to v splitting completely in F(ζ_{p^N}); distinct eigenvalues is equivalent to ad ρ̄(Frob_v) having an eigenvalue ≠ 1.
  • The local deformation rings at v ∈ Q are LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/taylor-wiles-local-ring (Gee Lemma 3.33).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.5/taylor-wiles-datum

The residual image hypotheses used to choose primesdefinition

Three residual hypotheses are used to choose Taylor–Wiles primes, and they are kept distinct. (1) Cyclotomic absolute irreducibility: ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible (KW II, p > 2). (2) Big image: p ≥ 5, p unramified in F, and ρ̄(G_F) ⊇ SL_2(𝔽_p) (Gee, Theorem 5.2(3)). (3) Non-solvable image: ρ̄(G_F) is not solvable (KW II, p = 2; Dickson then makes the projective image SL_2(𝔽_{2^r}) with r > 1). Adequacy (Thorne) and enormous image (ACC+ Definition 6.2.29) are further, different hypotheses, defined with their consumers (G7 and G8). Each theorem below states which one it uses; no implication between them is assumed.

Hypotheses

  • Dickson's classification and the cohomology vanishing H¹(SL_2(𝔽_{2^r}), M_2(𝔽)) = 0 (r > 1; KW II Lemma 4.3(5)) are requested from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4.

R04.6Global-to-local deformation presentations

KW II deformation datadefinitionplanetThe global deformation data of KW II §9

Let F be totally real, ρ̄ : G_F → GL_2(𝔽) as in KW II §8 with lifting data and ψ, Σ the places where the lifting data ramify away from p (together with the places above p in case (C), or when p = 2 and k(ρ̄) = 4), and S = Σ ∪ {v | ∞} ∪ {v | p}. For v ∈ S, R̄^{□,ψ}_v is the local ring classifying: semistable lifts with a fixed unramified character γ_v at finite v ∤ p (§3.3.4); odd lifts at the infinite places (§3.1, including the ring of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 at p = 2); and at v | p lifts of type (A) low-weight crystalline, (B) weight two (p > 2, k(ρ̄) ≤ p) or (C) weight-two semistable. Each R̄^{□,ψ}_v is a domain, flat over 𝒪, of relative dimension 3 (v ∤ p∞), 3 + [F_v : ℚ_p] (v | p) or 2 (v | ∞), with regular generic fibre. Hence R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S = ⊗̂_{v∈S} R̄^{□,ψ}_v is a flat domain of relative dimension 3|S| with regular generic fibre, and R̄^{□,ψ}_S = R^{□,ψ}_S ⊗̂_{R^{□,loc,ψ}_S} R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S.

Hypotheses

  • The local rings and their properties are KW II Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, exported by LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (requested). The completed tensor product of flat domains with regular generic fibres and an 𝒪-point is again one (KW II Proposition 2.2(ii); DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3).
  • Gee's version (§5.6) uses the problems 𝒮_Q, 𝒮′_Q, with the two local rings agreeing modulo λ and (R^{loc,′})^{red} irreducible. It is the same export with other local conditions.

Taylor–Wiles systemconstructionplanetThe Taylor–Wiles system of deformation rings

Let p > 2, B = R̄^{□,loc,ψ}_S, d = 3|S|, h = h¹_{{L_v^⊥}}(S, (Ad⁰)*(1)), j = 4|S| − 1, and Q_n (n ≥ 1) the Taylor–Wiles data of R04.5/odd-taylor-wiles-primes, with Q_n = {v_1, …, v_h} and generators δ_i of Δ′_{v_i}. For each n there are surjections of B-algebras B⟦x_1, …, x_{h+j−d}⟧ ↠ R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} ↠ R̄^{□,ψ}_S. R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} is an 𝒪⟦y_1, …, y_{h+j}⟧-algebra, with y_i ↦ δ_i − 1 (i ≤ h) from Δ′_{Q_n} and y_{h+1}, …, y_{h+j} the framing variables. Then R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n}/(y_1, …, y_h) ≅ R̄^{□,ψ}_S and R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n}/(y_1, …, y_{h+j}) ≅ R̄^ψ_S. The kernel of 𝒪⟦y_1, …, y_h⟧ → 𝒪[Δ′_{Q_n}] is generated by the (1 + y_i)^{#Δ′_{v_i}} − 1, so it lies in ((1 + y_1)^{p^n} − 1, …, (1 + y_h)^{p^n} − 1), since p^n divides #Δ′_{v_i}. This is the finite-level system exported to patching.

Hypotheses

  • The patching itself, with R_∞, M_∞ and the Hecke modules S_{k,ψ}(U_{Q_n}, 𝒪)_𝔪, is GL2ModularityLifting R22.3 (with DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5's abstract patching); only the deformation-ring side is exported here.
  • Gee's version (§5.10 and after) uses R^□_{Q_N} over R^loc with #T − 1 − [F : ℚ] + r generators and J_∞ = 𝒥⟦y_1, …, y_r⟧.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/taylor-wiles-deformation-system

The unframed ring as a trace subring, with its universal representationconstruction

R̄^ψ_S is the subring of R̄^{□,ψ}_S generated by the traces of the universal representation. Equivalently, it is the image of the unframed ring R^ψ_S. R̄^{□,ψ}_S is a power series ring over R̄^ψ_S in j = 4|S| − 1 variables, being a torsor under (∏_{v∈S}(GL_2)_1)/Ĝ_m. The universal representation descends to ρ̄^univ_S : G_{F,S} → GL_2(R̄^ψ_S): the traces lie in R̄^ψ_S and ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible (Carayol). The same holds with Q_n added, giving R̄^ψ_{S∪Q_n}, R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n} and ρ̄^univ_{S∪Q_n}.

Hypotheses

  • Carayol's descent to the subring generated by traces is R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem; the framed–unframed torsor is R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison with T = S (KW II Proposition 4.1).

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6/trace-subring-universal-representation

The finite-level data for 2-adic patchingconstruction

Let p = 2, h = |Q_n| (R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes), t = h¹_{S-split}(Q_n, 𝔽), G_n = Gal(F^S_{Q_n}/F), G′_n = G_n/2^{n−2}G_n ≅ (ℤ/2^{n−2})^t, and T = Hom(ℤ^t, Ĝ_m). For each n > n₀ this construction gives: R′_n = R̄^□_{S∪Q_n} (determinant fixed only on S, R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S) and R_n = R̄^{□,ψ}_{S∪Q_n}; a choice of ℤ^t ↠ G′_n, identifying (G′_n)* with T_{2^{n−2}} ⊂ T; the determinant map d_n : Sp R′_n → G*_n ⊂ T, ρ ↦ det ρ·(χ_pψ)^{−1}, with Sp R_n = d_n^{−1}(1) and d_n(λρ) = λ²d_n(ρ); the free twisting action of G*_n on Sp R′_n (R04.4/twist-action-free); a presentation B⟦x_1, …, x_{h+j+t−d}⟧ ↠ R′_n; and the Δ′_{Q_n}-structure compatible with the twists (a_χ ∘ δ = χ(δ)·(δ ∘ a_χ)). These are the level-n inputs to KW II's patching data (D_m, L_m, D′_m).

Hypotheses

  • The patched limit, with R′_∞, its free T-action and d(tx′) = t²d(x′), is GL2ModularityLifting R22.6; R04.4/truncated-actions and determinant-twist-torsor supply the group-action statements it uses.
  • KW II take a ≥ 2 and restrict the G′*_{n+a}-action to T_{2^n}; the truncation isomorphism T_{2^m} ≅ T at level m + 1 (R04.4/diagonalizable-groups) turns these into action chunks of T.

G7Polarized dimension-n deformation problems

Polarized deformation problemsdefinitionplanet

Let 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} with j(g, μ)j^{−1} = (μ·ᵗg^{−1}, μ), and ν : 𝒢_n → GL_1 sending (g, μ) ↦ μ and j ↦ −1. Let r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(k) be continuous with r̄^{−1}((GL_n × GL_1)(k)) = G_{F,S}, and χ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒪^× a lift of ν ∘ r̄. A lift of r̄ to A ∈ C_𝒪 is a continuous r : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄ with ν ∘ r = χ; lifts are equivalent when conjugate by 1 + M_n(𝔪_A); T-framed lifts (r; α_v)_{v∈T} are identified with (βrβ^{−1}; βα_v). A polarized global deformation problem 𝒮 = (F/F⁺, S, S̃, 𝒪, r̄, χ, {D_v}) takes for each v ∈ S a local deformation problem D_v for r̄|G_{F_ṽ} (GL_n-valued, as in R04.3); a lift is of type 𝒮 when each r|G_{F_ṽ} ∈ D_v. Equivalently (Lemma 2.1.1), for γ₀ ∈ G_{F⁺} ∖ G_F, a lift is a triple (ρ, μ, ⟨ , ⟩): ρ = r|G_F, μ = χ, and a perfect pairing with ⟨x, ρ(γ₀²)y⟩ = −μ(γ₀)⟨y, x⟩ and μ(δ)⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨ρ(δ)x, ρ(γ₀δγ₀^{−1})y⟩, i.e. an actual polarization ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ μ.

Hypotheses

  • F/F⁺ is a CM extension (F⁺ totally real, F totally imaginary quadratic over F⁺), S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ that split in F and contain the places above p, S̃ a choice of one place ṽ of F above each v ∈ S, and p odd.
  • The pairing, multiplier, symmetry sign and oddness sign of polarizations are requested from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7; this node takes them as given.
  • r̄ is Schur (CHT Definition 2.1.6) when every irreducible G_F-subquotient is absolutely irreducible and no subquotient W₂ satisfies W₂^∨ ⊗ ν∘r̄ ≅ (k^n/W₁)^{γ₀}; r̄|G_F absolutely irreducible suffices.
  • Fixed-multiplier variant: ν ∘ r = χ is imposed. Coefficient extension along 𝒪 → 𝒪′ is as in R04.1/change-of-coefficients.
